verified_metadata.title: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation method via dual-view graph contrastive learning and latent space uncertainty rectification
verified_metadata.abstract: As a typical application of artificial intelligence (AI), automated medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in numerous scenarios such as clinical diagnosis and auxiliary treatment. However, supervised medical image segmentation relies on abundant labeled data, which is expensive and time-consuming to obtain. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising engineering framework in this context to alleviate the annotation burden by leveraging abundant unlabeled data. However, existing SSL methods suffer from inadequate feature representation and high prediction uncertainty, which will cause blurred boundaries in complex anatomical structures and compromise diagnostic accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a semi-supervised medical image segmentation framework by integrating dual-view graph contrastive learning (DGCL) and latent space uncertainty rectification (LSUR) strategy. The DGCL constructs a topological graph in the feature space by adaptively linking high-entropy anchor points, which explicitly enforces the intra-class compactness and inter-class discriminability to enhance the structural semantic information extraction along decision boundaries. Complementarily, LSUR performs generative reconstruction and refinement in the latent space for high uncertainty regions, which significantly mitigates the error accumulation caused by pseudo-labels, and enhances model robustness and prediction accuracy. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art comparison methods on different evaluation metrics with 10% and 30% labeled data. This indicates that the proposed method provides an effective AI-driven solution for accurate clinical segmentation with limited annotations.

verified_metadata.title: A Mixture of Physics-Informed Expert system for robust prediction of concrete failure behavior under high impact loads
verified_metadata.abstract: Predicting concrete failure under high-impact loads is critical for designing protective structures. Machine learning models can provide high predictive accuracy, but they often lack robustness when applied to out-of-distribution data. Traditional physics-based methods cannot fully resolve this limitation because concrete failure under impact loading is highly nonlinear and difficult to describe with complete physical accuracy. To address this challenge, this study proposes a Mixture of Physics-Informed Expert system, an artificial intelligence and deep-learning framework for predicting concrete failure behavior under high-impact loading. The proposed system uses physics-based gating logic and a dynamic regularization strategy to improve prediction reliability when the input conditions differ from the training data. The system was evaluated for penetration depth prediction and achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.9884. It also reduced the mean absolute error by 9.7% compared with a standard neural network and by 68.0% compared with common empirical formulas. These results show that the proposed artificial intelligence approach can balance data-driven accuracy with physics-based reliability for robust prediction of concrete failure behavior in critical engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: Enabling inverse design of metamaterials via trustworthy and interpretable representation learning with epistemic uncertainty awareness
verified_metadata.abstract: Metamaterials enable advanced applications in compact, high-performance systems, such as soft robotics and mechanical neural networks, where continuous and independent tuning of effective properties is essential. Achieving such control requires solving the inverse-design problem of generating meso-scale geometries that realize prescribed material properties. However, conventional topology optimization often struggles with simultaneous multi-property control and smooth structural transitions, while existing machine-learning-based generative models typically lack interpretable latent representations and reliable epistemic uncertainty quantification. To address these challenges, we propose an interpretable and uncertainty-aware representation-learning framework for metamaterial inverse design. The framework embeds effective elastic material properties directly into structured latent dimensions, enabling continuous and decoupled property tuning with smooth geometric interpolation. An auxiliary surface-mapping mechanism quantifies epistemic uncertainty through predictive performance consistency, providing a reliability indicator for each generated design. The case study demonstrates a strong correlation between the estimated epistemic uncertainty and the actual design error for target elastic effective properties, validating its effectiveness for reliability assessment. The proposed approach further supports efficient exploration of the material property space, continuously decoupled property tuning and uncertainty-aware multi-lattice topology optimization. These results establish a trustworthy and interpretable paradigm for inverse design of metamaterials with controllable properties.

verified_metadata.title: A novel physics-constrained deep learning framework for the inverse design of assembly contact interfaces
verified_metadata.abstract: Assembly contact interface characteristics critically influence the performance of precision mechanical systems. Traditional design methods relying on iterative finite element analysis are computationally expensive, while existing deep learning approaches often neglect physical constraints and the complex effects of assembly processes. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-constrained deep learning framework for the inverse design of assembly interfaces. Specifically, we introduce a novel network architecture which integrates multi-source inputs including target contact pressure, assembly parameters, and service conditions. To enforce physical consistency, a differentiable loss function incorporating the impenetrability condition is developed. Furthermore, an optimized learning rate scheduling strategy is implemented to enhance model convergence. Comprehensive ablation and comparative experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional approaches in both accuracy and physical plausibility. When applied to an aero-engine flange structure, the framework enables rapid inverse design of interface morphology, reducing maximum contact pressure by 15.67% and increasing the effective contact area by 45.23% compared to traditional designs. This work provides a robust solution for assembly interface design and advances the application of physics-constrained deep learning in complex engineering systems.

verified_metadata.title: An incorporation of graph neural network with two-phase Convolutional feature representation model for indoor object detection and distance estimation in Internet of Things environment
verified_metadata.abstract: Recently, indoor object detection (OD) and distance estimation in an Internet of Things (IoT) environment have gained significant attention, integrating smart sensors, cameras, and connected devices to accurately detect and localize objects in enclosed spaces. OD is an important and effective technology across various fields because it can automatically detect and recognise objects and images. New developments in useful technology have mainly concentrated on improving navigation and object recognition. Using computer vision, machine learning, and sensor fusion techniques, the system can identify different object classes, estimate distances, and communicate data over the IoT network for surveillance, automation, and safety applications. Now, deep learning techniques are widely used for distance estimation and OD processes. In this paper, a Deep Learning with Convolutional Feature Representation for Indoor Object Detection and Distance Estimation (DLCFR-IODDE) approach is presented in an IoT environment. The paper aims to develop an IoT-based OD and distance estimation for indoor environments. To begin with, the image pre-processing phase employs a Gaussian filter to improve image quality. Furthermore, Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network method is used for the OD process. To achieve effective feature extraction, the DLCFR-IODDE method uses the Swin Transformer to capture both local and global features from image data. Moreover, graph convolutional network model is implemented for classification. Finally, distance estimation process uses the inverse depth regression model. To demonstrate the improved performance of the DLCFR-IODDE method, a comprehensive empirical study is conducted on the Indoor OD dataset. The comparison analysis of the DLCFR-IODDE method showed an accuracy of 99.77% compared with existing methods.

verified_metadata.title: Anti-vibration wavefront interferometry by physics-informed U-Net
verified_metadata.abstract: High-precision wavefront interferometry is extremely sensitive to environmental vibrations, which limits the industrial deployment of conventional phase-shifting interferometers. In this paper, an anti-vibration wavefront interferometry (AVWI) framework using only one or two interferograms is proposed. AVWI reduces the reliance on vibration-isolated environments and high-precision phase shifters by explicitly decoupling vibration-induced errors from the test wavefront. This is enabled by a vibration-detection model based on a physics-informed U-Net (AVWI-PIUN). The network learns vibration information from interferograms and enforces cross-frame consistency among phase-shifted interferograms. A physics-informed loss, denoted as {\mathcal{L}}_{Phy}${\mathcal{L}}_{Phy}$, is further introduced using partial-derivative relationships between phase-shifted interferograms, which significantly reduces the required training data and accelerates convergence. Experiments under vibrating conditions demonstrate that AVWI achieves superior accuracy, repeatability, and efficiency compared with a temporal phase-shifting method. Specifically, AVWI achieves a Q peak-to-valley (PVq) figure error of 13.750 nm (nm), a root mean square (RMS) figure error of 1.784 nm, and an RMS repeatability of 0.411 nm, corresponding to reductions of 50.1%, 76.0%, and 92.2%, respectively. In addition, AVWI tolerates phase-shifting errors up to ±9π/20. These results indicate that AVWI provides a practical route toward nanometer-level surface figure metrology in vibration-prone industrial and in-situ machining environments.

verified_metadata.title: Crystal graph convolutional neural network-based reinforcement learning for adaptive shipyard block transportation scheduling
verified_metadata.abstract: Hull blocks, as fundamental assembly units in vessel construction, require specialized transporters due to their substantial size and weight. Optimizing the scheduling of these transporters is crucial for ensuring on-time production and improving operational efficiency in shipyard logistics. Accordingly, this study proposes a scheduling approach that minimizes block transport tardiness and empty travel time. While previous studies have primarily focused on transport scheduling using metaheuristic algorithms, this study introduces a scalable and dynamic scheduling algorithm that employs reinforcement learning integrated with the Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN). CGCNN is used to encode edge-attributed graphs for state representation, effectively capturing the importance of each location. The proposed algorithm demonstrates stable and superior performance compared to existing priority rules and metaheuristic algorithms across diverse problem distributions, demonstrating its generalizability. Finally, the algorithm is validated through simulations using real-world shipyard transportation data, confirming its practical efficiency and applicability.

title: Deep active sequential learning of stress evolution in early-age concrete informed by thermo-chemo-mechanical modelling
abstract: This study presents an integrated finite-element–machine-learning framework for predicting early-age stress evolution in concrete materials/structures by combining an enhanced thermo-chemo-mechanical (TCM) model, deep sequential learning (DSL), and active learning (AL). The proposed TCM model incorporates experimentally informed viscoelasticity, a stable exponential creep–relaxation conversion, and an efficient exponential algorithm for the Maxwell-chain formulation in finite element analysis, which is further validated by a temperature stress testing machine. This model generates high-fidelity stress–time data across diverse mixtures, temperatures, and structural configurations. These simulations are used to train a Gated Recurrent Unit with Monte Carlo Dropout (GRU-MCD) model, whose predictive performance surpasses conventional point-wise approaches such as Light Gradient Boosting Machine and Gaussian Process Regression, yielding higher accuracy with reduced overfitting. The AL strategy further enhances efficiency by enabling the GRU-MCD model to achieve the accuracy of ∼900 Latin Hypercube samples using only ∼200 samples selected by active learning. Although demonstrated on a wall–base structure, the proposed framework is general and applicable to other cementitious material or structural systems, providing an effective tool for cracking-risk evaluation, reliability analysis, and the design of low-carbon concrete structures.

title: Research on defect recognition method of mine belts based on deep learning
abstract: The traditional manual inspection method is inefficient and prone to missed detections. Although the existing non-destructive testing technologies such as ultrasonic and infrared imaging equipment can provide accurate results, they are complex to operate and have high equipment costs. This paper proposes a defect recognition method for mining belts based on deep learning, which uses the You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection algorithm to automatically identify and classify surface cracks, wear, tears and other defects of the belts. By analyzing the network structure and experimental results of the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) algorithm, it is found that its recognition accuracy is poor for defect categories with small sample sizes, samples with complex environments, and samples with high noise levels. To solve these problems and improve the robustness and accuracy of the model in complex environments, the attention mechanism and the Focal Loss function were introduced. YOLOv8 is improved by introducing the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and Focal Loss. Finally, the effectiveness of the method we proposed was verified through experiments. The experimental results show that the improved model demonstrates better accuracy than the original model in identifying all five types of defects.

title: A novel physical extraction multi-step neural network algorithm for power lithium-ion battery state of charge and available capacity estimation
abstract: The state of charge (SOC) and available capacity estimation of power lithium-ion batteries (LIB) are important for battery management systems. In this paper, a novel physical extraction multi-step neural network (PEMSNN) algorithm is proposed for state estimation. First, to solve the problems of insufficient input feature dimension and complex nonlinear coupling relationship of neural network, a model-driven physical feature extraction method is proposed, which effectively extends the input feature dimension. The extracted features are input into the long short-term memory to construct a fusion neural network. Secondly, the complex electrochemical processes within the LIB are comprehensively analyzed. Subsequently, in combination with the external discharge characteristic curve, a multi-segment prediction method is proposed. This method resolves the issue of zone attention allocation and enhances the prediction accuracy of the SOC. Finally, by leveraging the slow time-varying characteristics of capacity and the high-precision SOC results, a PEMSNN algorithm is proposed for the prediction of available capacity. Consequently, this resolves the problem of capacity calibration in the estimation of the SOC. The estimation accuracy and robustness are verified under dynamic operating conditions at 15 °C (°C), 25 °C, and 35 °C. The SOC estimation accuracy has improved by at least 38.42%. The error of the available capacity is within the range of 74 mA-hours. The proposed PEMSNN algorithm offers a potentially viable strategy for applying artificial intelligence to state estimation in new energy electric vehicles.

verified_metadata.title: Nonlinear multi-field coupling analysis and prediction of thermo-mechanical response of oil shale under microwave heating using physics-informed neural network
verified_metadata.abstract: Strongly nonlinear multi-field coupling problems in the microwave heating of oil shale require high-precision and efficient solution methods. Physics-informed neural network (PINN) has emerged as a powerful tool for solving partial differential equations (PDEs); however, existing PINN approaches often have limited applicability under specific conditions, and their training convergence remains suboptimal when applied to strongly nonlinear, temperature-dependent material problems. To address this, this study proposes a PINN framework with a strong physical constraint weighting strategy, in which the physical loss weight is constrained within 0.5-0.6 and dynamically balanced during training. Coupled with experimentally obtained temperature-dependent material parameters, this enables efficient surrogate solutions of the coupled PDEs. Three test cases (600 W, 800 W microwave heating, and cross-condition high-temperature steam heating of oil shale) were used for training and prediction. The results show that the PINN framework can output temperature and displacement fields at arbitrary points in milliseconds, with total loss stabilized at the 10^{−4}-10^{−3} level, high prediction accuracy, and strong agreement with COMSOL simulations. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high-precision, rapid prediction and cross-condition generalization for strongly nonlinear thermo-mechanical coupling problems in temperature-dependent materials.

verified_metadata.title: Quantum-resilient federated learning with trust-assisted adaptive anomaly detection for Internet of Things environment
verified_metadata.abstract: Internet of Things environments require secure and privacy-preserving collaborative learning mechanisms that remain robust under emerging quantum-era threats. Many existing distributed learning approaches do not provide dynamic threat detection and quantum-resistant protection, which leaves Internet of Things deployments exposed to adaptive attacks and future cryptanalytic advances. This study proposes an Adaptive Anomaly Detection and Trust-Aware Federated Learning framework to address these limitations. The framework integrates: (i) a deep learning-based adaptive anomaly detection component for real-time identification of malicious behavioral patterns, (ii) a quantitative trust assessment component that computes a mathematical trust score using behavioral evidence, integrity verification outcomes, and time-dependent factors, and (iii) a quantum-resilient encryption mechanism that combines post-quantum cryptography with quantum key distribution while remaining compatible with Internet of Things resource constraints. These components operate within a secure federated learning architecture that employs a decentralized design together with differential privacy and homomorphic encryption to protect local data and secure model aggregation. Experimental evaluation indicates 96% accuracy for anomaly detection, 93% accuracy for trust assessment, 97% encryption stability, and 2–4 s for federation synchronization under the tested settings.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-driven preconditioned conjugate gradient method for finite element analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: With the rapid advancement of urbanization, structural systems are evolving toward ultra-large-scale and clustered configurations. Correspondingly, the number of degrees of freedom in finite element (FE) models of these large-scale structural systems has increased dramatically, which necessitates efficient computational performance of large-scale sparse linear systems. The preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method is widely utilized for solving large sparse symmetric positive-definite systems, owing to the preconditioner computational efficiency. This study employs the condition number of the preconditioned matrix as the loss function and develops a sparse convolutional U-shaped neural network (SU-net) as the core architecture for constructing an efficient preconditioner generator. The proposed approach is embedded into the workflow of finite element–based structural analysis, enabling a significant reduction in computational time for displacement responses of superstructure frames and soil–structure interaction systems. Compared with the non-preconditioned CG method, the proposed framework achieves a speedup of 6.23-8.43 times for superstructure frame problems and 13.48-19.89 times for soil–substructure interaction problems, without any loss of accuracy. Furthermore, within the convergence tolerance range of 1 × 10^{−2} to 1 × 10^{−10}, the proposed deep learning-based preconditioner consistently demonstrates superior acceleration in comparison with Jacobi, symmetric Gauss–Seidel, symmetric successive over-relaxation, incomplete Cholesky factorization without fill-in and algebraic multigrid method. The developed SU-net demonstrates strong generalization capability for random material parameter problems at a fixed mesh resolution, suggesting that it has considerable potential as an effective preconditioning strategy for load combination design, material parameter optimization, and stochastic finite element analysis in large-scale structures.

verified_metadata.title: A physics-informed neural network approach for marine turbocharger performance evaluation in ocean-going vessels: Under incomplete parameter conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: Marine turbochargers are critical for improving fuel efficiency and reducing emissions in maritime transport, yet evaluating their performance under dynamic ocean conditions remains challenging due to incomplete sensor data and limitations of conventional models. While physics-based approaches lack adaptability, purely data-driven methods require complete datasets and may violate thermodynamic consistency. This study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that embeds mean - value thermodynamic equations into the loss function, integrating multi-source operational data with physical constraints. The method employs a two-stage progressive training strategy with adaptive weighting and a novel gradient coordination mechanism to balance competing objectives and ensure stable, thermodynamically consistent learning. Validated on 2.1 million data points from a 300,000 DWT bulk carrier, the PINN achieves high accuracy in predicting key turbocharger performance indicators, significantly outperforming traditional models in bench tests and maintaining robust performance even under incomplete parameter conditions. This framework bridges physics-based modeling and deep learning, enabling robust turbocharger evaluation in dynamic environments, advancing condition monitoring, and supporting condition-based maintenance of ship propulsion systems.

verified_metadata.title: A whole-life fatigue crack growth rate prediction method based on active learning and physics-informed loss
verified_metadata.abstract: Whole-life fatigue crack growth presents a critical challenge in structural integrity assessment, particularly under complex loading conditions. To address the limitations of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in capturing the temporal dynamics of fatigue crack growth, this study proposes an active learning-based physics-informed recurrent neural network (AC-PI-RNN). Specifically, a recurrent neural network (RNN) is integrated with a fully connected network, where dynamic features (stress intensity factor range) and static features (stress ratio, load amplitude, and pre-strain) are fused at the RNN input layer to provide comprehensive loading information. To optimize sample selection under data-limited conditions, a query-by-committee active learning strategy is employed. Furthermore, a modified Jones physical model is embedded into the network's loss function to enforce adherence to the underlying physics of fatigue crack growth. Comprehensive evaluations validate the efficacy of the proposed framework, demonstrating enhanced predictive fidelity, robust generalization, and improved physical consistency. A comparative analysis reveals that the AC-PI-RNN significantly outperforms traditional RNN and PINN models, showing a distinct advantage in capturing the complete trajectory of whole-life crack propagation with high precision. The proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable approach for whole-life fatigue crack growth rate prediction under complex loading conditions.

verified_metadata.title: Adversarial contrastive learning to augment deep knowledge tracing
verified_metadata.abstract: Knowledge Tracing forecasts students’ future learning outcomes by analyzing historical interactions and modeling learning trajectories, which is essential for personalized learning on online education platforms. However, deep knowledge tracing methods face challenges due to data sparsity, which hinders their ability to differentiate between interactions and leads to overfitting. To address the challenge of data sparsity, this paper proposes a deep knowledge tracing approach that integrates an adversarial contrastive learning framework. This framework generates challenging adversarial samples and uses contrastive learning to refine the model’s discrimination accuracy, helping it learn subtle distinctions between sample categories and improving overall performance. Additionally, our approach incorporates a self-attention mechanism to integrate information from multiple knowledge points, further improving adversarial sample quality through enhanced question embeddings. Experimental results on various real-world educational datasets show that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, particularly in datasets with different levels of sparsity, effectively mitigating overfitting. Furthermore, the adversarial contrastive learning framework not only improves the performance of individual models but also demonstrates scalability and flexibility, enabling integration and enhancement of numerous existing knowledge tracing models.

verified_metadata.title: Anomaly detection of bamboo chopsticks based on cross-domain mixup augmentation and self-supervised learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Aiming at the practical problem of visual detection of abnormal surface quality of disposable bamboo chopsticks in an industrial production environment, this paper proposes an application-oriented anomaly detection algorithm based on cross-domain mixup augmentation (CDMA) and self-supervised learning to improve the inspection quality of bamboo chopsticks in production. Firstly, a novel data augmentation algorithm is proposed, which combines cross-domain sample images unrelated to chopsticks images with normal sample images to generate pseudo-abnormal samples and drive model learning. Then, a self-supervised learning algorithm based on intra-class relevance retrieval and reconstruction constraints is proposed. This model reconstructs the normal input images and its associated intra-class image, and at the same time, adds regular term constraints to the pseudo-abnormal images, so that their reconstruction errors could not be lower than a limited value, so as to increase the discrimination with the normal samples. Finally, the maximum local error is used to generate anomaly scores for detection. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy and speed performance of the algorithm have reached an advanced level.

verified_metadata.title: Fractal-guided multi-scale contrastive learning for robust liver tumor classification in ultrasound
verified_metadata.abstract: Ultrasound-based liver lesion classification remains challenging because diagnostically relevant cues are often localized, structurally heterogeneous, and easily corrupted by speckle noise, boundary ambiguity, and acquisition variability. Existing deep learning methods mainly emphasize global image-level representations and may therefore be suboptimal for modeling lesion-relevant local morphology. We propose a structure-constrained multi-scale contrastive learning framework for liver ultrasound classification. During training, semantic-guided anchoring is used to identify informative local regions, within which positive samples are selected under joint constraints of semantic similarity, local statistical consistency, and fractal-based structural complexity. A multi-scale local positive mining strategy and multi-positive supervised contrastive objective are further introduced to capture lesion patterns across different spatial granularities and enhance class discrimination. Importantly, the framework requires no auxiliary annotations during inference and operates directly on full ultrasound images. Experiments on a private four-class liver ultrasound dataset and two public ultrasound datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over representative convolutional neural network-based, Transformer-based, self-supervised, and ultrasound-specific methods. On the private dataset, the proposed method achieved 97.27% accuracy, and maintained 91.15% accuracy on an independent external validation cohort. Ablation studies and interpretability analyses further show that the method improves both structural discriminability and lesion-focused attention. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and practically deployable solution for robust liver lesion classification in ultrasound imaging.

verified_metadata.title: Enhancing air quality forecasting through homogeneous transfer learning: A novel approach for improved accuracy
verified_metadata.abstract: Air pollution from various sources poses a significant threat to human health and the environment. Developing accurate air quality prediction models is crucial for effective environmental monitoring and public health management. Transfer learning has emerged as a promising approach to enhance such models by leveraging knowledge from related domains. This research paper explores the application of homogeneous transfer learning for building more efficient air quality prediction models. By adapting pre-trained models to new air quality datasets, transfer learning improves predictive accuracy, reduces training time, and addresses data scarcity issues. Meteorological and pollutant data from Trivandrum are collected to develop an Air Quality Prediction model. The knowledge from this prebuilt model is then utilized to construct an Air Quality Index (AQI) model for the Cochin region using the deep learning algorithms Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), where data availability is limited. Experimental evaluations on diverse datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of homogeneous transfer learning in enhancing air quality forecasting. The findings highlight the impact of transfer learning in creating robust air quality index models, aiding pollution control and mitigation strategies.

verified_metadata.title: Solving ill-posed inverse heat conduction: Reconstruction of blast furnace inner wall temperature fields using a physics-informed diffusion model
verified_metadata.abstract: The internal temperature field of a blast furnace, vital for steelmaking, impacts energy use, emissions, and smelting costs, ensuring operational stability. Direct measurement of inner wall temperatures is infeasible due to the furnace’s enclosed, dusty, high-temperature, and high-pressure environment. Current approaches thus rely on sparse outer wall thermocouple measurements to reconstruct the internal temperature field via mathematical models. However, the large furnace volume coupled with limited outer wall data lead to a highly ill-posed inverse heat conduction problem, hindering accuracy and efficiency for industrial needs. To address this, we propose Diffusion-PINN, a Diffusion-Physics-Informed Neural Networks, which transforms the temperature field inversion into a diffusion-based generation process for temperature distribution maps. For the inverse heat conduction problem, the diffusion model is designed to fit the joint distribution of inner and outer wall temperature fields, directly generating coupled temperature distributions to circumvent the multi-solution issue of inverse problems. To address sparse measurement points and enhance solution accuracy, physical heat transfer information is embedded as conditional constraints in the diffusion process, progressively narrowing the constraint range during training. A dynamic loss-pulling algorithm is further proposed to enhance both solution accuracy and training speed. For the challenge of large spatial scales, the computationally intensive inversion process is reduced to a highly parallelizable map generation task, enabling rapid reconstruction of large-scale temperature fields. Simulations demonstrate that this method effectively addresses ill-posed inverse heat conduction problems. When applied to blast furnace smelting, it achieves the accuracy and efficiency required for industrial applications, offering substantial practical value.

verified_metadata.title: A Dual-Encoder Convolutional Neural Networks–Frequency Transformer framework with bidirectional attention for precise brain tumor segmentation
verified_metadata.abstract: Brain tumors present significant neurological challenges with high mortality rates, where early diagnosis based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is clinically vital but is hindered by labor-intensive manual segmentation. To overcome limitations in existing approaches, where convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggle with global context dependencies and Transformers face computational inefficiency, we propose a dual-branched framework called bifurcated fusion dual-encoder convolutional neural networks –frequency Transformer (BiF-DTNet). The BiF-DTNet employs a dual-encoder architecture, where the CNN encoder captures local features. In contrast, the frequency-domain vision Transformer (FViT) encoder efficiently models global context through fast Fourier transform and self-attention. The model incorporates bidirectional spatial-channel attention (BISC) blocks for effective multi-scale feature fusion, enhancing segmentation accuracy. While BiF-DTNet performs feature encoding on two-dimensional (2D) axial slices for computational efficiency, the model reconstructs the final segmentation in a volumetric manner, enabling precise and coherent three-dimensional (3D) tumor prediction. Evaluated on the brain tumor segmentation (BraTS) 2020 and BraTS 2021 benchmarks, BiF-DTNet achieves Dice scores of 80.42%/85.15%/91.34% (enhancing tumor (ET)/tumor core (TC)/whole tumor (WT)) on BraTS 2020 and 85.98%/91.25%/93.64% on BraTS 2021, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. These results conclusively demonstrate BiF-DTNet’s superiority in precise 3D tumor segmentation, particularly for irregular boundaries and small lesions, through its synergistic integration of local and global features.

title: Active learning driven materials discovery for low thermal conductivity rare-earth pyrochlore for thermal barrier coatings
abstract: High-Entropy/multicomponent rare-earth oxides (HECs and MCCs) show promise as alternative materials for thermal barrier coatings (TBC) with the ability to tailor properties based on the combination of rare-earth elements present. By enabling the substitution of scarce or supply-risk rare-earths with more readily available alternatives while maintaining comparable material performance, HECs and MCCs offer a valuable path towards alternative TBC material design. However, navigating this search space of compositionally complex materials is both time and resource intensive. In this study, an active learning (AL) framework was employed to identify HEC/MCC materials with a pyrochlore structure, with acceptable thermal conductivity (TC) for TBC applications. The AL framework was applied through a Bayesian optimisation (BO) strategy, coupled with a random forest surrogate model. TC was selected as the optimisation criterion as that is the most fundamental requirement of TBC materials. Over two iterations of the AL cycle, four compositions were generated and synthesised in the lab for experimental evaluation. The first iteration yielded two single-phase pyrochlores, ( La 0 . 29 Nd 0 . 36 Gd 0 . 36 ) 2 Zr 2 O 7 and ( La 0 . 333 Nd 0 . 26 Gd 0 . 15 Ho 0 . 15 Yb 0 . 111 ) 2 Zr 2 O 7 , with measured thermal conductivities of 2.03 and 1.90 W/mK, respectively. The surrogate model predicted a TC of 2.009 W/mK for both compositions, demonstrating its accuracy for completely new compositions. The second iteration compositions showed dual-phase when synthesised, highlighting the need to take into account phase formation in the AL framework.

verified_metadata.title: Toward brain magnetic resonance imaging analysis intelligence: A review of federated learning and visual foundation models
verified_metadata.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to brain research and clinical care. However, heterogeneity across scanners, acquisition protocols, and populations, together with privacy constraints, limits the reliability and scalability of the magnetic resonance imaging analysis. In this review, we use brain MRI analysis intelligence (BMI) to denote a layered and governance-aware framework. This framework integrates visual foundation models (VFMs) and federated learning (FL) through shared anatomical representations, lightweight center-local adaptation, and federated orchestration with provenance tracking, privacy budgets, and rollback mechanisms. This review (i) outlines brain magnetic resonance imaging fundamentals and major task categories; (ii) surveys federated learning as a practical route for multi-center collaboration without sharing raw data; and (iii) summarizes visual foundation model pretraining and fine-tuning methods for label-efficient and cross-contrast adaptation. Finally, we summarize three principles toward brain magnetic resonance imaging analysis intelligence: representation first, orchestration always, and measure what matters. Looking ahead, federated visual foundation models, domain adaptation, and governance-aware continual learning could further advance the analysis intelligence toward routinely audited clinical use.

title: Joint underwater image enhancement and multi-scale fish detection
abstract: Automatic fish detection in images plays a crucial role in marine biodiversity monitoring and environmental conservation. The advent of deep learning has significantly improved the results achievable in fish detection; however, underwater challenges such as scale variability, optical distortions, and color inconsistencies reveal some limitations of conventional deep learning-based detectors. To address these issues, we propose an improved fish detection model designed for underwater environments trained to perform joint underwater image enhancement and multi-scale fish detection. While incorporating structural enhancements for multi-scale robustness, such as a dedicated tiny object detection head and attention mechanisms, the core of our approach resides in the joint training of an underwater image enhancement module with the detector. We evaluate our method on two challenging test sets. The experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average precision between 0.84 and 0.89. Despite its superior accuracy, the proposed solution maintains a lightweight architecture with only 24 millions of parameters and ensures real-time processing capabilities (13 frames per second on edge hardware), highlighting its potential for effective deployment in marine research and autonomous fisheries monitoring. • YOLO-JUICE boosts small-object detection with an extra tiny-object head. • YOLO-JUICE preserves details without extra cost with a space to depth module. • YOLO-JUICE refines spatial and channel features with a spatial-channel attention. • YOLO-JUICE is jointly trained for image classification and enhancement.

title: Accurately modelling the resting-state functional connectivity with eigen-based connected-graph diffusion model
abstract: Understanding how functional dynamics emerge from the brain’s underlying structural architecture remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Conventional graph diffusion (GD) models are limited by sparse anatomical connectivity, leading to a failure to capture indirect connectivity and negatively correlated relationships. To overcome these challenges, we introduce hypergraphs and deep neural networks to enhance the representation of brain connectivity. Specifically, graphs and hypergraphs are integrated to construct a connected-graph, providing a comprehensive representation of inter-regional brain connectivity. The Fourier-induced deep neural network is employed to infer latent inter-regional relationships from structural connectivity by leveraging spectral features, effectively capturing both low- and high-frequency components. These deduced relationships are incorporated into the connected-graph, giving rise to a connected-graph diffusion (CD) model, which is further refined via eigen-decomposition to form an eigen-based connected-graph diffusion (ECD) model. Evaluated on 1012 subjects from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) S1200 release, the ECD model achieves a mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.7230 in functional connectivity (FC) prediction, outperforming the GD model (0.5513) and CD model (0.6518). The stability analysis demonstrates that the prediction of the ECD model is reliable. This work demonstrates that integrating biological mechanisms with machine learning methods can accurately model complex brain networks, with implications for neural signal processing, brain-inspired computing, and neuropsychiatric diagnosis.

verified_metadata.title: Accurately modelling the resting-state functional connectivity with eigen-based connected-graph diffusion model
verified_metadata.abstract: Understanding how functional dynamics emerge from the brain’s underlying structural architecture remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Conventional graph diffusion (GD) models are limited by sparse anatomical connectivity, leading to a failure to capture indirect connectivity and negatively correlated relationships. To overcome these challenges, we introduce hypergraphs and deep neural networks to enhance the representation of brain connectivity. Specifically, graphs and hypergraphs are integrated to construct a connected-graph, providing a comprehensive representation of inter-regional brain connectivity. The Fourier-induced deep neural network is employed to infer latent inter-regional relationships from structural connectivity by leveraging spectral features, effectively capturing both low- and high-frequency components. These deduced relationships are incorporated into the connected-graph, giving rise to a connected-graph diffusion (CD) model, which is further refined via eigen-decomposition to form an eigen-based connected-graph diffusion (ECD) model. Evaluated on 1012 subjects from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) S1200 release, the ECD model achieves a mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.7230 in functional connectivity (FC) prediction, outperforming the GD model (0.5513) and CD model (0.6518). The stability analysis demonstrates that the prediction of the ECD model is reliable. This work demonstrates that integrating biological mechanisms with machine learning methods can accurately model complex brain networks, with implications for neural signal processing, brain-inspired computing, and neuropsychiatric diagnosis.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed neural network modeling for digital control of pneumatic systems with binary valve inputs and adaptive parameter identification
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling of pneumatic actuation systems is crucial for design optimization and control stability. Traditional physics-based models struggle with accuracy and adaptability due to factors like gas compressibility, nonlinear friction, and varying operating conditions, while data-driven models often lack physical consistency and generalize poorly under extrapolated conditions. Although physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) effectively combine physical priors with data-driven learning, existing approaches focus primarily on systems with continuous control inputs, with limited attention given to digitally controlled pneumatic systems using binary on-off valve signals and hybrid dynamics. Furthermore, most PINN methods assume known physical parameters. This paper presents a PINN-based framework for digitally controlled pneumatic systems, directly using binary valve signals as inputs, embedding governing dynamics as soft constraints in the loss function, and introducing a physical-parameter encoder for key constants. An adaptive range-optimization mechanism is also introduced to identify difficult-to-calibrate parameters such as dead volume and friction. Validation of the approach on two pneumatic platforms demonstrates its superiority over purely data-driven feedforward neural networks (FNN) in predicting displacement and pressure, achieving R2 > 0.99 under supply pressure conditions outside the training set. These results confirm the model's accuracy, generalization, and adaptability across diverse operating conditions.

verified_metadata.abstract:
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) by embedding physical laws directly into the training process, making them particularly attractive for complex engineering applications such as computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Despite their promise, conventional PINNs often struggle to enforce boundary conditions (BCs) accurately, resulting in suboptimal performance for challenging flow simulations.
This paper proposes a novel Adaptive Loss Weighting (ALW) scheme combined with a Gradient-Based Attention (GBA) mechanism to enhance boundary condition enforcement in PINNs. The ALW strategy dynamically rebalances the contributions of the PDE residual and boundary loss terms during training, while the GBA mechanism selectively emphasizes boundary collocation points associated with large gradients, thereby guiding the optimization process more effectively.

verified_metadata.title: Uncertainty-aware precipitation nowcasting with diffusion model simulating precipitation evolution processes
verified_metadata.abstract: Precipitation nowcasting is a critical field of meteorology research. Current methods fail to fully account for uncertainties in nowcasting, leading to issues such as ambiguity, omission, and localized bias. This paper introduces a conditional diffusion model to mitigate uncertainty by modeling the probability distribution of spatio-temporal evolution features of precipitation. Based on the continuity equation of precipitation evolution, an evolution feature autoencoder decouples the precipitation evolution process into motion fields and precipitation intensity residuals through two distinct encoding pathways. The diffusion model based on U-shaped architecture with spatio-temporal attention mechanism, simulates precipitation evolution conditioned on evolution features. Accurate nowcasting is achieved by decoding the generated spatio-temporal evolution features into precipitation. Extensive experiments on two real-world precipitation datasets demonstrate that the proposed method mitigates uncertainties in nowcasting, particularly for high-intensity precipitation, achieving improvements of at least 10.9% in Critical Success Index (CSI) and and 9.8% in Heidecker Skill Score (HSS) over state-of-the-art methods.

title: Surrogate modeling of inductance in axial active magnetic bearings using data-driven and physics-informed neural networks
abstract: In active magnetic bearing (AMB) systems, accurate modeling of nonlinear electromagnetic effects is essential for high-fidelity simulation and control design. Conventional approaches rely on either analytical approximations, which are often too simplified to capture the full nonlinear behavior, or on finite element method (FEM)-based lookup tables, which require computationally expensive interpolation and exhibit poor generalization in sparsely sampled regions. This motivates efficient surrogate modeling approaches that preserve FEM-level accuracy while enabling scalable, continuous evaluation. This paper proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for inductance modeling in axial AMBs, combining data-driven learning with electromagnetic circuit physics. Two architectures are developed for comparison: a purely data-driven NN and a PINN. The main novelty of this work is a physics-informed learning formulation in which the actuator voltage equation as an ordinary differential equation (ODE) constraint, is embedded into the PINN loss function, enabling consistent enforcement of the nonlinear electrical dynamics and the coupled dependence of inductance on airgap position and coil current. The trained models are validated under open- and closed-loop conditions with position and inner current control, followed by offline experimental verification using data collected from a real AMB setup. Comparative analysis with a data-driven NN, Polynomial Regression, and Gaussian Process Regression surrogate models demonstrates that incorporating physics-based constraints into the loss function improves model accuracy and consistency, particularly in sparsely sampled regions. The proposed PINN thus provides a physics-consistent and computationally efficient surrogate model for axial AMB systems, replacing conventional FEM-based lookup tables.

title: When control meets large language models: From words to dynamics
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) are transforming engineering and technology through enhanced control capabilities and decision support, they are simultaneously evolving into complex dynamical systems whose behavior must be regulated. This duality highlights a reciprocal connection in which prompts support control system design while control theory helps shape prompts to achieve specific goals efficiently. In this study, we frame this emerging interconnection of LLM and control as a bidirectional continuum, from prompt design to system dynamics. First, we investigate how LLMs can advance the field of control in two distinct capacities: directly, by assisting in the design and synthesis of controllers, and indirectly, by augmenting research workflows. Second, we examine how control concepts help LLMs steer their trajectories away from undesired meanings, improving reachability and alignment via input optimization, parameter editing, and activation-level interventions. Third, we look into deeper integrations by treating LLMs as dynamic systems within a state-space framework, where their internal representations are closely linked to external control loops. Finally, we identify key challenges and outline future research directions to understand LLM behavior and develop interpretable and controllable LLMs that are as trustworthy and robust as their electromechanical counterparts, thereby ensuring they continue to support and safeguard society.

title: Improving fire and smoke detection with ghost convolutions, Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Networks, and image enhancement
abstract: Wildfire monitoring is an important application of artificial intelligence for reducing ecological, economic, and human losses through earlier and more reliable fire and smoke detection. Conventional methods, such as satellite surveillance, often suffer from limited coverage, delayed response times, and reduced effectiveness in complex outdoor environments. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family of object detectors, have shown strong potential for real-time wildfire detection. However, these models still face challenges related to computational overhead and reduced robustness under low-contrast conditions. This paper introduces You Only Look Once version 11 small with Ghost Neck and Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (YOLOv11s-GN+BIFPN), an enhanced object detection framework based on the small variant of YOLOv11. Ghost Neck (GN) modules are incorporated into both the backbone and neck of the network to reduce feature redundancy and improve computational efficiency. A Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BIFPN) is further integrated at the Pyramid Level 4 (P4) stage to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion, enabling more effective detection of fire and smoke objects across different sizes. In addition, several image enhancement techniques are systematically evaluated, including contrast stretching (CS), histogram equalization (HE), dual gamma correction (DGC), contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), and their hybrid combinations. Experiments on the Fire and Smoke dataset containing 11,667 images show that CLAHE+CS preprocessing combined with YOLOv11s-GN+BIFPN achieves the best performance, reaching 89.50% mean Average Precision (mAP). This result surpasses the baseline YOLOv11 and recent state-of-the-art models.

title: GeoFusion: A hybrid convolutional neural network-transformer model for boreal peatland classification
abstract: The generation of high-resolution boreal peatland maps through the integration of multi-source remote sensing data provides critical support for greenhouse gas inventories and environmental management. In this study, we propose GeoFusion, a pixel-wise peatland classification architecture that leverages open-access radar imagery from Sentinel-1 and optical imagery from Sentinel-2. GeoFusion combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for hierarchical local feature extraction with vision transformers (ViTs) for modeling long-range dependencies, enabling effective fusion of spectral–textural and structural information. The architecture also incorporates data augmentation, multi-head self-attention, and dropout regularization to enhance robustness and mitigate overfitting. Performance was assessed at two classification levels: site type and fertility level, capturing both ecological diversity and functional characteristics of complex peatland ecosystems. Comparative experiments against well-known deep learning models and hybrid Transformer-based models were conducted across three ecologically distinct regions in Finland. The obtained results demonstrate that GeoFusion outperforms other models and achieves average accuracies of 79.25% and 72.68% for fertility-level and site-type predictions, respectively.

verified_metadata.title: A comparative study on monthly precipitation forecasting using time-series foundation models in South Korea
verified_metadata.abstract: In this study, four artificial intelligence-based time-series foundation models were evaluated: a generative pretrained transformer for time series (TimeGPT), Time Series Foundation Model (TimesFM), Chronos, and Moirai. These models were used to forecast monthly precipitation in four major cities in South Korea: Seoul, Daejeon, Daegu, and Busan. Because of increasing uncertainty in weather forecasts caused by climate change, the development of accurate and efficient prediction models is critical. Historical monthly precipitation data from the Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS), spanning 1985 to 2024, were partitioned into separate training and test sets. We applied a sliding-window approach for continuous model retraining and quantitatively evaluated the prediction accuracy against seasonal autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. The results highlight the complementary strengths of the time-series foundation models and LSTM baseline relative to the SARIMA benchmark. Moirai was effective in predicting intense, highly variable monsoon rainfall, whereas TimesFM provided stable skill during other, more predictable seasons and surpassed SARIMA in root mean square error (RMSE) for Seoul. The LSTM baseline underperformed in full-period error metrics, but reproduced peak and dry-month precipitation more accurately than the other models, underscoring a tradeoff between average accuracy and fidelity to extremes. SARIMA achieved the lowest full-period RMSE and mean absolute error for most city–lead time combinations. Overall, these findings suggest that combining time-series foundation models with traditional statistical and deep-learning forecasting methods can yield more balanced forecasting performance with lower full-period errors and better capture of extremes.

title: Identifying the post-pandemic determinants of low performing students in Latin America through interpretable Machine Learning methods
abstract: The high prevalence of students not achieving the basic competencies in Latin America is concerning. Even more so given the region’s deep structural inequalities and the larger post-pandemic regional learning losses. Within this scenario, this paper contributes to the identification of the determinants of bottom and low performers (below level 2) using recent advancements on explainable machine learning methods. In particular, relying on PISA 2022 data for 10 countries and using the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis, I identify critical factors impacting on the student performance across low performers groups. I find that a student with the highest probability of being a not achiever speaks a minority language and had repeated, has no digital devices at home, comes from a poor family and works for payment half of the week, and the school he/she attends has wide disadvantages such as bad school climate, weak ICT infrastructure and poor teaching quality (only a third of teachers being certified). Regarding countries' estimates, I find quite homogeneous patterns as far as global average contribution of top ranked factors is concerned, with repetition at primary, household wealth, and educational ICT inputs being top ten ranked covariates in at least 8 out of the 10 total countries. The paper findings contribute to the broad literature on strategies to identify and to target those most left behind in Latin American education systems.

verified_metadata.title: Identifying the post-pandemic determinants of low performing students in Latin America through interpretable Machine Learning methods
verified_metadata.abstract: The high prevalence of students not achieving the basic competencies in Latin America is concerning. Even more so given the region’s deep structural inequalities and the larger post-pandemic regional learning losses. Within this scenario, this paper contributes to the identification of the determinants of bottom and low performers (below level 2) using recent advancements on explainable machine learning methods. In particular, relying on PISA 2022 data for 10 countries and using the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis, I identify critical factors impacting on the student performance across low performers groups. I find that a student with the highest probability of being a not achiever speaks a minority language and had repeated, has no digital devices at home, comes from a poor family and works for payment half of the week, and the school he/she attends has wide disadvantages such as bad school climate, weak ICT infrastructure and poor teaching quality (only a third of teachers being certified). Regarding countries' estimates, I find quite homogeneous patterns as far as global average contribution of top ranked factors is concerned, with repetition at primary, household wealth, and educational ICT inputs being top ten ranked covariates in at least 8 out of the 10 total countries. The paper findings contribute to the broad literature on strategies to identify and to target those most left behind in Latin American education systems.

verified_metadata.title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph contrastive learning for node classification and anomaly detection
verified_metadata.abstract:
Dynamic graph contrastive learning methods commonly assume that nodes preserve stable structural roles over time. However, real-world networks often violate this assumption: nodes may change their connectivity patterns, reactivate after long inactivity, or undergo local structural reorganisation. Such heterogeneity not only weakens temporal consistency constraints but also causes volatile nodes to generate unreliable negative signals. This work shows that temporal contrasts vary substantially in reliability and should not be treated uniformly.

We introduce an uncertainty-aware dynamic graph contrastive learning framework driven by temporal contrast uncertainty, which quantifies the reliability of cross-temporal contrasts directly from the graph structure. Nodes with low temporal contrast uncertainty exhibit stable structural patterns, whereas nodes with high temporal contrast uncertainty indicate volatile evolution. Leveraging temporal contrast uncertainty, the proposed framework integrates three mechanisms: (1) adaptive temporal sampling, (2) uncertainty-weighted contrastive objectives, and (3) group-level prototype calibration to correct estimation bias. We theoretically show that temporal contrast uncertainty weighting yields a favourable trade-off with respect to the mutual information lower bound, while prototype calibration provides an upper bound for controlling temporal drift. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets for node classification and seven datasets (including two with real-world anomaly labels) for anomaly detection demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with pronounced improvements on datasets containing a high proportion of structurally volatile nodes.

title: Subgraph-based contrastive learning with distribution alignment for graph anomaly detection

verified_metadata.title: Subgraph-based contrastive learning with distribution alignment for graph anomaly detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Graph anomaly detection has become increasingly crucial for identifying suspicious patterns in complex networks, with broad applications in domains such as social network analysis, fraud detection and network security. Recent advances in graph contrastive learning (GCL) have demonstrated great potential for unsupervised anomaly detection by capturing discriminative representations from local subgraphs. However, existing GCL-based methods still face challenges in detecting subtle anomalies due to the inherent structural heterogeneity of real-world graphs. Furthermore, their reliance on rigid or stochastic subgraph sampling strategies limits their ability to capture fine-grained structural variations, thereby reducing detection sensitivity. To address these limitations, we propose a subgraph-based contrastive learning framework for graph anomaly detection, referred to as SubGAD. Specifically, SubGAD constructs informative subgraph views by integrating first- and second-order neighbors, thereby capturing richer contextual patterns without the bias of fixed-size sampling. It first performs node-to-subgraph contrastive learning to highlight local deviations, and then introduces the Graph Earth Mover’s Distance (G-EMD) to align subgraph representations across views, effectively quantifying structural and semantic discrepancies in a distribution-aware manner. Moreover, SubGAD mitigates positional bias through subgraph centering and performs kernel-based anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets demonstrate that SubGAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving notable performance gains and confirming its effectiveness in detecting subtle anomalies in attributed graphs. Our source code is available at https://github.com/GNNteam/SubGAD.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed belief rule base with high interpretability model for complex mechatronic system performance evaluation considering intermittent power
verified_metadata.abstract: Intermittent power (IP) has become an important operational strategy for complex mechatronic systems (CMS) due to its energy-saving potential and dynamic adaptability. However, most existing performance evaluation models assume stable power supply and therefore fail to accurately capture the performance degradation of CMS under IP conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed belief rule base model with high interpretability for CMS performance evaluation under IP conditions, termed IPBRB-IP. An event-driven damage accumulation model for IP (DAM-IP) is first developed to calculate dynamic damage factors, through explicit embedding of physical knowledge. An interval belief rule base is then constructed, where the bounds of belief distributions are determined conservatively and aggressively using expert knowledge and limited data. Based on the calculated damage factors, the initial belief distributions are adaptively inferred, allowing accurate representation of the performance degradation trajectory of CMS. To further preserve interpretability, an interpretability-constrained optimization criterion is introduced to ensure cognitive consistency between physics-corrected expert understanding and model outputs. Finally, a CMS case study under IP conditions demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach. From an artificial intelligence perspective, this work develops a physics-informed and interpretable belief rule base framework that integrates damage modeling and knowledge–data fusion for CMS performance evaluation under IP. From an engineering perspective, the proposed IPBRB-IP model provides a transparent and reliable tool for performance evaluation of CMS operating under IP conditions.

verified_metadata.title: A novel extreme gradient boosting based adaptive genetic algorithm method for electro-thermal performance optimization of power integrated circuits
verified_metadata.abstract: Effective thermal management for high-power-density integrated circuits faces significant challenges due to electrical and dimensional constraints in modern electronic systems. Existing design methods often treat thermal analysis as a post-layout verification step, lacking efficient co-optimization strategies. This paper proposes a co-optimization method that integrates data-driven modeling with an adaptive genetic algorithm. First, an electro-thermal coupling model generates a calibrated dataset, enabling the development of a high-precision chip temperature predictor using the extreme gradient boosting algorithm. The proposed model then optimizes printed circuit board layout parameters under simultaneous electrical and dimensional constraints. The integrated extreme gradient boosting based adaptive genetic algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional models, achieving an average temperature reduction of 2.92% over the standard genetic algorithm and 4.93% over Bayesian optimization. Subsequent simulations and experimental validations confirm the accuracy of steady-state temperature predictions. Experimental findings reveal that, across varying load conditions, the optimized samples exhibit an average target temperature reduction of 7.95%, with a maximum decrease of 8.54 °C. These results demonstrate its practical value of the proposed model, providing an optimization strategy for thermal design of high-power-density integrated circuits.

verified_metadata.title: Hybrid fractional-order physics-informed neural network and reinforcement learning framework with blockchain for dynamic optimization of flux, fouling and heavy metal rejection in metal foam-enhanced direct contact membrane distillation systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in industrial wastewater requires sustainable remediation solutions. This study introduces a hybrid computational framework combining Fractional-Order Physics-Informed Neural Networks (FO-PINNs) for surrogate modeling, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for dynamic optimization, and blockchain for auditable logging, applied to Direct Contact Membrane Distillation (DCMD). Under CFD-verified simulation conditions over a 12-h cycle (1500 epochs), the framework predicts a mean permeate flux of 4.51 L/m^{2}.h, representing a 32% improvement compared to non-foam CFD baselines, and suggests a 68% reduction in fouling rate. Energy-intensity modeling, after subtracting computational overhead, indicates an approximate 15% net reduction in CO_{2} emissions under the simulated operating conditions. Blockchain provides auditable data tracking, while a GUI facilitates dynamic optimization. While experimental validation remains necessary, this approach demonstrates the feasibility of physics-informed adaptive control for DCMD and offers a foundation for scalable, low-carbon wastewater treatment.

verified_metadata.title: Neural network-driven inverse design of a two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide with a 90-degree bend for low-loss and broadband transmission in telecommunication bands
verified_metadata.abstract: Optical communication systems require compact routing elements that maintain high transmission while minimizing bending loss. This study presents an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design framework based on a multilayer perceptron neural network to optimize a two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide incorporating a 90-degree bend for broadband telecommunication operation. First, three candidate bend configurations were evaluated using full-wave electromagnetic simulations, and the third configuration provided the best conventional performance, achieving a maximum bandwidth of 165.1 nm with a minimum transmission loss of 11.76 percent, including 73.1 nm within the original telecommunication band. Next, the multilayer perceptron neural network was trained on simulated samples incorporating waveguide operating conditions, enabling rapid prediction of improved geometric parameters. The waveguide predicted by the neural network was then re-simulated, demonstrating a 26.288 percent increase in bandwidth to 208.5 nm. In this case, the proposed waveguide completely covered the original telecommunications band and 50.6 nm of the telecommunications Extended-band. Across the entire operating bandwidth, transmission losses remained below 10 percent, and at the peak bandwidth, they were below 1.2 percent, representing an 89.8 percent reduction compared to the previous best case. These results show that neural network-based inverse design can efficiently identify parameter settings that substantially improve bandwidth and reduce loss in photonic crystal waveguide bends, providing a practical route toward data-driven design of photonic integrated circuits.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed surrogate modeling for hydrogen production in plastic waste gasification
verified_metadata.abstract: In this study, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework was proposed for predicting hydrogen production in the gasification of plastic waste by embedding kinetic- and equilibrium-based physical knowledge as soft constraints into the learning process. Three PINN variants—kinetic, equilibrium, and combined—were developed and compared with a conventional artificial neural network (ANN) under varying dataset ratios (1%, 10%, 50%, and 100%) to evaluate their performance in data-scarce environments. Although the ANN model exhibited substantial performance degradation with limited data, all PINN models maintained robust predictive accuracy (R^{2}, the coefficient of determination >0.99) and physically plausible behavior within the surrogate modeling scope, with the equilibrium model achieving the lowest error and the combined model showing the best overall balance. Gradient-based residual analysis also confirmed that the PINN results were consistent with expected thermodynamic and reaction trends, rather than strictly enforcing the governing physical laws. Although the models were trained on simulated data from a simplified single-unit process, they have demonstrated their effectiveness as a proof-of-concept for physics-guided surrogate modeling, providing a useful basis for future real-time optimization and control of hydrogen production systems.

verified_metadata.title: Boundary Region Reinforcement Physics-Informed Neural Networks for solving partial differential equations
verified_metadata.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a deep learning framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). However, standard approaches often struggle to strictly enforce boundary conditions, limiting their computational accuracy, especially in complex multiphysics coupled systems. To address this challenge, we introduce Boundary Region Reinforcement Physics-Informed Neural Networks (BRR-PINNs), a novel framework designed to strengthen boundary constraint enforcement and significantly improve solution accuracy. The method converts non-Dirichlet conditions into exact Dirichlet boundaries using intermediate variables to reduce redundant loss terms, and applies a spatial reinforcement function to prioritize training near boundaries. We validate the effectiveness of BRR-PINNs on a two-dimensional axisymmetric thermo-elastic coupling problem, involving a circular ring subjected to both thermal and mechanical loads. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms several existing approaches, achieving approximately one order of magnitude improvement in accuracy.

verified_metadata.title: Fragment target-based unsupervised transformer-enhanced deep image prior for selected-band hyperspectral image super-resolution
verified_metadata.abstract: High-resolution hyperspectral images enable precise fragment detection, explosive residue analysis, and explosion-proof design. Owing to technical restrictions in hyperspectral sensor hardware, significant challenges exist in acquiring high-resolution hyperspectral images of small-sized fragments at a safe standoff distance. Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HISR) technology can compensate for the limitations of single-sensor imaging, enabling the simultaneous acquisition of spatial details and spectral information of fragments. However, most existing super-resolution networks are trained on simulated degraded image pairs, failing to account for the issue of spatial misalignment between heterogeneous sensors. Therefore, a mathematical observation model is developed to describe the physical degradation during the fusion of fragment low-resolution hyperspectral images and high-resolution Red-Green-Blue (RGB) images, considering the presence of spatial misalignment. Based on these models, we then propose a fragment target-based unsupervised transformer-enhanced deep image prior network (FT-UTDIP-Net) for selected-band HISR. The network comprises modules for image registration and blur kernel learning, initial image estimation generation, multi-scale feature progressive alignment, and super resolution hyperspectral image generation. The proposed method achieves promising fusion performance for HISR across both public and selected-band steel fragment datasets. Furthermore, downstream experiments demonstrate that the method significantly enhances fragment recognition performance. This study demonstrates feasibility for selected-band HISR of steel fragments under a controlled UAV acquisition setting.

verified_metadata.title: Toward ahead prediction of molten pool penetration states in laser welding via physics-informed spatiotemporal learning
verified_metadata.abstract: In laser welding, the penetration state is a critical factor affecting joint formation quality and service performance. However, during actual welding processes, the molten pool exhibits a delayed response to heat input, and the welding system inherently involves unavoidable delays, which significantly limit the effectiveness of traditional real-time monitoring and control methods. To address these issues, this research proposes a laser welding molten pool state ahead prediction method that integrates physics features based on dimensionless numbers, aiming to mitigate delay effects in the welding process and to provide predictive state information for intelligent welding process control. The proposed method exploits image sequences to characterize the dynamic behaviors of the molten pool and keyhole. By analyzing the thermal history characteristics of the welding process, a penetration state score model is introduced, providing a physical motivation for modeling temporal dependencies. On this basis, dimensionless number-based physics features are collaboratively integrated with image sequences, leading to the development of a physics-informed multi-scale temporal convolutional network (MSP-TCN). The proposed model is capable of learning the evolution patterns of the molten pool state across different welding scenarios in a more stable manner, thereby enabling ahead prediction of molten pool state sequences. Experimental validation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms purely image-driven models in terms of both prediction accuracy and generalization capability, providing an effective solution for delay compensation in laser welding processes.
