verified_metadata.title: Quantifying physics-informed causal pathways in flow-induced vibration heat transfer enhancement through spectral dynamics and mediation analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Most flow-induced vibration (FIV) studies rely on amplitude or correlations without quantifying causal paths. We introduce a physics-informed causal inference framework to explain heat transfer mechanisms. A directed acyclic graph was pre-specified from fluid–structure–thermal interaction principles and evaluated using mediation analysis of 120 high-fidelity simulations covering Re = 2300–7700, Ur = 5–15, and G = 0.4–1.2. The optimal spectral-response regime achieved a peak performance evaluation criterion (PEC) of 1.32 ± 0.03 (sampling error; combined uncertainty ±0.06), exceeding the energy-efficiency threshold of PEC = 1.0, while excessive structural stiffness reduced PEC by 18.3%. Three dominant causal pathways were statistically validated, with path coefficients of |β| = 0.25–0.38 (bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero) (p < 0.001). Compared with an amplitude-only benchmark, spectral features explained an additional 18.3% of performance variance and mediated 63–64% of the total causal effect from system parameters to performance, demonstrating that vibration quality is not a secondary descriptor but a primary causal determinant. Physically, high Spectral Purity enabled vortex–thermal phase locking with Δt/T = 0.12 ± 0.02, Harmonic Energy Ratio predicted regime transitions with 87% accuracy and a 6% false-positive rate, and high Modal Coherence directed 72% of vibrational energy into productive thermal mixing, compared with only 38% in low-coherence configurations. Bootstrap resampling confirmed that the identified causal pathways remained directionally consistent in more than 96% of resamples. The present framework lies not only in predicting enhanced heat transfer but also in explaining why it occurs, thereby shifting FIV thermal-system design from amplitude maximization toward spectral-quality optimization.

verified_metadata.title: Attention-based graph neural operators for learning parametric response mappings in discrete structures
verified_metadata.abstract:
Parametric analysis of discrete engineering structures requires repeated finite element simulations, leading to high computational cost in design exploration. Graph neural operators have emerged as a promising surrogate modeling framework for learning parametric solution mappings on graph-structured systems; however, existing approaches remain limited in effectively capturing long-range dependencies.

This study introduces an attention-based graph neural operator (AGNO) for learning parametric response mappings in discrete structural systems under variations in node-indexed features, particularly structural geometry (via nodal coordinates) and applied nodal loading. The proposed model integrates kernel-induced graph neural operator layers, which emulate operator learning through edge-conditioned message passing, with a permutation-invariant global attention mechanism acting on graph-indexed latent functions, resulting in a unified local–global operator architecture.

The key contribution lies in addressing the locality of graph neural operators in the context of discrete structural systems through this local–global operator architecture. This formulation enables effective modeling of nonlocal structural interactions while preserving topology-aware local behavior, and provides a principled operator-learning framework tailored to graph-based structural response problems.

The approach is evaluated on benchmark problems involving two- and three-dimensional trusses and frames, including mesh-refinement studies and scaling to larger structural systems. Results show that AGNO demonstrates strong performance compared to existing graph-based and operator-learning surrogate models across the considered benchmarks, achieving lower prediction errors and improved robustness with respect to discretization refinement and increasing geometric complexity, while maintaining comparable computational cost. These findings indicate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for parametric response prediction in discrete structural systems under the tested conditions.

title: A unified causality-enhanced separable physics-informed neural network for predicting beam and plate dynamics
abstract: A thorough understanding of the dynamic behavior of structural elements, such as beams, plates, and membranes, is crucial for reliable structural analysis. This behavior is typically governed by higher-order partial differential equations (PDEs), which accurately capture their spatiotemporal response. However, the presence of high-order differential operators and inherent high-frequency components, especially over large spatial domains, poses challenges for Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). To tackle this challenge, we propose a causality-informed Separable Physics-Informed Neural Network (SPINN) framework augmented with auxiliary variables (Causal Aux SPINN) to enhance the performance of PINNs in structural engineering applications. The proposed framework integrates three key components. First, the SPINN formulation decomposes the spatiotemporal solution into low-rank components, allowing efficient representation of high-dimensional dynamic fields with reduced computational cost. Second, the causality-informed loss function re-weights the training objective to respect the temporal evolution of structural dynamics and mitigate error accumulation over time. Third, the auxiliary-variable formulation introduces additional outputs for second-order fields, such as curvature-related quantities, enabling accurate enforcement of fourth-order differential operators without relying solely on successive differentiation of displacement fields. The proposed “Causal Aux SPINN” algorithm is evaluated on both forward and inverse benchmarks in structural dynamics, including Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams, membranes, and Kirchhoff–Love plates. Across all benchmarks, the Causal Aux SPINN method consistently reduces error and improves robustness, while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to the Baseline SPINN formulation. Overall, coupling causal weighting with auxiliary-variable learning is shown to provide an effective framework for structural engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: Applications of generative models in medical imaging:A review
verified_metadata.abstract: Generative models have become a foundational technology for medical imaging, supporting image generation, enhancement, segmentation, registration, image-to-image translation, and anomaly detection. Despite the rapid growth of methodological work, the literature still lacks a unified comparative framework that helps practitioners decide between Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, and diffusion models for specific medical-imaging tasks; existing surveys also provide limited treatment of validation strategies, dataset constraints, and ethical or clinical considerations. This survey reviews representative methods from each model family across six core tasks, covering anomaly detection, image-to-image translation, image generation, segmentation, denoising, and registration, consolidating them into a unified comparison spanning accuracy, computational cost, data requirements, robustness, uncertainty quantification, and practical deployment. We further compile commonly used benchmark datasets together with their scale, diversity, and known limitations, and we critically discuss validation strategies, model complexity and regularization, and ethical, clinical, and practical considerations. Our key findings are threefold. First, no single model family dominates across all tasks, as Generative Adversarial Networks remain leading for image-to-image translation and data augmentation, Variational Autoencoders are well-suited to reconstruction-based anomaly detection where their posterior provides native uncertainty estimates, and diffusion models currently offer the strongest results in image generation, segmentation, and denoising. Second, practical deployment metrics and external validation remain under-reported in the literature, which limits clinical translation. Third, domain shift, demographic bias, regulatory uncertainty, and reproducibility are open challenges shared across model families. We close with a conceptual taxonomy organized along the model-family by imaging-task axis and outline future research directions.

title: Multi-component Weather Prediction using Self-Supervised Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Learning with Model Explainability
abstract: Accurate weather prediction remains a persistent challenge due to the multi-component nature of atmospheric systems and the limitations of traditional forecasting models. This study presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)–driven weather forecasting framework that integrates Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), self-supervised learning, ensemble learning, and explainable AI techniques. Particularly, we propose a Self-Supervised Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Learning (SSMFEL) model, which integrates low-, mid-, and high-fidelity long short-term memory architectures with regularization, dropout, and a decoder to extract meaningful patterns from unlabeled data. The proposed model achieved over 95% R-squared ( R 2 ) metric, coefficient of determination, for humidity and temperature prediction and more than 52% R 2 for wind speed and precipitation, significantly outperforming existing ML, DL, and transformer-based models. SSMFEL also demonstrated the 0.00018 Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 0.03489 root MSE across all components. Results from test statistic tests , sensitivity analysis, and fairness evaluation further confirmed the statistical superiority of the proposed approach. Model explainability analysis revealed that specific humidity is the most influential feature, while temperature and relative humidity contribute contextually. Theoretical analysis based on bias–variance reduction and generalization theory further supports the improved forecasting performance of the proposed method.

verified_metadata.title: Reinforcement learning-enhanced barrier function super-twisting sliding mode control for bidirectional electric vehicle charging with superconducting magnetic energy storage
verified_metadata.abstract: The fast development of electric vehicles is putting a strain on the possibility of having intelligent bidirectional charging infrastructures, which are capable of supporting vehicle to grid operation but are also able to handle renewable intermittency and rapid load swings. The current energy management and control policies of renewable-integrated charging stations frequently cannot be used to guarantee high power quality, real-time feasibility, and robust stability at the same time, especially when sophisticated storage technology is used. This paper develops a unified control and artificial intelligence solution to bidirectional electric vehicle charging which integrates superconducting magnetic energy storage with solar photovoltaic and wind generation. A barrier based super-twisting sliding mode controller is designed at the control level to impose safety requirements, enhance disturbance rejection, and reduce chattering with parameter uncertainty. Red Fox Optimization aims at optimizing controller gains with the view of improving dynamic performance. Bidirectional recurrent neural networks at the intelligence layer forecast renewable power, and a Deep Q-Network based reinforcement learning energy management system optimizes and determines the best power scheduling between the grid, renewable sources, electric vehicle battery and superconducting magnetic storage. In addition, performance of the proposed super-twisting sliding mode controller with enhanced barrier functionality is compared to a synergetic approach to control and confirmed in a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop experiment. High-fidelity simulations and experimental validation demonstrate improved charging efficiency, enhanced utilization of superconducting magnetic energy storage during fast transients, and reduced total harmonic distortion during transitions between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid modes. The proposed framework offers a scalable and intelligent solution for renewable-aware bidirectional charging in sustainable transportation systems.

verified_metadata.title: TDFormer: A novel triple decoupled transformer for accurate multi-step wind power forecasting
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of power systems. Long-term effective forecasting can optimize wind power generation planning and reduce operational costs. Although deep learning advancements have significantly improved wind power forecasting accuracy, existing methods often struggle to effectively separate the complex relationships between variables, features, and time dimensions in multivariate time-series data, limiting their predictive performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel model, named Triple Decoupled Transformer (TDFormer), for multi-step wind power forecasting. The model incorporates a novel Triple Decoupled Attention (TDA) mechanism to independently decouple input data across three dimensions—variables, features, and time—enabling more efficient and precise feature extraction. TDFormer adopts an encoder-decoder architecture to integrate historical data from multiple variables and future time sequences, making it ideal for multi-step wind power forecasting. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets from wind farms with varying capacities and geographical locations demonstrate that the proposed TDFormer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, especially in scenarios involving longer forecasting horizons. In addition, the model demonstrated excellent generalization ability and practical application potential in the transfer learning experiments, making it particularly suitable for newly established wind farms with limited data, and offering significant application value. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/USTC-AI4EEE/TDFormer.

title: Deep learning framework for the diagnosis of systemic sclerosis using serum-derived microbial signatures
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare and severe autoimmune disease of unknown etiology, currently lacking effective treatment. Therefore, early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical for improving clinical outcomes. Accumulating evidence implicates the human microbiome as a key contributor to SSc pathogenesis, with distinct microbial alterations identified in patients. Given that circulating anti-microbial immunoglobulin M(IgM) antibodies reflect recent and systemic microbial perturbations across multiple organ systems, comprehensive profiling of serum IgM antibodies against diverse microbial species may offer a promising strategy for predicting early disease development through the identification of SSc-associated microbial signatures. However, predictive diagnostic models incorporating microbiome derived serological data in SSc have not yet been developed. In this study, we introduce a novel and, interpretable deep learning framework based on Graph Attention Networks (GAT) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to enable accurate diagnosis of SSc using serum anti-microbial IgM antibody data and uncover valid inter-bacterial relationships. We analyzed a dataset comprising 126 individuals (76 SSc and 50 healthy controls). To capture complex inter-species correlations often overlooked by conventional tabular data, we first converted the microbial profiles into a graph structure. The constructed ensemble model, combining GAT for relational feature extraction and CNN for hierarchical pattern recognition, achieved a high diagnostic accuracy of 0.9051, representing an improvement of up to 10.96 percentage points over recent comparable studies. To interpret the model's diagnostic rationale, we applied Association Rule Mining (ARM) to the latent representations from the proposed framework's intermediate layer. This analysis revealed significant clustering patterns, distinguishing groups with specific microbial combinations common in SSc patients, and these patterns that were rarely observed in healthy controls. Our work presents a novel methodology for interpreting deep learning predictions in healthcare and provides initial evidence for the diagnostic potential of this approach in a rare disease setting, using only a small set of core microbial combinations. These findings suggest the potential to enhance screening efficiency for SSc and provide hypothesis-generating insights into biological mechanisms underlying the disease, warranting further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

verified_metadata.title: Prototype-driven contrastive learning enables transferable seismic representation
verified_metadata.abstract: Deep learning has become increasingly important in seismic monitoring and analysis, yet most existing methods remain heavily dependent on large labeled datasets and often transfer poorly across tasks and regions. To address these limitations, this study proposes ConProSeis, a self-supervised pretraining framework for learning transferable representations from seismic waveforms. ConProSeis develops a prototype-driven contrastive strategy that uses diverse physics-guided multi-view augmentations to improve representation robustness and reduce semantic shifts caused by perturbations. Intra-prototype and inter-prototype contrastive losses are further introduced to enhance feature discrimination. A dual-encoder architecture is adopted, in which the target encoder is updated by exponential moving average to stabilize training. Experiments on a large-scale Chinese seismic dataset show that the learned representations transfer effectively to earthquake event classification, magnitude regression, and phase detection. In tectonic-versus-non-tectonic event classification, ConProSeis achieves an accuracy of 99.03%. Additional experiments on the Pacific Northwest dataset further demonstrate cross-regional transferability. Overall, the results suggest that physics-aware self-supervised pretraining can reduce label dependence and improve the robustness and transferability of seismic representation learning.

verified_metadata.title: A hybrid transformer-based multi-task framework for rapid seismic response prediction of reinforced concrete chimneys
verified_metadata.abstract: Reinforced concrete (RC) chimneys represent critical industrial infrastructure with significant seismic vulnerability due to their slender and high-rise geometry. Conventional nonlinear numerical simulations, while accurate, are computationally expensive and unsuitable for real-time response prediction and large-scale parametric investigations. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a Deep Learning (DL) framework for fast and accurate prediction of dynamic seismic responses. A dataset of over 40,000 high-fidelity Nonlinear Time History Analyses (NLTHAs) was generated using OpenSees, incorporating diverse geometric configurations, and material nonlinearities subjected to real Ground Motion Acceleration (GMA) records scaled across multiple intensities. A hybrid Transformer-based architecture is proposed, utilizing a multi-task learning configuration with a shared encoder backbone, a transfer learning strategy and an adaptive sequence compression module. This design allows the model to simultaneously predict dominant modal frequencies and full dynamic response time histories, while effectively managing long-range temporal dependencies. The model demonstrates exceptional predictive accuracy on unseen test data, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients (R) exceeding 0.99 for modal frequencies and 0.98 for dynamic response time histories. It demonstrates promising generalization capability for previously unseen geometries and seismic waveforms, maintaining high fidelity in capturing peak responses, and phase alignment. The architecture reduces computational cost from several minutes per simulation to milliseconds per prediction. This efficiency enables near-instantaneous predictions, providing a practical tool for performance-based design and potential future integration into real-time structural health monitoring of critical industrial infrastructure.

title: Machine learning–integrated spatial decision framework for sustainable offshore wind and marine spatial planning: A Black Sea case study
abstract: A newly developed integrated Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP), Entropy Weight Method (EWM), Machine Learning (ML), and Half-Quadratic Programming (HQ Programming) framework within a Geographic Information System (GIS) environment was designed for offshore wind farm (OWF) site selection. This hybrid methodology was applied to the Samsun–Ordu–Giresun continental shelf along the southern Black Sea to identify technically feasible, environmentally compatible, and policy-relevant offshore wind development zones. The scientific problem addressed in this work is the limited ability of conventional GIS–multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches to reconcile uncertain expert judgments, objective spatial variability, and data-driven criterion relevance within a single transparent weighting structure. FAHP represented expert judgments under uncertainty, while EWM provided objective entropy-based weights derived from geospatial variability. Five supervised ML algorithms—Decision Tree, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Ridge Classifier, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machines (SVM)—were implemented using Annual Energy Production (AEP) as the target variable to quantify the empirical importance of spatial criteria. HQ Programming merged FAHP, EWM, and ML-based weights into a unified balance between subjective and objective assessments. Wind resource parameters contributed ∼18% to total suitability, infrastructural factors 16%, oceanographic–geophysical conditions 28%, and environmental–navigational constraints 30%. GIS-based analysis identified the Atakum–Ünye–Gülyalı corridor as the most favorable development zone. The framework helps decision-makers prioritize offshore wind investment areas, reduce conflicts with navigation and protected zones, and support grid- and port-oriented marine spatial planning. verified_metadata.title: Machine learning–integrated spatial decision framework for sustainable offshore wind and marine spatial planning: A Black Sea case study
verified_metadata.abstract: A newly developed integrated Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP), Entropy Weight Method (EWM), Machine Learning (ML), and Half-Quadratic Programming (HQ Programming) framework within a Geographic Information System (GIS) environment was designed for offshore wind farm (OWF) site selection. This hybrid methodology was applied to the Samsun–Ordu–Giresun continental shelf along the southern Black Sea to identify technically feasible, environmentally compatible, and policy-relevant offshore wind development zones. The scientific problem addressed in this work is the limited ability of conventional GIS–multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches to reconcile uncertain expert judgments, objective spatial variability, and data-driven criterion relevance within a single transparent weighting structure. FAHP represented expert judgments under uncertainty, while EWM provided objective entropy-based weights derived from geospatial variability. Five supervised ML algorithms—Decision Tree, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Ridge Classifier, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machines (SVM)—were implemented using Annual Energy Production (AEP) as the target variable to quantify the empirical importance of spatial criteria. HQ Programming merged FAHP, EWM, and ML-based weights into a unified balance between subjective and objective assessments. Wind resource parameters contributed ∼18% to total suitability, infrastructural factors 16%, oceanographic–geophysical conditions 28%, and environmental–navigational constraints 30%. GIS-based analysis identified the Atakum–Ünye–Gülyalı corridor as the most favorable development zone. The framework helps decision-makers prioritize offshore wind investment areas, reduce conflicts with navigation and protected zones, and support grid- and port-oriented marine spatial planning. This study provides a transferable basis for explainable, data-calibrated spatial decision-making in offshore renewable energy planning.

verified_metadata.title: State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries based on probabilistic diffusion models and self-learning dynamic channel attention assisted extended long short-term memory
verified_metadata.abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation is critical for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of lithium-ion batteries. However, limited data and insufficient temporal–spatial feature representation often restrict model performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel SOH estimation method that integrates data augmentation, temporal modeling, and feature attention mechanisms. First, a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is employed to generate multidimensional temporal health features of batteries, which can improve both the quantity and diversity of training data. Subsequently, a self-learning dynamic channel attention (SDCA) mechanism is designed to adaptively model the correlations among cross-channel features via dynamic convolution kernels, enabling the model to focus on more informative features during prediction. Finally, an SOH estimation framework named SDCA-assisted extended long short-term memory network (SDCA-xLSTM) is developed, which adopts the extended long short-term memory (xLSTM) to better capture long-term dependencies in sequential data. Experiments on two battery datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior SOH estimation performance, outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines.

verified_metadata.title: A collaborative graph–transformer network for spatial transcriptomics data clustering with semantic graph induction
verified_metadata.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the simultaneous capture of gene expression profiles and spatial localization, offering critical insights that facilitate the deciphering of tissue architecture and cell–cell interactions. To fully exploit spatial transcriptomic data, effective modeling of spatial relationships is essential. However, current methods exhibit limitations when constructing graph structures. Traditional static topological relationships built on spatial proximity struggle to delineate cell-layer boundaries and fail to adequately identify the cross-regional distribution patterns of cells within the same layer. Meanwhile, those based on raw gene expression similarity are susceptible to noise and cellular heterogeneity, making it difficult to capture the underlying semantic relationships. To address these challenges, we propose GTFST, a graph–Transformer network for spatial transcriptomics clustering. GTFST employs a dual-branch architecture with designed Reciprocal Contrastive Alignment (RCA) strategy to comprehensively model both local microenvironmental interactions and global contextual semantics. Notably, we introduce a Semantic Graph Induction (SGI) module that automatically learns and induces graph topology from gene semantic relationships. This design overcomes the limitations of fixed-neighborhood approaches, enabling more insightful modeling of complex biological interactions. Extensive experiments on spatial transcriptomic datasets demonstrate the superiority of GTFST over state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain clustering. Its enhanced precision provides a robust foundation for subsequent biological analyses such as differentially expressed gene identification, functional enrichment, and cell–cell interaction inference.

verified_metadata.title: A Faster region convolutional neural network and recurrent neural network based approach of Parkinson’s disease diagnosis by analyzing gait
verified_metadata.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that significantly affects human motor functions, particularly gait patterns. Early and accurate diagnosis of PD is essential for timely clinical intervention. However, manual diagnosis based on visual observation of gait can be time-consuming and error-prone. To achieve faster and more accurate diagnosis, this article presents a combination of Faster region-convolutional neural network (R-CNN) and convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) based artificial intelligence (AI) system to diagnose PD by analyzing the human gait from the videos. In the proposed framework, Faster R-CNN with a residual network 50 (ResNet50) backbone has been used to detect and extract the human subject from each video frame, enabling robust person localization under varying backgrounds and lighting conditions. Subsequently, spatial gait features have been extracted from the detected human using convolutional layers. The extracted frame-level features have been aggregated to form a sequence representing the entire video. These sequential features have been provided to a bidirectional long short-term memory (BLSTM) network to model temporal dependencies across frames and predict the final class label of the video. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves classification accuracies of 91.85%, 99.30%, 99.70%, and 97.82% on four popular publicly available datasets knee osteoarthritis-Parkinson’s disease-normal (KOA-PD-NM), gait-Instituto Superior Tecnico (IST), gait-Instituto de Telecomunicacoes (IT), and multimodal video dataset respectively, outperforming several state-of-the-art gait-based PD diagnosis methods. These results indicate that integrating robust human detection with spatio-temporal deep learning improves PD diagnosis from gait videos and shows strong potential for real-world clinical screening.

verified_metadata.title: Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty-enhanced one-dimensional convolutional neural network for early cardiovascular disease risk prediction with limited pulse wave samples
verified_metadata.abstract: Early cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk assessment based on pulse wave analysis is challenged by data scarcity, severe class imbalance, and the difficulty of modeling continuous pathological progression with discrete classification schemes. To learn data distributions from limited samples and to generate high-fidelity synthetic pulse waves for data augmentation, this study proposes a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) enhanced one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) framework for pulse-wave-based CVD risk grading. Subjects are stratified into four clinically meaningful stages—healthy controls, risk exposure, sub-clinical damage, and confirmed lesion—based on vascular functional and structural indicators, enabling a physiologically interpretable pathological continuum. The proposed framework demonstrates strong classification performance under extreme class imbalance. By augmenting limited real pulse-wave samples into a substantially larger training set, the framework achieved an overall accuracy of 92.28% and a recall of 85.33% for severe lesion cases, representing improvements of 8.54% and 24.00%, respectively, compared with the baseline model trained on the original unaugmented dataset. Moreover, the framework may also be beneficial in scenarios with relatively sufficient data, where generative augmentation can further enrich feature variation and potentially improve classification performance. These results indicate that the proposed method provides a robust and generalizable engineering solution for early CVD risk screening.

title: State-of-the-art artificial intelligence and hybrid model approaches for sediment load prediction in dynamic watersheds
abstract: Predicting sediment production is a complex, nonlinear, and dynamic process influenced by watershed geomorphology and spatiotemporal variability in hydrological drivers. Conventional modeling approaches often face limitations in accurately representing these processes, which has encouraged the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning techniques. This review presents a comprehensive overview of AI-based methods applied to sediment load and concentration prediction in studies published between 2000 and 2025. The reviewed approaches include artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic–based models, support vector machines, tree-based algorithms, deep learning architectures, and evolutionary optimization techniques. The paper summarizes commonly used model structures, input variables, temporal scales, and training algorithms reported in the literature, and highlights the role of hybrid modeling frameworks in enhancing predictive performance. Particular attention is given to studies addressing sediment load prediction under flood conditions, where rapid and accurate estimation is essential. In addition, the review discusses how historical hydrological data have been utilized to improve model reliability. Finally, the paper outlines current challenges and presents general recommendations to support future research and applications of AI-based sediment load prediction models.

verified_metadata.title: Volatility-aware adaptive hybrid deep learning for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate short-term forecasting of photovoltaic power generation is a critical enabler for reliable microgrid operation. However, forecasting accuracy is frequently hindered by data non-stationarity, regime-dependent variability, and the presence of non-physical records within operational datasets. To address these challenges, this study develops a volatility-aware gating, adaptive hybrid forecasting framework using two years of hourly measurements collected from the Datan Power Plant. A physics-informed data validation procedure is applied to improve data quality by excluding nighttime samples according to the solar zenith angle. The proposed architecture employs a shared convolutional neural network-bidirectional long short-term memory backbone for temporal feature extraction and integrates a dual-branch architecture designed to capture both stable and volatile regimes. These branches are interconnected through a sigmoid-based gating mechanism that adaptively blends a dense-fusion stable branch with an attention-enhanced volatile branch in response to input variability. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms the naive baseline, achieving reductions in mean absolute error, weighted mean relative error, root mean square error, and mean absolute percentage error by 18.27%, 20.84%, 23.83%, and 23.86%, respectively. These findings underscore the robustness of the adaptive hybrid model in handling volatile photovoltaic generation patterns and emphasize its potential to improve forecasting reliability in microgrid systems incorporating renewable energy sources.

verified_metadata.title: A unified parameterized-hard-constrained physics-informed neural network framework for rapid temperature prediction of thin-walled targets across weather conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: Predicting the transient temperature field of three-dimensional (3D) targets under rapidly changing weather remains challenging due to the prohibitive cost of traditional solvers, the training instability of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and the poor generalization of data-driven methods. This paper addresses all three challenges through a unified Parameterized-Hard-Constrained PINN (P-HC-PINN) framework with three key innovations. First, a hard-constrained PINN (HC-PINN) enforces initial conditions exactly, yielding stable training and partial differential equation (PDE) loss of 2.9e-5, three orders of magnitude lower than a soft-constrained baseline. Second, extending this to a Parameterized HC-PINN (P-HC-PINN) that accepts meteorological parameters as inputs enables prediction for new conditions 200 times faster than retraining the HC-PINN. Third, the physics of rain is integrated into the loss function, reducing the rain-period prediction error by 64%. Validated on experimental and simulated data, the framework predicts full-day 3D temperature fields of thin-walled targets with a mean error below 2 K and inference speeds 100 times faster than finite-volume simulations, providing a fast, physics-aware, and generalizable surrogate for thermal analysis.

verified_metadata.title: Leakage localization method for pipeline based on physics-informed neural networks
verified_metadata.abstract: Pipeline transportation is essential for high-pressure gas delivery, but leaks cause significant economic and environmental damage. Traditional localization methods, which rely on external monitoring or dense sensor networks, are limited in harsh marine environments. This study proposes a pipeline leakage localization framework using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), which reconstructs internal flow fields from sparse sensor data and extracts physically interpretable indicators for detection. Three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to generate leakage flow-field data under various conditions (0.5–2 MPa pressure, different leak locations and angles, and single/dual leakage scenarios). So the optimal sensor configuration was identified as five monitoring planes with four sensors on each plane. The PINN embeds Navier-Stokes and continuity equations into the loss function, reconstructing the entire flow field using only 20 sensors. Leakage localization is achieved by analyzing axial velocity profiles and applying a threshold indicator. For single-leakage cases, the average localization error is approximately 7.5% over all tested conditions, with larger errors in some high-pressure cases with large polar-angle offsets. For dual-leakage cases, the errors are mainly within 2%–13%. This approach enables high-precision leakage localization with low sensor density, offering a feasible solution for intelligent pipeline monitoring in complex environments.

verified_metadata.title: Enhancing groundwater forecasting through a spatio-temporal feature mixer deep learning model
verified_metadata.abstract: Groundwater is a critical freshwater resource worldwide, yet its sustainability is increasingly threatened by over-extraction and climate variability. Accordingly, reliable and computationally efficient forecasting of groundwater is essential for supporting adaptive aquifer management. In this regard, this study develops a Spatio-Temporal Feature Mixer (STFMixer) deep learning model to forecast groundwater hydraulic heads three months ahead in the Choushui River Alluvial Fan, a region strongly influenced by agricultural pumping and climatic variability in Central Taiwan. The STFMixer model integrates convolutional spatio-temporal encoding with temporal and feature mixing layers to jointly learn spatial, temporal, and inter-feature dependencies of groundwater changes based on historical five-month inputs, including hydraulic heads from groundwater monitoring wells interpolated to spatial grids, gridded precipitation and temperature, and spatially aggregated pumping electricity consumption. Predictive performance is benchmarked against four established deep learning architectures: Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM), Time-Series Mixer (TSMixer), Transformer, and Convolutional Neural Network-Backpropagation Neural Network (CNN-BPNN) models under identical calibration conditions (2007-2017 training; 2018-2021 testing). Results showed that STFMixer achieved the highest average Index of Agreement (IOA >0.79) and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE <1.5 m) among the evaluated models, while maintaining stable error growth in three-month-ahead forecasting at a spatially heterogeneous aquifer. Ablation analysis further indicated that pumping input contributes most strongly to predictive performance, followed by precipitation and temperature which is typically observed for agriculturally active regions. With approximately 224 thousand trainable parameters which is significantly lower than most benchmark models, the proposed STFMixer model provides a computationally efficient framework for short-term multi-step groundwater forecasting and aquifer management.

verified_metadata.abstract: To address the computational bottleneck of deep learning, a key artificial intelligence (AI) technology, in resource-constrained Battery Management Systems (BMS), this paper presents a lightweight, linear-complexity State of Health (SOH) estimation framework. First, a systematic feature selection process identifies robust health indicators from partial voltage–time integrals, effectively reducing online extraction burdens. Subsequently, we propose SL-AgentNet (integrating Small-kernel and Large-kernel convolutions), an AI architecture designed to resolve the quadratic overhead of traditional Transformers. By integrating the Fast Local–Global Fusion Attention (FLFA) mechanism with diversity-enhancing modules, specifically the Fast Diversity Feature Fusion Attention (FDFA) and Parallel Informed Activation Function (PIAF), this AI model achieves linear complexity while capturing long-range degradation dependencies. Experiments on the Oxford, National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), and Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) datasets demonstrate superior robustness, reducing the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 74.78% on the Oxford dataset against Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer baselines. With a model size of only 40.92 Kilobytes (KB), the AI framework proves its feasibility through hardware-in-the-loop validation on a Texas Instruments (TI) Cortex-M4 microcontroller, where a Look-Up Table (LUT) implementation maintains accuracy loss within 0.3%, demonstrating its readiness for embedded deployment.

title: Physics-informed neural network for patient-specific left ventricular finite element modelling with image motion consistency
abstract: Elucidating the biomechanical behaviour of the myocardium is important for understanding cardiac physiology. This cannot be directly inferred from clinical imaging, but requires finite element (FE) simulations. However, conventional FE simulations are computationally expensive and often do not accurately reproduce clinically observed cardiac motions. Here, we propose the IMC-PINN-FE, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework that integrates imaged motion consistency (IMC) with FE modelling for patient-specific simulations of left ventricular (LV) biomechanics. Cardiac motion is first estimated from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or echocardiography using either a pre-trained attention-based network or an unsupervised cyclic-regularised network, followed by extraction of motion modes. IMC-PINN-FE then estimates myocardial stiffness and active tension by fitting clinical pressure measurements within seconds. Based on these parameters, IMC-PINN-FE performs FE modelling throughout the cardiac cycle and achieves an overall ∼ 75-fold speed-up over conventional FE simulations. Through motion constraints, its outputs of cardiac displacements across the cardiac cycle match imaged motions much more accurately, improving Dice coefficient from 0.849 to 0.927 compared to conventional FE methods. Concurrently, it preserves a realistic pressure–volume (P–V) relationship that is very similar to that of conventional FE. IMC-PINN-FE improves on existing PINN-FE models by enabling back-computation of myocardial properties and achieving better imaged motion fidelity. This strategy of using cardiac motions of a single individual to reconstruct shape modes avoids the need for a large dataset, and enables better patient-specificity. IMC-PINN-FE thus presents a robust approach for rapid, patient-specific, and image-consistent cardiac biomechanical modelling.

title: Model-based predictive digital twin for bridge structural health monitoring: the integration of building information modeling, finite element analysis, and machine learning in a Netherlands case study
abstract: Advancements in bridge health monitoring systems are a trending issue for many researchers and industry professionals these days, where the bridge community is looking for Artificial Intelligence (AI) based automated solutions. To address this challenge, this study integrates Building Information Modeling (BIM), Finite Element Method (FEM), and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to create a comprehensive Digital Twin (DT) framework capable of real-time monitoring and predictive analysis of the bridge's structural integrity. A robust design of the workflows and technical framework is proposed to enable seamless interaction between the physical bridge assets and the proposed model-based Predictive Digital Twin (PDT) system using virtual designs and Neural Network (NN) prediction algorithms. The major research contributions of this article include model-based Bridge Structural Health Monitoring (BSHM) using accurate predictions from ML and sensor data and the novel PDT-based approach. It proposes information flows through an integrated BIM, ML, and DT platform to ensure improved BSHM. The proposed ML-based PDT framework is validated using a steel girder bridge located in the Netherlands, which demonstrates automated health monitoring of the bridge. The PDT system is validated using actual BSHM data (strain data), with predictions from the ML model compared against known load cases. The outcomes of this research showcase the PDT framework's ability to predict load placement and magnitude with precision, contributing to the ongoing advancement of suitable infrastructure management practices.

verified_metadata.title: An efficient hybrid network based on convolution and transformer for object detection in underground drilling sites
verified_metadata.abstract: Intelligent monitoring at underground drilling sites underpins mine automation, where rapid and accurate object detection is essential for both production efficiency and safety. However, drilling-site imagery is shaped by multiple factors, including non-uniform illumination, cluttered equipment, and frequent viewpoint changes, resulting in large appearance and scale variations that are difficult to handle with standard detectors. To address these challenges, we propose an Efficient Hybrid Detection Network (EHD-Net) for high-accuracy detector for drilling-site surveillance. Specifically, our backbone adopts the Large–Small Kernel Block (LSKB) to expand the receptive field while preserving local details. We introduce a Shallow–Deep Interaction Attention (SDIA) to couple shallow-detail features with deeper semantic representations. For scale variation, we design an efficient Multi-Scale Fusion Block (MSFB) with lateral residual connections between parallel branches. In addition, a Channel-Spatial Gated Unit (CSGU) is applied along the backbone–neck pathway to suppress irrelevant activations. We further collect a dataset of 17,358 real-world drilling-site images from four coal mines in Henan Province. On the proposed drilling-site dataset, EHD-Net achieves 92.1% mean average precision (mAP) at an inference speed of 123 frames per second (FPS). The corresponding precision and recall are 94.4% and 88.5%, respectively. It also generalizes well to public coal mine benchmarks, including safety helmet and conveyor belt datasets, demonstrating strong cross scenario performance in underground environments.

title: Coupling Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics with multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for cooperative control of point absorbers
abstract: Wave Energy Converters, particularly point absorbers, have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for harvesting ocean wave energy. Nevertheless, achieving high conversion efficiency remains challenging due to the inherently complex and nonlinear interactions between incident waves and device motion dynamics. This study develops an optimal adaptive damping control model for the power take-off (PTO) system by coupling Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. The proposed framework enables real-time communication between high-fidelity SPH simulations and intelligent control agents that learn coordinated policies to maximise energy capture. In each training episode, the SPH-based environment provides instantaneous hydrodynamic states to the agents, which output continuous damping actions and receive rewards reflecting power absorption. The Multi-Agent Soft Actor Critic algorithm is employed within a centralised-training and decentralised-execution scheme to ensure stable learning in continuous, multi-body systems. The entire platform is implemented in a unified GPU-accelerated C++ environment, allowing long-horizon training and large-scale three-dimensional simulations. The approach is validated through a series of two-dimensional and three-dimensional benchmark cases under regular and irregular wave conditions. Compared with constant PTO damping, the learned control policy increases overall energy capture by 23.8% and 21.5%, respectively, demonstrating the strong potential of intelligent control for improving the performance of wave energy converter arrays. The developed three-dimensional GPU-accelerated multi-agent platform in computational hydrodynamics, is extendable to other fluid-structure interaction engineering problem that require real-time, multi-body coordinated control.

title: SHIELD: Advanced persistent threats detection and intelligent explanation using large language models
abstract: Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are sophisticated cyber attacks that can remain undetected for extended periods, making their mitigation particularly challenging. Given their persistence, significant effort is required to detect them and respond effectively. Existing provenance-based attack detection methods often lack interpretability and suffer from high false positive rates, while investigation approaches are either supervised or limited to known attacks. To address these challenges of threat detection and investigation, we introduce SHIELD, a novel approach that combines statistical anomaly detection and graph-based analysis with the contextual analysis capabilities of large language models (LLMs). SHIELD leverages the implicit knowledge of LLMs to uncover hidden attack patterns in provenance data, while reducing false positives and providing clear, interpretable attack descriptions. This reduces analysts’ alert fatigue and makes it easier for them to understand the threat landscape. Our extensive evaluation demonstrates SHIELD’s effectiveness and computational efficiency in real-world scenarios. SHIELD was shown to outperform state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher precision and recall. SHIELD’s integration of anomaly detection, LLM-driven contextual analysis, and advanced graph-based correlation establishes a new benchmark for APT detection.

verified_metadata.title: A unified image-driven physics-informed learning framework for mechanical field reconstruction and material identification
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate characterization of mechanical fields under load is essential for material assessment and engineering design. Although Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving inverse problems, they typically rely on noisy, pre-processed Digital Image Correlation (DIC) data, which can lead to significant error propagation. This paper proposes an image-driven physics-informed neural network (I-PINN), a unified framework that fundamentally overcomes this limitation by integrating full-field image data into the learning process. Instead of relying on discrete DIC-derived points, the method introduces a dense observational constraint based on brightness constancy at the original signal level. Combined with equilibrium residuals, boundary conditions, and a global energy balance, the I-PINN framework enables solving the forward and inverse problems simultaneously without intermediate error propagation steps. Furthermore, a two-stage training strategy is implemented to ensure convergence by learning data-consistent kinematics prior to enforcing physical constraints. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework yields physically consistent and accurate displacement, strain, and stress fields and reliably identifies material parameters, even with poor initial guesses. The approach outperforms traditional DIC-based analysis and delivers comparable accuracy to finite element analysis. Ablation studies further confirm the essential roles of the dense image-based constraint and the adopted training strategy for robust convergence. Noise robustness experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains stable reconstruction accuracy and reliable parameter identification even under significant image noise. Overall, the proposed methodology establishes a noise-resistant framework that directly bridges experimental observations and mechanical field inference, offering an effective solution for mechanical field reconstruction and material identification.

verified_metadata.title: Hybrid deep learning models for projecting cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms under climate change scenarios
verified_metadata.abstract: Cyanobacteria Harmful Algal Blooms (CyanoHABs) in inland water reservoirs pose ecological and public health risks. Unlike previous studies that primarily focused on past bloom detection, this research introduces a novel framework that predicts future CyanoHAB coverage under climate change scenarios using meteorological variables. Specifically, satellite remote sensing is integrated with hybrid machine learning and deep learning models to detect and project CyanoHAB coverage in Oman's largest reservoir, the Wadi Dayqah Dam. Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) and Landsat satellite images (2010–2023) were utilized to estimate bloom area sizes via the Floating Algae Index (FAI), achieving strong validation. We evaluated four models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest combined with LSTM (RF + LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting combined with LSTM (XGBoost + LSTM), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine combined with LSTM (LGBoost + LSTM). The best performing model was RF + LSTM. Temperature was identified through sensitivity analysis as the most significant bloom driver. Projections using downscaled Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) data revealed opposite trends: in Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 126 (SSP126), bloom coverage decreased by the late century, particularly in spring (March averages <0.1 square kilometers); Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 245 (SSP245) stayed near historical levels; while Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 585 (SSP585) increased bloom coverage, with summer maxima >0.7 square kilometers. Hybrid modeling effectively predicts CyanoHABs, with temperature as the main driver, and climate mitigation can help reduce associated risks. The findings support adaptive water management and bloom preparedness, noting that larger bloom coverage generally signals higher ecological and public health concerns.

title: Noninvasive pressure difference mapping by integrating ultrasonic vector flow imaging and physics-informed conditional variational learning
abstract: Pressure differences across the circulatory system provide valuable insights into many cardiovascular diseases, including arterial stenosis. Catheterization is used clinically to measure intravascular pressure, but it is invasive, costly, and carries risks. As a noninvasive alternative, physics-informed deep learning combined with measured flow data can estimate intravascular pressure by embedding physical laws, such as the Navier–Stokes equations, into the learning process. However, this approach is still vulnerable to data noise, which can disrupt the balance between data fidelity and physical consistency, leading to unstable predictions. This study proposes a physics-informed conditional variational learning method that integrates ultrasonic vector flow data, probabilistic latent representation, and computational fluid dynamics principles for robust pressure difference estimation. The method is validated using both in-vitro and in-vivo experiments with high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging. For in-vitro experiments, compared to the conventional fully-connected network approach, the proposed method demonstrates improved accuracy, leading to a root mean square error reduction from 23.5 pascals to 13.1 pascals (a 9.3% reduction relative to the peak pressure difference), and demonstrates robustness in the presence of dark regions and across various network sizes, while the conventional fully-connected network method fails under certain conditions. In in-vivo experiments, the proposed method provides stable predictions across different training data volumes, with a peak pressure difference discrepancy of 1.8 pascals, compared to 12.1 pascals for the conventional fully-connected network method. This work demonstrates advances in deep learning strategies for robust pressure difference estimation using practical flow imaging measurements, particularly when incorporating noisy, sparse, or missing data.

title: Physics-informed sparse identification-based tube model predictive control for aerial vehicles
abstract: Autonomous aerial vehicles necessitate control strategies that balance computational efficiency with robust performance in dynamic operational environments. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) framework for aerial platforms that leverages physics-informed machine learning (PIML) to achieve an optimal balance between computational tractability and robust performance. At the core of the proposed approach lies a sparse, control-affine model identified via the PIML method, which provides a parsimonious yet interpretable representation of the system dynamics by embedding first-principles knowledge and learning residual uncertainties from operational data. This model is incorporated within a robust MPC scheme that adopts a high-order Runge-Kutta discretization to ensure prediction accuracy and an adaptive tube-based mechanism to guarantee constraint satisfaction under uncertainty. The online adaptation of the tube, directly informed by the residual error of the PIML model, ensures robust stability without introducing excessive conservatism. Rigorous theoretical proofs are provided to establish recursive feasibility and stability. Numerical simulations and experiments on a quadrotor demonstrate that our method significantly reduces computational load compared to nonlinear MPC and robust MPC using a first-principles high-fidelity model, while outperforming PID, nonlinear MPC, neural-network-based MPC, and fixed-tube robust MPC in tracking performance and robustness, showcasing the practical efficiency of the proposed PIML-based control synthesis for resource-constrained aerial systems.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed sparse identification-based tube model predictive control for aerial vehicles
verified_metadata.abstract: Autonomous aerial vehicles necessitate control strategies that balance computational efficiency with robust performance in dynamic operational environments. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) framework for aerial platforms that leverages physics-informed machine learning (PIML) to achieve an optimal balance between computational tractability and robust performance. At the core of the proposed approach lies a sparse, control-affine model identified via the PIML method, which provides a parsimonious yet interpretable representation of the system dynamics by embedding first-principles knowledge and learning residual uncertainties from operational data. This model is incorporated within a robust MPC scheme that adopts a high-order Runge-Kutta discretization to ensure prediction accuracy and an adaptive tube-based mechanism to guarantee constraint satisfaction under uncertainty. The online adaptation of the tube, directly informed by the residual error of the PIML model, ensures robust stability without introducing excessive conservatism. Rigorous theoretical proofs are provided to establish recursive feasibility and stability. Numerical simulations and experiments on a quadrotor demonstrate that our method significantly reduces computational load compared to nonlinear MPC and robust MPC using a first-principles high-fidelity model, while outperforming PID, nonlinear MPC, neural-network-based MPC, and fixed-tube robust MPC in tracking performance and robustness, showcasing the practical efficiency of the proposed PIML-based control synthesis for resource-constrained aerial systems.

verified_metadata.title: A novel decomposition-based deep stacked residual convolutional recurrent neural network for ultra-short-term wind speed and wind power forecasting
verified_metadata.abstract: Decomposition methods, such as complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN), effectively address the non-stationary and intermittent nature of time series in wind power and wind speed forecasting, enhancing prediction accuracy. However, the residual noise in the subsequences generated by these decomposition methods can degrade predictive performance. Furthermore, most existing predictive models rarely address the reduction of redundant nonlinear operations in the neuron activation functions within the regression subnetwork, which can lead to high computational costs and diminished prediction accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel decomposition-based deep stacked residual convolutional recurrent neural network (DB-DSRC-RNN) for wind speed and wind power forecasting. DB-DSRC-RNN first uses CEEMDAN to decompose non-stationary wind speed or power data into stable subsequences. Then, a deep stacked residual convolutional recurrent neural network (DSRC-RNN) learns the underlying spatio-temporal features in each subsequence. In DSRC-RNN, a residual convolution threshold denoising block is designed to mitigate the impact of residual noise in the subsequences of CEEMDAN for the first time, while extracting spatial features. A bidirectional long short-term memory is also integrated into DSRC-RNN to capture temporal features. Additionally, a regression subnetwork with a dense dendrite module is designed to further enhance the model’s performance by reducing the computational complexity associated with nonlinear activation functions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed DB-DSRC-RNN outperforms eight benchmark models in terms of predictive accuracy, generalization ability, and robustness for ultra-short-term wind power and wind speed forecasting in energy systems.

verified_metadata.title: Unified seismic capacity prediction for reinforced concrete columns via an interpretable two-stage machine learning approach: From failure mode classification to an explicit equation
verified_metadata.abstract: Traditional empirical formulas suffer from insufficient accuracy and limited applicability in predicting the seismic performance of reinforced concrete (RC) columns, while high-precision machine learning (ML) models are often inapplicable in engineering practice due to their “black-box” nature. These issues constitute two core challenges in the field of seismic assessment for reinforced concrete columns. To address these challenges, this study proposes an integrated method combining two-stage machine learning prediction, interpretable analysis, and explicit formula derivation, aiming to simultaneously enhance prediction accuracy, improve model transparency, and derive an explicit formula for practical engineering use. The study achieves this by proposing a novel “classify-then-regress” strategy which first predicts the failure mode and then uses the predicted failure-mode information to condition the Categorical feature boosting (CatBoost)-based shear capacity prediction. The resulting two-stage model achieves high predictive accuracy while providing an explicit failure-mode-conditioned pathway for engineering interpretation and safety-oriented assessment. To tackle the “black-box” issue, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantifies the non-linear effects of key parameters and reveals the model's physical logic, leading to an explicit formula with clear physical meaning. While slightly less accurate than the full machine learning model, this formula significantly surpasses traditional formulas and compensates for the lack of interpretability in data-driven methods. Finally, a graphical user interface (GUI) is developed to integrate the system, providing engineers with an efficient and intuitive tool for practical seismic assessment.

verified_metadata.title: Jamming-resilient unmanned aerial vehicle reconnaissance strategy using hybrid ordinary differential equation and deep reinforcement learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Reconnaissance Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) operating in complex adversarial electromagnetic environments are highly vulnerable to dynamic jamming. To address this challenge, we formulate the UAV’s jamming-resilient maneuvering problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), integrating flight dynamics with physical-layer receiver performance. However, solving this POMDP requires accurately estimating the underlying continuous and time-varying jamming dynamics from only discrete, noisy observations. Standard recurrent networks often fall short because they fail to explicitly model the physical process governing jamming evolution. Our key insight is that jamming dynamics, despite being observed discretely, evolve continuously over time. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel physical perception encoder that integrates Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) with Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) solvers. The GRU efficiently extracts latent features from historical observation sequences, while the ODE solver serves as a continuous-time dynamics engine, interpolating and extrapolating these latent states to simulate jammer behavior between and beyond observation points. This GRU-ODE encoder is embedded within a Discrete Soft Actor-Critic (DSAC) framework, forming an end-to-end intelligent decision-maker. The resulting algorithm, DSAC-ODE, synergistically optimizes both low-power reconnaissance modes—achieved through sampling bit truncation and beam sparse control—and adaptive flight maneuvers to balance mission success against energy consumption. Extensive evaluations demonstrate its superior performance: a 97% mission success rate, an average decision delay of just 47 ms, and a 9.25% reduction in energy consumption, outperforming several strong baselines.

title: Physics-integrated machine-learning framework for predicting torsional strength and response behavior of reinforced concrete beams
abstract: Predicting torsional cracking and failure in reinforced concrete beams remains challenging because of the complex interactions among material properties, geometry, and reinforcement mechanisms. This study proposes a hybrid physics–machine-learning framework that integrates physics-guided neural networks, graph neural networks, and a Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble to achieve accurate and interpretable torsional strength prediction. A database comprising 300 experimental tests and 500 physics-informed synthetic samples is used for model development and validation. The proposed graph neural network achieves the highest standalone performance (coefficient of determination (R 2 ) = 0.92, root mean squared error (RMSE) = 25 kN-meter (kN·m)), outperforming previously reported machine-learning models and conventional design codes. The Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble further improves predictive robustness, achieving a test RMSE of approximately 33 kN m. In comparison, the models reported by Yu et al. (2022), including boosted tree ensembles, support vector machines, and two-dimensional convolutional neural networks, yielded mean absolute errors of 119%, 198%, and 184%, respectively. Conventional design codes, including American Concrete Institute 318-25, Canadian Standards Association A23.3-14, and Eurocode 2, exhibit substantially lower predictive accuracies (R 2 = 0.55–0.65). Beyond prediction, the framework generates physically consistent failure boundaries across reinforcement domains. Shapley additive explanations analysis confirms interpretability by identifying longitudinal and transverse reinforcement indices as dominant parameters. A graphical user interface is developed for practical engineering application. The dataset and implementation code are publicly available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20322665 . Overall, the proposed framework provides an accurate, interpretable, and deployable artificial intelligence tool for structural assessment and torsional design support.

verified_metadata.title: Simultaneous co-estimation of impedance spectra, state of charge, and state of health for lithium-ion batteries via multi-task deep learning using short-term pulses
verified_metadata.abstract: The accurate and concurrent estimation of a lithium-ion battery's electrochemical impedance spectrum (EIS), state of charge (SOC), and state of health (SOH) is critical for optimizing performance and ensuring safety, yet conventional methods are often impractical for real-time applications. This study proposes a novel deep learning framework capable of simultaneously predicting all three parameters using data from a single, short-term current pulse. Three advanced model architectures are designed and compared: a long short-term memory (LSTM) sequence-to-sequence model, an Attention-LSTM variant, and a multi-task learning (MTL) Transformer. The models are trained and validated on a comprehensive dataset from eight batteries under various temperatures, aging levels, and SOCs. Results demonstrate the MTL Transformer achieves superior overall performance, yielding the lowest test mean squared errors for SOC (0.1172%) and SOH (0.2221%). Concurrently, the Attention-LSTM model excels at high-fidelity EIS prediction with a minimal test error of 0.043 mΩ. With inference times under 17 ms, this work presents a hardware-agnostic, data-driven solution that enables comprehensive and real-time battery diagnostics, marking a significant advancement in battery management systems.

title: Constraint representation through support vector machines and its application to model predictive control
abstract: In this work we consider the control of dynamical systems subject to state and input constraints of arbitrary shape. In particular, we are interested in cases where some of the constraints are not described by a smooth function but are instead specified by a mix of functions and logical statements, a lookup table, or an oracle that returns whether a queried point is safe. We propose to use a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier to approximate the constraint boundaries with a smooth function and define a smooth nonconvex optimal control problem (OCP). We derive tightening bounds on the classifier to ensure safety of the system and investigate a class of kernels that lead to the OCP being a Difference-of-Convex (DC) programming problem. Moreover, we construct a natural difference of convex function decomposition for the Gaussian Radial Basis Function. The proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations including the control of a planar robotic manipulator with obstacle avoidance constraints.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-encoded unsupervised deep learning for lightweight structural health monitoring of short and medium-span bridge networks
verified_metadata.abstract: The surging structural failure of the Short- and Medium-Span (SMS) bridges underscores the need for structural safety monitoring and assessment. However, it is impossible to install the Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems comprehensively on all SMS bridges in the traffic networks due to budget limitations. To address this limitation, a lightweight SHM framework for the SMS bridge network is proposed based on a physics-encoded unsupervised deep learning architecture, where merely a single sensor is installed on each bridge. It integrates physics-based and data-driven modules to learn the nonlinear mapping relationships between the structural responses across different bridges. In the physics-based modules, the vehicle-induced quasi-static responses are extracted by using a Butterworth filter, and subsequently, they are used to identify the vehicular spatiotemporal information to construct the physics-informed temporal masks. In the data-driven modules, the physics-informed masks and geometric constraints are encoded into a multi-branch deep convolutional autoencoder. The measured responses of a source bridge are mapped to those of the target adjacent bridges, where the response reconstruction error is formulated as the loss function. Subsequently, the probability density pruning technique is adopted to collect the damage-sensitive indices from the loss values among different bridge pairs. These cross-bridge damage indices in a bridge network are integrated to identify the individual abnormal bridge. Numerical and laboratory experiments on simply supported beam bridges have been conducted under multi-vehicle dynamic loading, diverse sensor configurations, and multiple damage conditions. The damage index sensitivity is 151.3% with 10% stiffness reduction in 1/10 length of the beam.

verified_metadata.title: When transformers obey physics: A physics-guided transformer with symbolic regression for real time monitoring of flowing bottom-hole pressure
verified_metadata.abstract: Most machine learning models for predicting flowing bottomhole pressure (FBHP) are either black-box models, which offer high accuracy but lack interpretability, and white-box models, which provide transparency but often lack the flexibility or predictive power needed to capture nuances in the data. They are also predominantly data-driven, often ignoring physical laws, which can lead to accurate but physically inconsistent predictions. To bridge this gap, a physics-guided transformer model is proposed for FBHP in inclined production wells, addressing the trade-off between accuracy and interpretability. The model employs a dual-input architecture combining physical variables with sequential production data and enforces physical consistency via domain-informed loss functions. Trained and tested on 1329 samples from four production wells, the model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 38.31 psia (pounds per square inch absolute), root mean square error (RMSE) of 77.19 psia, and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.10%. To achieve interpretability, symbolic regression was used to derive a closed-form expression that captures physical trends which was validated via sensitivity analysis, yielding an MAE of 158.03 psia, RMSE of 233.37 psia, and MAPE of 3.83%. Uncertainty quantification was implemented using Monte Carlo Dropout, producing an average lower bound to upper bound (P10–P90) prediction spread of approximately 135 psia and a well-calibrated 95% prediction interval (miscalibration score = 0.030). Trend analysis showed that both the physics-guided transformer model and the symbolic regression equation captured trends consistent with physics. The framework delivers a high-performance, interpretable model that maintains physical plausibility in FBHP prediction.

verified_metadata.title: A lightweight machine learning method for real-time log anomaly detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Log anomaly detection is essential for system monitoring in cloud computing and microservice architectures. Current methodologies face substantial challenges including ambiguity in template extraction, domain-specific vocabulary difficulties, and outlier influence on feature selection. These issues impede practical implementation in resource-constrained environments requiring real-time detection, creating a technological gap that diminishes system reliability. This paper presents Optimized Principal Component Analysis (OPCA), a lightweight framework enabling efficient real-time anomaly detection through three innovations. First, an enhanced Drain-based log parsing module incorporates heuristic token splitting and optimized similarity calculations to improve template extraction accuracy while preserving semantic information. Second, Log-Specific Word Embedding (LSWE) integrates contrastive vocabularies with domain-specific semantic enhancement via offline pre-training and online out-of-vocabulary management, effectively capturing log semantics. Finally, a robust Principal Component Analysis (PCA) framework employs adaptive loss functions to mitigate outlier influence on principal component detection, enabling anomaly detection with minimal online training requirements, as the principal component estimation requires only a small set of normal log samples once the LSWE embeddings have been pre-trained offline. Experimental results demonstrate OPCA's strong performance, achieving F1-scores of 0.995 on Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) and 0.984 on BlueGene/L (BGL), while processing logs at 4750 samples per second on HDFS, up to 357-fold faster than graph-based methods, with F1-scores within 0.2 to 1.3 percentage points of the best-performing baseline on each dataset.

title: Bayesian multimodal fusion for seafloor habitat mapping with autonomous underwater vehicles
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles collect rich multimodal remote sensing data, but robust fusion and classification of heterogeneous sensor streams remains challenging due to noise and habitat variability. We propose a Bayesian multimodal neural network for fusing optical imagery, bathymetry, and side-scan sonar, quantifying epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty to improve classification reliability in complex underwater environments. Our model leverages uncertainty estimates to identify ambiguous predictions and highlight poorly sampled regions, enabling reliable mapping and evaluation of model confidence. We evaluated our model on large-scale Autonomous Underwater Vehicle survey data, achieving 85.5% classification accuracy, surpassing unimodal baselines by ∼ 7%. We provide a preliminary complexity analysis to estimate onboard feasibility, enabling rapid onboard processing for uncertainty-aware habitat classification. We vary the number of Monte Carlo runs to explore the balance between computational cost and uncertainty estimation. We further analyse how spatial context in side-scan and bathymetric imagery affects mapping accuracy, showing that a 30 metre patch size provides the best balance between habitat continuity and boundary delineation. This work demonstrates a scalable, uncertainty-aware multimodal fusion framework, enhancing the reliability and interpretability of underwater classification and mapping. We release the full codebase and trained models via an open-source software library (PyPI: multimodal-auv).
