verified_metadata.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Diffusion models in Drug Discovery: A Critical Review
verified_metadata.abstract: The drug discovery process is a deep multi-stage procedure in which generative artificial intelligence, specifically diffusion-based generative models, has been identified as having significant potential to address critical challenges in drug discovery, including de novo molecule design, structure-based ligand generation, and pharmacological property optimization. Unlike other popular generative models such as variational autoencoders (VAEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion models are found to possess more stable training behaviors and better ability to capture complex molecular distributions in both two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) chemical space. This review is a critical analysis of diffusion-based generative models in drug discovery. The analysis is based on a transparent literature search process. The literature search process includes articles published between 2017 and 2025 in peer-reviewed journals. The articles are obtained from Scopus, PubMed, and arXiv. In addition, we analyze the applications of diffusion models in different stages of drug discovery, such as molecule generation, protein-ligand docking, scaffold hopping, and conformation prediction. Moreover, we analyze the benchmarking of diffusion models on popular datasets such as Quantum Mechanics 9 (QM9), Geometric Ensemble of Molecules for drug discovery (GEOM-DRUG), CrossDocked2020 (a structure-based docking benchmark), Protein Data Bank binding data (PDBbind), and popular platforms such as Molecular Sets (MOSES) and GuacaMol. Unlike prior surveys, this review adopts an explicit literature selection protocol, provides per-model computational complexity analysis, and critically examines both benchmarking pitfalls and the emerging transition from denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) toward flow matching as a distinct generative paradigm. We demonstrate that existing metrics such as validity, novelty, and docking scores do not provide a complete understanding of chemical and biological relevance. In addition, we identify that synthetic feasibility constraints are not considered in existing studies, there is a lack of experimental validation, and evaluation protocols are not consistent. In addition, we discuss the existing limitations of explainable artificial intelligence in generative molecular modeling.

title: Optimal quantum reservoir computing for market forecasting: An application to fight food price crises
abstract: The emerging technology of Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) stands out in the noisy-intermediate scale quantum era for its efficiency, adaptability, and compatibility with current quantum hardware. By harnessing quantum dynamics for feature extraction, QRC offers a promising alternative for complex forecasting tasks — such as predicting agri-commodity price fluctuations — central to addressing food price crises and supply chain sustainability. In this work, we systematically investigate the design of quantum reservoirs and identify circuit complexity, quantified via the majorization criterion, as a practical indicator of forecasting performance. Unlike alternative complexity measures that require full state tomography or time-reversed dynamics, majorization can be evaluated from measurement statistics alone, making it particularly suited for near-term quantum devices. We demonstrate that quantum reservoirs built from a universal gate family composed of Hadamard, controlled-NOT, and T gates achieve strong predictive accuracy while requiring significantly fewer gates than the widely used transverse-field Ising model. Our results show that quantum reservoirs outperform deep learning and statistical baselines, and achieve comparable, slightly superior, performance to classical reservoir computing—an improvement consistent with the compact model structure of QRC, which, with significantly fewer trainable parameters, is better suited to prevent overfitting in data-scarce regimes. We further explore robustness under realistic noise conditions, showing that certain types of quantum noise, such as amplitude damping, can even enhance performance at low error rates. These findings suggest that QRC is a promising tool for time series prediction in data-limited, high-impact domains.

verified_metadata.title: Flux-conserved physics-informed neural networks for electromagnetic scattering computation
verified_metadata.abstract: Electromagnetic field modeling is important for remote sensing and target detection, but accurate solutions remain challenging in the presence of heterogeneous interfaces, multiple material parameters, anisotropic media, and multidimensional field coupling. This paper proposes a Flux-Conserved Physics-Informed Neural Networks framework that combines domain decomposition with a discontinuous Galerkin-inspired residual formulation and numerical-flux-based interface coupling. Roe numerical flux is adopted as the specific upwind-type flux in the interface loss to promote physically consistent information transfer across subdomains. Hard boundary constraints, joint input–output normalization, gradient-normalization-based adaptive loss balancing, and a two-stage adaptive moment estimation and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization strategy are also incorporated to improve training stability and accuracy. The framework is evaluated on four fixed benchmarks: a one-dimensional two-parameter time-domain layered model, a one-dimensional frequency-domain anisotropic model, a three-dimensional time-domain model, and a three-dimensional frequency-domain anisotropic model. Across the tested configurations, the predictions agree well with discontinuous Galerkin and finite-element reference solutions, with maximum relative field errors below five percent and approximately fifty percent fewer residual sub-elements than the reference discretizations used for comparison. In the tested one-dimensional benchmark, the framework required approximately 500 s of offline training but became computationally advantageous after approximately 536 repeated evaluations. Comparisons with conventional, conservative, and extended physics-informed neural networks indicate improved interface consistency and convergence stability. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed framework for forward electromagnetic field prediction under the examined configurations. Generalization to unseen parameters, frequencies, and geometries, and extension to parametric and inverse modeling, are left for future study.

verified_metadata.title: Dynamic weighted mixture-of-experts physics-informed learning for real-time microchannel cooling field reconstruction
verified_metadata.abstract: Real-time thermal management of high-power microchannel cooling systems requires fast and accurate reconstruction of temperature, pressure, and velocity fields. However, full three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations remain computationally prohibitive for online deployment, while purely data-driven surrogate models may violate governing thermal-fluid constraints. This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled physics-informed surrogate framework, the Dynamic Weighted Learning Rate Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts Physics-Informed Neural Network (DWLR-MMoE-PINN), for real-time field reconstruction in microchannel cooling. The proposed framework integrates three problem-specific components into a unified workflow: a corrected reduced-order model for efficient dataset generation, learned soft expert routing to mitigate multiphysics task interference, and component-wise dynamic loss normalization to balance heterogeneous physical objectives. The corrected two-dimensional (2D) model decreased the composite error by 37.4% compared with the uncorrected counterpart. Under a unified case-level learning protocol, DWLR-MMoE-PINN reduced the final validation loss by 31.0% and the overall out-of-distribution error by 49.5% relative to DWLR-PINN. The trained surrogate enables microsecond-level point-wise prediction and reconstructs the exported spatial field of one case in 0.116 s, giving speedups of more than three orders of magnitude over the corrected 2D solver and four orders of magnitude over the full 3D simulation. These results support DWLR-MMoE-PINN as a real-time field-reconstruction surrogate for future digital-twin applications, while sensor integration, online calibration, and closed-loop thermal control remain future work.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-driven automated forensic data anomaly detection using blockchain-based integrity verification
verified_metadata.abstract: In Internet of Things (IoT) systems, blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques have a major trend due to their significant. However, security, efficiency, and scalability are challenged due to the integration of AI techniques, which generate redundant data. To overcome these challenges, a novel Efficient Channel Attention-assisted Dense Transformer (ECA-deTrans) based data anomaly detection with blockchain is proposed for forensic evidence integrity verification. Initially, the raw data is collected from the repository and pre-processed. Feature extraction is performed using feature extraction using a Hybrid Autoencoder with 1 Dimensional Convolutional Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (HAE-1DBiLSTM). Based on the extracted features, ECA-deTrans performs forensic anomaly detection. Then, the smart contract system performs blockchain based integrity verification using Keccak-based Secure Hash Algorithm-3 with Enhanced Logistic Map (SHA-3-ELMC) chaotic algorithm. The blockchain creates an immutable audit trail that guarantees accountability, transparency, and compliance by permanently storing all AI discoveries, smart contract operations, and verification outcomes. Based on the simulation, the accuracy of 99.74%, precision of 99.48%, recall of 99.63%, F1-score of 99.55%, Mean Average Error (MAE) of 0.58%, throughput of 28.251 transactions per second (tps), and latency of 0.395 s were achieved. The experimental results demonstrate the significant of the proposed approach for real-time applicability.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed machine learning for asphalt mixture dynamic modulus: Balancing high accuracy with stability and rationality
verified_metadata.abstract: The dynamic modulus, a critical parameter for asphalt mixture viscoelasticity and pivotal for pavement engineering, conventionally faces determination challenges due to high costs, extensive data dependency, and limited physical insight. To overcome these, this study introduces a dual-driven predictive framework that integrates physical knowledge with data science principles. Initially, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) was employed to quantify the influence weights of twelve material composition parameters. Subsequently, leveraging K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), and Random Forest (RF) algorithms, a sensitive feature space was meticulously constructed. Critically, established positive correlations between softening point, asphalt type, and dynamic modulus were encoded as physics-based constraints within a Backpropagation Neural Network (BP-NN), culminating in a physics-informed, data-driven dynamic modulus prediction model. Rigorous multi-error index cross-validation and stability evaluation confirmed model robustness. Results revealed void volume and asphalt aggregate ratio as dominant dynamic modulus influencers, while apparent density of mineral powder and asphalt specific gravity could diminish generalization. Compared to data-driven counterparts, the proposed physical-data-driven model exhibited a marginal increase in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 41–46 Megapascals (MPa) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 28–29 MPa, yet consistently maintained Coefficient of Determination (R^{2}) > 0.96 and a significantly narrowed prediction confidence interval. These findings underscore that embedding physical constraints substantially enhances model stability and rationality, ensuring adherence to engineering principles while largely preserving high accuracy. This research offers a robust methodology for accurate dynamic modulus prediction and optimized material design in asphalt mixtures, advancing scientific road design and sustainable pavement engineering.

title: Kalman-enhanced artificial intelligence in machining: A systematic review
abstract: Hybrid methods combining Kalman filters (KFs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) integrate state estimation with nonlinear learning in machining. This systematic review develops a taxonomy of Kalman–AI coupling patterns, examines evaluation practice, and derives deployment implications for machining applications. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement and the PRISMA extension for search reporting (PRISMA-S). Searches in Scopus and the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection (peer-reviewed English journal/full conference papers, 2022–2026) were completed in November–December 2025, with a May 2026 Scopus/WoS update and a supplementary sensitivity search. From 7176 original and 1325 update records, 4419 database records were screened; with supplementary screening, 21 studies (2022–2026) were included. Four coupling patterns were identified: (A) Kalman-based preprocessing and feature conditioning; (B) learned system or observation components within Kalman loops; (C) Kalman-updated neural or polynomial models; and (D) cascaded or ensemble observer–learning schemes. Patterns A (9/21) and B (7/21) dominated. Reported comparisons usually favoured hybrids. Applications covered milling, turning, drilling, spindle thermal behaviour, and robotic machining, targeting tool wear and remaining useful life (RUL), force/deformation, fault detection, thermal error, and path correction. Evidence remains fragmented because datasets are narrow, tightly matched baselines and controlled ablations isolating the Kalman and AI contributions are limited, explicit uncertainty quantification is uncommon, and shared benchmarks are scarce. Shared datasets, controlled ablation protocols, physics-informed hybrids, and shop-floor demonstrators are priorities.

verified_metadata.title: Robust extrapolation of sparse particle image velocimetry measurements via a Mamba-integrated physics-informed neural network framework
verified_metadata.abstract: In industrial fluid engineering, continuous monitoring of unsteady flows is essential for mechanism analysis and process optimization, but is often limited by the hardware cost and data-storage burden of high-frequency particle image velocimetry systems. This study considers an artificial intelligence application in which sparse and short-duration particle image velocimetry observations are used to reconstruct flow-field evolution and to extrapolate the flow over a short future window. We propose a Mamba-integrated physics-informed neural network framework for this task. The implemented artificial intelligence uses a Mamba selective state-space sequence model to learn temporal advancement from probe-wise velocity histories, while a physics-informed neural network reconstructs continuous velocity and pressure fields under incompressible Navier–Stokes residual constraints. A mutual learning procedure links these two parts: the physics-informed reconstruction supplies residual-filtered temporal samples for sequence learning, and the learned temporal prior then guides reconstruction in the interval without observations. Evaluated on standard two-dimensional laminar cylinder-flow benchmarks and demonstrated qualitatively on real experimental particle image velocimetry data, the proposed framework reduces extrapolation root mean square error by up to approximately 61% compared with a standard physics-informed neural network baseline and maintains a reported three-cylinder extrapolation coefficient of determination of 0.986596 over the reported extrapolation window from 5 to 7 s. These results indicate that the proposed framework can serve as an artificial intelligence post-processing method for sparse-flow diagnostics, although broader deployment still requires validation under more complex flow and measurement conditions.

verified_metadata.title: Asymmetric spatio-temporal synergistic graph neural network for traffic flow forecasting
verified_metadata.abstract: Precise traffic flow forecasting continues to be difficult because of the intricate spatio-temporal interdependencies within transportation networks. While existing methods have achieved no-table progress, two critical limitations persist: (i) insufficient synergistic integration of spatio- temporal features that reflect real traffic dynamics, and (ii) ineffective capture of multi-timescale traffic node features. To resolve these concerns, we propose an Asymmetric Spatio-Temporal Synergistic Graph Neural Network (ASGNN). Our model introduces three key innovations: First, a learnable synergistic spatio-temporal adjacency matrix that dynamically unifies temporal and spatial relationships within the same latent dimension. Second, an asymmetric feature extraction mechanism that adaptively applies enhanced synergistic modeling to pivotal nodes. Third, a hierarchical architecture that progressively fuses multi-timescale node features into comprehensive global representations. To verify the effectiveness of our model in traffic flow forecasting, we conducted experiments on real-world datasets (PeMSD4 and PeMSD8), with detailed ablation studies confirming the contribution of each component.

verified_metadata.title: Transformers in protein informatics: A survey of structure prediction, function annotation, interactions, and drug discovery
verified_metadata.abstract: Protein informatics increasingly requires artificial intelligence models for analyzing biological sequences, structures, interactions, and drug-related targets. Transformer architectures, built on self-attention mechanisms, have become widely used in this field, but their reliability remains dependent on data coverage, biological context, and evaluation protocol. This survey critically reviews over 100 representative studies on Transformer-based methods for protein research. We organize the literature through a two-level taxonomy that separates model-class principles from problem-space applications, covering sequence-only language modeling, geometry-aware prediction, multimodal alignment, and generative design, together with structure prediction, function annotation, interaction analysis, drug discovery, and drug-target identification. We examine how pre-trained protein language models, structure-aware Transformers, and multimodal variants incorporate sequences, evolutionary profiles, and three-dimensional coordinates to address protein-specific constraints. We further synthesize key methodological issues, including geometric inductive bias, physical plausibility, scalability, uncertainty calibration, dataset bias, reproducibility, and generative-model evaluation. Through comparative tables and cross-domain analysis, this survey connects protein Transformer architectures to automated protein engineering, high-throughput drug screening, proteome-scale annotation, and laboratory-in-the-loop design. It evaluates these systems not only by predictive accuracy, but also by computational cost, latency, calibration, reproducibility, physical validation, and experimental utility, and concludes with a prioritized roadmap for deployable protein artificial intelligence.

verified_metadata.title: A physics-informed multi-source adaptive learning framework for tunnel settlement prediction under blasting excavation
verified_metadata.abstract: This study develops a physics-informed, multi-source adaptive learning framework for predicting tunnel settlement during drill-and-blast excavation. Blasting vibration data, geological conditions, and monitoring measurements are integrated to capture complex spatiotemporal interactions. A Spatial Exponential Decay Weighted interpolation with Local Residual Correction (SEDW-LRC) method is proposed to enhance vibration features. The framework combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with an attention mechanism to model temporal dependencies, while Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) is introduced for feature evaluation and adaptive model fusion based on prediction performance. A case study of the Xingye tunnel demonstrates that the enhanced vibration representation improves prediction accuracy by 7.2%. The proposed framework outperforms standalone models, achieving accuracy gains of 7.3% over XGBoost, 8.2% over LSTM-Attention, and 18.3% over LSTM. The results highlight the importance of integrating vibration response in data-driven prediction, providing support for intelligent blasting control and construction optimization.

verified_metadata.title: Adaptive resource-constrained neural networks for multi-class medical image classification
verified_metadata.abstract: Medical imaging classifiers are increasingly used to inform clinical decision-making. However, these systems often operate under implicit assumptions of unconstrained treatment capacity. In reality, healthcare providers face severe resource constraints, ranging from radiologist time to surgical availability, necessitating models that align classification decisions with actionable capacity. We propose a novel deep learning framework for multi-class medical image classification that integrates resource-aware constraint optimization directly into neural network training. This approach enables knowledge-intensive engineering of predictive models tailored for clinical decision support under real-world treatment or computational constraints. Our method is particularly suited to common clinical scenarios such as staging cancer progression, grading knee osteoarthritis, or classifying skin lesions, where disease stages imply different treatment pathways but not all can be addressed due to resource limitations. We evaluate our method on two distinct medical imaging tasks: knee osteoarthritis severity grading from X-ray images and skin lesion classification from dermatoscopic images. Across both datasets, our approach demonstrates improved performance and constraint compliance over traditional predict-then-optimize pipelines, particularly under tight resource constraints Our results highlight the framework’s generalizability across diverse medical imaging modalities and class imbalance scenarios, making it a compelling tool for engineering intelligent diagnostic systems in healthcare.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed data-driven model for design-oriented shear capacity prediction and resistance factor calibration of ultra-high-performance concrete beams
verified_metadata.abstract: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) is one of the most promising cement-based materials for sustainable and resilient infrastructure, owing to its exceptional strength and durability. Nevertheless, the complex interactions among fiber bridging, aggregate interlock, dowel action, and size-dependent fracture mechanics in shear-critical UHPC beams are not adequately captured by current design codes, leading to large prediction scatter and uncertain safety margins. To address these limitations, this study introduces a physics-informed and interpretable machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) framework, termed the Monotone Additive Interaction Network (Phys-MAIN), for design-oriented shear capacity prediction and resistance factor calibration of UHPC beams across four reinforcement configurations. The architecture embeds four configuration-specific submodels within an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), where each submodel enforces physically consistent input–output relationships through monotone functions and bivariate interaction surfaces. Distribution-free conformal prediction intervals calibrated on held-out residuals provide finite-sample coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions. Model uncertainty is further characterized through the American Concrete Institute (ACI) 318 load and resistance factor design (LRFD) reliability calibration at a target reliability index of ${\beta }_{T}=3.5$, with resistance factors calibrated across four reinforcement configurations and five shear-mechanism sub-populations. Phys-MAIN achieves a cross-validated ${R}^{2}$ of 0.933 with a zero percent physical monotonicity violation rate. Configuration-specific calibration reveals that reinforcement type strongly governs the required safety margin, with calibrated resistance factors (for the fiber-containing configurations) ranging from 0.485 for fiber-only beams to 0.625 for fiber-with-prestress beams. To facilitate practical adoption, the framework is deployed as a user-friendly interactive tool available at https://twakjira.github.io/Phys_MAIN/.

title: A mesh-adaptive hypergraph neural network for unsteady flow around oscillating and rotating structures
abstract: Graph neural networks, recently introduced into the field of fluid flow surrogate modeling, have been successfully applied to model the temporal evolution of various fluid flow systems. Existing applications, however, are mostly restricted to cases where the domain is time-invariant. The present work extends the application of graph neural network-based modeling to fluid flow around structures rotating with respect to a certain axis. Specifically, we propose to apply a graph neural network-based surrogate model with part of the mesh/graph co-rotating with the structure and part of the mesh/graph static. A single layer of interface cells are constructed at the interface between the two parts and are allowed to distort and adapt, which helps in circumventing the difficulty of interpolating information encoded by the neural network at every graph neural network layer. Dedicated reconstruction and re-projection schemes are designed to counter the error caused by the distortion and connectivity change of the interface cells. The effectiveness of our proposed framework is examined on two test cases: (i) fluid flow around a 2D oscillating airfoil, and (ii) fluid flow past a 3D rotating cube. Our results show that the model achieves stable rollout predictions over hundreds or even a thousand time steps. We further demonstrate that one could enforce accurate, error-bounded prediction results by incorporating the measurements from sparse pressure sensors. In addition to the accurate flow field predictions, the lift and drag force predictions closely match with the computational fluid dynamics calculations, highlighting the potential of the framework for modeling fluid flow around rotating structures, and paving the path towards a graph neural network-based surrogate model for more complex scenarios like flow around marine propellers.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Alzheimer’s disease screening via handwriting images acquired by smartphones
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a common neurodegenerative disorder that progressively impairs cognitive and motor functions. Early diagnosis can slow the progression and improve the quality of life. However, many diagnostic tools are invasive or costly, making them unsuitable for large-scale screening. Although Artificial Intelligence applied to medical imaging can aid diagnosis, it often relies on specialised hardware, controlled environments, and expert operators, limiting scalability. This study presents a smartphone-acquired handwriting screening system evaluated on data acquired in everyday settings. We design an end-to-end validation of a deployable, task-specific pipeline for unconstrained smartphone image captures. This pipeline integrates region-of-interest extraction that is robust to uneven lighting and paper transparency, convolutional feature extraction, multiple per-task classifiers, and late-fusion ensemble strategies to improve robustness across handwriting tasks. The engineering application is a practical screening tool for Alzheimer’s disease that enables remote, low-cost data collection via standard smartphones, without specialised equipment or professional supervision. Evaluation on a dataset of 174 participants (89 patients and 85 healthy controls) acquired with a 25-task protocol shows that smartphone-acquired images yield task-wise accuracies of up to 76%, comparable to those from high-resolution scans, while ensemble methods achieve accuracy exceeding 84%, with precision of 90%. These results indicate a scalable and practical route to real-world screening beyond clinical environments.

verified_metadata.title: Review of physics augmented: Physics-guided, physics-informed, and physics-encoded machine learning models in condition monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: In a broader sense, condition monitoring solutions can be either data-driven or physics-based. The performance and robustness of data-driven models largely depend on the quantity of training data and the interpretability level of the machine learning (ML) model (e.g., black box, white box, grey box). These models often suffer from limited interpretability, as their predictions do not necessarily adhere to underlying physical laws. In contrast, physics-based models are influenced by modeling assumptions, system complexity, computational cost, and the level of domain expertise required. Recently, increasing attention has been given to combining both paradigms, generally referred to as Physics Augmented Machine Learning (PAML). In this hybrid approach, physical knowledge can be integrated into any module of the ML framework. In this study, PAML methods are classified into three categories according to how physical information is embedded: Physics-guided Neural Network (PGNN), Physics-informed Neural Network (PINN), and Physics-encoded Neural Network (PENN), and a detailed analysis of their algorithmic frameworks and structural characteristics is provided. Furthermore, a review of their applications in the context of rotating machinery, including dynamic modeling, fault diagnostics, and fault prognostics is presented. Finally, several current challenges and future directions are outlined to support the integration and further development of physical information and machine learning-based approaches.

title: Learning reduced-order dynamics with singularity via Latent-Augmented Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of self-intersecting trajectories (in phase space) in industrial reduced-order modeling and proposes the Latent-Augmented Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (LA-NODEs) framework. From the perspective of artificial intelligence, the proposed method augments conventional neural ordinary differential equations to enhance model expressiveness, enabling the representation of conflicting vector fields that may arise in reduced-order systems, thereby improving learning accuracy. Through theoretical analysis, the underlying mechanism of the framework is established, and a condition for determining the minimum required augmentation dimension is derived. From the perspective of engineering applications, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on the reduced-order system of two representative industrial models, namely an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drive and a distributed energy system (DES). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can recover system features that are difficult to capture using conventional approaches and achieve superior performance in terms of prediction accuracy and modeling fidelity, thereby providing an effective approach for high-precision data-driven modeling of complex industrial systems.

title: Image-driven machine learning constitutive mapping the confluence of material and micro-topological attributes in short fiber polymer composites
abstract: Short Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composites have attracted significant attention due to their customizable mechanical behavior. However, the inherent complexity and heterogeneity of these composites pose critical challenges in accurately quantifying their constitutive properties and optimizing micro-structural designs through experimental and computational methods. To circumvent the intricacies and labour-intensive nature of traditional experimental and numerical modelling approaches, we propose a machine learning (ML) model that takes the microstructural topology of fiber distribution as input in the direct image form, along with material properties of fibers and matrix, and generates insightful visualization of the stress and strain fields as output. Such direct image-based mapping of the topological architectures significantly alleviates the hurdle of numerical representation of randomly oriented and randomly located fibers along with intrinsic material properties of the constituting elements, while making the ML model capable of handling high-dimensional datasets that would be impossible to deal with based on traditional data-driven approaches. We have employed finite element simulations based on Representative Area Element to train a paired image-to-image (pix2pix) model exploiting conditional Generative Adversarial Networks, considering three scenarios of constitutive mapping in the order of increasing complexity, (1) only varying material properties, (2) only varying microstructural geometry, and (3) simultaneously varying material properties and microstructural geometry. Developing an efficient, strictly image-based ML algorithm for constitutive mapping of composites can reduce analysis time and cost, while enabling qualitative and quantitative insights for microstructure development, multiscale design, and multifunctional optimization. Further, it establishes the foundation for image-to-video learning of evolving heterogeneous composite mechanics.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed reinforcement learning for energy-efficient unmanned aerial vehicle navigation with context-aware power estimation
verified_metadata.abstract: The transition of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) from simulation to real-world deployment presents significant challenges due to the simulation-to-reality (sim-to-real) gap, particularly concerning simplified electromechanical dynamics and energy optimization. To address these discrepancies, this paper proposes a hierarchical framework integrating bottom-up physics modeling, neural system identification, and energy-aware control. In contrast to conventional kinematic models, the developed high-fidelity environment explicitly integrates actuator dynamics, including voltage saturation, Back-Electromotive Force (Back-EMF), and transient delays, ensuring that the learned policies respect realistic physical constraints. Central to this framework is a novel context-aware neural architecture designed to decouple flight states from latent hardware signatures. This module achieves a hardware classification accuracy exceeding 97% and robust power estimation with a nominal Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE) of approximately 1.5%, effectively functioning as a virtual sensor. Leveraging these learned dynamics, we introduce an Energy-Cost-Optimized Reinforcement Learning (Eco-RL) policy that couples a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) planner with a robust Feedback Linearization and Model Reference Adaptive Control (FBL-MRAC) execution layer. By incorporating the learned power consumption into the reinforcement learning reward loop, the agent synthesizes momentum-conserving trajectories that strategically trade off altitude potential against air density variations. Extensive validation across five heterogeneous hardware classes demonstrates an overall energy reduction of 19.8% across randomized sorties, which consolidates into a highly significant 13.5% efficiency gain under strict pair-wise evaluations compared to standard policies, confirming the efficacy of physics-informed Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) in optimizing flight efficiency.

title: Holistic segmentation of minimally-invasive robotic surgical scenes using feature-adaptive localization
abstract: Holistic surgical scene segmentation is vital for training novice surgeons in robotic minimally invasive surgeries (RMIS). While the SegFormer model shows great potential due to its adaptability to various input image resolutions, the contrast between surgical instruments and anatomical structures poses challenges for segmentation output. In this paper, we propose a F eature- A daptive S patial L ocalization Seg Former ( FASL-Seg ) model, an artificial intelligence-based semantic segmentation model for surgical video analysis. Built on a SegFormer backbone, FASL-Seg introduces feature processing mechanisms to improve holistic segmentation of anatomy and instruments in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery. FASL-Seg incorporates two feature processing streams: a High-Level Feature Projection (HLFP) targeting low-resolution features, and a Low-Level Feature Projection (LLFP) for high-resolution feature maps. These streams are coupled with a shallow decoder that maximizes information conservation from both stream outputs, together introducing robustness against diverse feature representations of tools and anatomy. Extensive experiments were conducted on four surgical benchmark datasets, where FASL-Seg achieved results that were competitive or superior to thestate-of-the-art, at mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 0.73 on Endoscopic Vision 2018 Challenge (EndoVis18), 0.75 on Cholecystectomy Segmentation, 0.86 on EndoVis18 tool segmentation, 0.74 on Endoscopic Vision 2017 (EndoVis17), and 0.9594 on Kvasir-Instrument binary segmentation. These results support the advantages of the proposed architecture for holistic scene segmentation, potentially enabling automated annotations of robotic videos to support RMIS training programs. Code is available at: https://github.com/Muraam-Abdel-Ghani/FASL-Seg .

verified_metadata.title: Neural network combining traditional features and deep features for electroencephalograph motor imagery brain-computer interfaces
verified_metadata.abstract: Feature extraction and classification are key tasks in brain-computer interfaces (BCI) based on motor imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG), which have applications in motor function compensation and rehabilitation. However, existing deep learning methods suffer from issues such as insufficient utilization of neurophysiological priors (event-related desynchronization/synchronization) and inadequate handling of multi-domain (spectral, spatial, temporal) information. To address these problems, this study proposes a parallel hybrid network integrating traditional feature engineering and deep learning, which differs from serial cascade and purely data-driven paradigms: it integrates one-versus-rest filter bank common spatial patterns (for extracting spatial-spectral features), residual convolutional neural network (for learning nonlinear spatio-temporal features), dynamic graph convolutional network (for analyzing feature relations), and gated recurrent unit (for capturing long-term temporal patterns). Additionally, we use an attention mechanism to dynamically fuse features and a composite loss function to enhance feature clustering performance. Our method was validated on three public datasets: BCI Competition IV-2a (4-class, 85.28 ± 10.43%), IV-2b (2-class, 89.75 ± 8.02%), and the dataset by Kaya et al., 2018, Sci Data (3-class, 78.66 ± 8.31%; 5-class, 59.80 ± 8.69%; 6-class, 65.33 ± 8.04%). Results show that our method significantly outperforms recent methods and traditional methods, with a reduction in accuracy fluctuation. Ablation experiments show the contribution of each module, with accuracy drops of 1.5%-2.5% after removing any single component. This study demonstrates that the hybrid network model, by complementing traditional feature engineering and deep learning, breaks through the limitations of a single technical route and provides an approach with accuracy and robustness for multi-class MI-EEG decoding.

verified_metadata.title: A physics-informed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous reinforcement design of double-pile caps
verified_metadata.abstract: Pile caps in bridge foundations serve as critical load-bearing components, directly influencing structural safety and economic efficiency. However, the current reinforcement design of double-pile caps still relies on engineering experience and manual verification, resulting in low efficiency. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) method, termed Rein-MARL, for intelligent reinforcement design. Rein-MARL integrates a physics-guided reinforcement learning environment with a knowledge-informed reward function. By decomposing the collaborative design process of rebars into multiple sub-tasks, a multi-agent system (MAS) is employed to independently design different components. Validation using practical design cases demonstrates that the artificial intelligence (AI)-generated reinforcement schemes satisfy both code-based safety and economic requirements. Compared with engineer-designed layouts, Rein-MARL achieves average relative errors of 9.8% in load-bearing capacity and 3.6% in steel consumption. Remarkably, Rein-MARL reduces the design time to only 0.5% of that required by the manual process, indicating a substantial improvement in reinforcement automation and providing a theoretical basis for future intelligent design in bridge systems.

verified_metadata.title: A medical image classification approach based on vision transformer features and the enhanced Bayes algorithm
verified_metadata.abstract: Image classification is a fundamental task in computer vision, requiring methods that balance high accuracy with computational efficiency. In this study, we introduce an efficient image classification approach that combines feature extraction using Vision Transformer (ViT) with an improved probabilistic classification technique, referred to as Enhanced Bayes. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, three experiments were conducted. The first experiment assessed overall classification performance, while the second and third experiments compared our approach with ten models, including both traditional machine learning and deep learning models. The results demonstrate that our method performed better than ten existing classification models, including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Residual Network with 50 layers (ResNet50), Visual Geometry Group with 16 layers (VGG16), GoogLeNet Inception version 3 (Inception V3), Inception Residual Network version 2 (Inception ResNet-V2), and the original ViT, achieves higher classification accuracy while maintaining low computational cost. Additionally, we conducted a comparative analysis of different feature extraction methods. The combination of ViT-based features with the Enhanced Bayes classifier consistently performed better than other combinations, such as VGG16, Inception V3, and Inception ResNet-V2, in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. In addition, the proposed method is computationally efficient and requires less training time than deep learning models. The feature extraction process is lightweight and efficient, making the method suitable for real-time medical image classification applications.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed pedestrian trajectory prediction under Haze with selective state space and heterogeneous graph modeling
verified_metadata.abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction in image-driven perception pipelines is central to intelligent transportation, yet haze degrades image formation, detection, tracking, and forecasting. This study presents the Fog-Aware Physics-Informed Trajectory Predictor (FAPTP), a physics-informed framework for robust pedestrian motion forecasting under haze. It couples a Koschmieder-based physical-prior feature module, an input-dependent selective state-space temporal encoder with cross-layer attention, and a visibility-conditioned heterogeneous graph network for pedestrian and group interactions. Estimated scattering, atmospheric light, and scene-normalized pseudo-depth variables condition temporal encoding, graph interactions, feature fusion, and probabilistic decoding, while temporal representations initialize graph nodes to maintain cross-module flow. A controlled detection-cascaded benchmark is constructed from pedestrian trajectory datasets with four haze-severity levels, shared detector–tracker inputs, and independently specified image and target factors. External predictors are evaluated under a coordinate-only protocol, whereas the complete frame-conditioned model is compared with input-matched controls. Original and behavior-transformed annotations are reported separately, and held-out image-haze/target pairings test cross-transformation generalization. Controlled ablations further isolate the roles of frame evidence, physical-variable correspondence, temporal encoding, and social interaction modeling. Further analyses examine alternative perception pipelines, non-uniform haze, severe missing observations, dense-scene group identification, sequence-length latency, qualitative failure cases, and zero-shot transfer to real daytime light-rain sequences. The results show that atmospheric priors, selective temporal modeling, and visibility-aware social reasoning reduce cascade degradation across the validated operating range.

verified_metadata.title: Comparative artificial intelligence modeling for taxon-specific gene ontology term prediction in Flavobacterium proteins
verified_metadata.abstract:
Accurate Gene Ontology (GO) term prediction is essential for biomedical research, yet broad computational predictors may underperform on lineage-specific proteomes such as Flavobacterium, a genus that includes major aquaculture pathogens. To address this gap, we developed a taxon-specific artificial intelligence framework using all available Universal Protein Resource (UniProt) reference Flavobacterium proteomes (35,554 proteins, 762 GO terms). We used sequence-derived physicochemical descriptors and Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2 (ESM-2) protein language model embeddings as feature vectors for non-graph models and as node attributes for graph models, while a Many-against-Many sequence searching version 2 (MMseqs2) sequence similarity graph was constructed from amino-acid sequence alignments. We evaluated five multi-label classification methods: eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), a deep neural network (DNN), Graph Attention Network (GAT), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Graph Sample and Aggregate (GraphSAGE). At the fixed 0.5 decision threshold, the DNN achieved the highest Micro F1 score (0.9290) and significantly exceeded the other taxon-specific models in aligned paired comparisons. GCN ranked next (0.9033) and significantly exceeded XGBoost (0.8952), whereas GAT (0.8929) was not statistically resolved from XGBoost after multiple-comparison correction. In a controlled evaluation on the same 5333 held-out proteins under symmetric retained-space GO ancestor closure, validation-selected protein-centric F1 was 0.9406 for DNN and 0.9121 for XGBoost, compared with 0.8401 for ProteInfer, 0.6426 for reduced available-component NetGO 4.0, and 0.4741 for DeepGO-SE; both taxon-specific models exceeded all three pretrained general-purpose predictors after paired Holm correction (
𝑝
=
0.0006
 for each comparison). The sensitivity analysis showed that the shared baseline configuration understated GAT and GCN performance, whereas GraphSAGE was less sensitive near the baseline. These findings establish the value of architecture-specific model selection and aligned evaluation for clade-restricted functional annotation, with potential applications to aquaculture reverse vaccinology and vaccine–target prioritization. The code is available at https://github.com/CEL-lab/go-flavo.

title: Beyond real-time sensing: A design-model-constrained method for robust acquisition of road geometry, friction, and visibility in rainy-weather automated driving
abstract: Automated driving requires continuous perception, but sensors often fail in heavy rain, causing perceptual blindness. To address this challenge, we propose a perception backup system that guarantees the availability of essential environmental parameters independent of compromised sensors. This system integrates three model-driven modules: (i) The Design-Model-Constrained Geometric Parameter Generation (DMC-GPG) method accesses digital Building Information Modeling (BIM) / Computer-Aided Design (CAD) design models via deterministic coordinate mapping mapping, generates high-fidelity road geometric parameters (e.g., curvature, grade) at the vehicle's position, and exhibits strong weather robustness; (ii) A physics-informed neural network, trained on multi-physics simulation data, directly maps environmental inputs (e.g., rainfall intensity, speed) to the tire-pavement friction coefficient (μ), bypassing unreliable intermediate variables such as water film depth(WFD); (iii) A Random Forest-Back Propagation-XGBoost (F-BP-X) ensemble model predicts the Maximum Visible Distance (MVD) under the combined effects of rainfall, illumination, and vehicle spray, using field experimental data. Extensive validation under rainfall conditions demonstrates high accuracy (R² > 0.99 for friction; Mean Absolute Percentage Error = 3.05% for MVD) and strong generalization across tested scenarios. By providing a reliable, model-driven alternative during sensor failure, this work establishes a robust foundation for fail-operational automated driving under heavy rainfall.

verified_metadata.title: Multi-grained image-text retrieval in farmland remote sensing via multimodal large language models
verified_metadata.abstract: Low-altitude farmland remote sensing (FRS) has become an important tool for precision agricultural monitoring. However, existing FRS methods are mainly designed for segmentation with predefined categories, making them insufficient for semantic understanding and unable to support flexible natural-language queries. To address this limitation, we introduce an artificial intelligence-based task, FRS cross-modal retrieval, which aims to retrieve target farmland regions from large-scale remote sensing images using textual descriptions. To support this task, we construct the first Farmland Remote Sensing Cross-Modal Retrieval (FRS-CMR) dataset, containing 67,806 image-text pairs generated through multimodal large language models and expert refinement. Based on FRS-CMR, we propose a Farmland-oriented Multi-Grained Retrieval (FarmMGR) framework for image-text alignment. FarmMGR jointly exploits global scene semantics and local region-level cues to capture both large-scale landscape patterns and fine-grained farmland characteristics. To further improve semantic alignment, we design Prototype-Based Semantic Alignment (PBSA) to alleviate the soft-positive sample problem, Global Semantics Hierarchical Feature Integration (GSHFI) to adaptively fuse global and local representations, and Instance-Level Semantic Relation Modeling (ISRM) to capture relational dependencies among farmland instances. In addition, Memory-Enhanced Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning (MECCL) enlarges the negative sample pool and improves representation discrimination. Extensive experiments on FRS-CMR show that FarmMGR achieves a mean recall of 28.57%, outperforming existing image-text retrieval methods and demonstrating its effectiveness for language-driven farmland remote sensing retrieval.

title: Global deep learning-based maritime anomaly detection with transformed features derived from passage plans
abstract: Safety at sea has gained crucial importance due to the dense vessel traffic caused by the immense increase in world maritime trade. Therefore, it is vital for the vessels to possess onboard awareness procedures, such as anomaly detection methods, to avoid unsafe situations. The vast majority of state-of-the-art methods focus on regional solutions processing location-based features that require dense automatic identification system message coverage, which limits the applicability of these solutions to different regions or introduces scalability issues. Consequently, maritime anomaly detection from a global perspective is still a challenging problem. In this paper, we address the maritime anomaly detection problem from a global perspective using transformed features (TF) derived from passage plans, which are preconstructed plans related to voyages. We present a solution, namely GeoTrackNet-TF, that builds on an existing maritime anomaly detector by integrating transformed features. Such integration enables a location abstraction and projection of the location-related features onto passage plans. Furthermore, we use an explanation technique to provide further insights into the anomaly decisions made by the trained model. We evaluate the proposed solution on real-world automatic identification system messages obtained from vessels sailing globally without region restrictions. The experiments indicate that the proposed solution provides reasonable results in detecting unusual vessel sailing patterns.

verified_metadata.title: A novel channel-encoder latent diffusion models for in vivo human brain spectral reconstruction
verified_metadata.abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) provide neurosurgeons with a powerful tool to accurately identify and remove brain tumors while minimizing damage to healthy tissues. However, conventional HSI systems suffer from insufficient temporal resolution, inadequate spectral resolution for precise tissue differentiation, and high hardware costs that limit clinical accessibility. To address these challenges, we propose a spectral reconstruction method based on a latent diffusion model (LDM), termed the channel encoder latent diffusion model (CE-LDM), which reconstructs high-fidelity HSI from snapshot RGB images captured by standard cameras. This snapshot-based acquisition inherently resolves temporal constraints by freezing tissue motion, while dramatically reducing hardware costs through the use of conventional Red–Green–Blue (RGB) sensors. Given the high-dimensional nature of hyperspectral data, we design a channel encoder to extract prior information, reduce data redundancy, and effectively mitigate the underconstrained problem in spectral reconstruction. Meanwhile, the diffusion model significantly improves spectral fidelity through iterative denoising. Additionally, we design a residual attention denoising network (RADNet) to enhance feature extraction and image detail reconstruction. Tests on in vivo Human Brain HSI dataset validate demonstrates that CE-LDM achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality with the lowest computational cost, offering an optimal balance for real-time intraoperative applications, and subsequent classification tasks confirm its clinical applicability and great potential in advancing hyperspectral brain tumor diagnosis.

title: Data-driven cycle time optimisation in semiconductor manufacturing using machine learning and heuristic search algorithms
abstract: In semiconductor wafer fabrication, cycle time strongly affects throughput and cost, yet is hard to control because bottlenecks shift across tools over time. This paper presents a hybrid framework that combines machine learning (ML) and heuristic optimisation to minimise the imposed Delta Cycle Time (ΔCT) in a wafer fabrication plant. Multiple ML models were trained to predict ΔCT from each tool's Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO), and Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) were used to optimise these indicators against the trained model. The Random Forest model demonstrated greater robustness than the other Machine Learning models, achieving a best-case per-tool root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.029, although the cross-validated RMSE varies widely across tools (median ≈ 0.49). The framework was evaluated on proprietary data from a Seagate Technology wafer fabrication facility comprising 96 tools. The Random Forest with the Genetic Algorithm achieved the greatest improvement, reducing average ΔCT from +0.276 to −0.392 days (a 0.668-day mean reduction), improving all 96 tools. PSO was comparable at −0.347 days, a 0.623 day reduction, again improving all 96 tools; SQP was more conservative at +0.091 days, a 0.184 day reduction, improving 77 of 96 tools. In some tools, baseline ΔCT is close to zero, so absolute day reductions are a more appropriate indicator than percentage reductions. This framework converts production logs into tool-specific KPI recommendations, showing where cycle-time reductions are achievable.

verified_metadata.title: A unified hard-constraint physics-informed neural network approach for sparse-observation airflow-field reconstruction under complex boundary conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate reconstruction of the full airflow field is essential for real-time monitoring and control in engineering applications. Although conventional computational fluid dynamics methods offer high accuracy, their computational cost is often prohibitive for real-time scenarios. Data-driven methods present a more efficient alternative; however, their performance is constrained by the sparse observations typically encountered in practical environments. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) alleviate this limitation by incorporating physical laws, yet their practical applicability remains hindered by the difficulty of enforcing complex boundary conditions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a unified hard-constraint approach for airflow field reconstruction that enables numerous, discontinuous, and irregular boundary conditions to be handled simultaneously within a single framework. The proposed method establishes a unified implicit geometry representation for complex boundary conditions by integrating analytical distance functions for regular geometries and neural-network-based distance functions for irregular geometries via R-function-inspired smooth Boolean composition. A customized PINN framework is further developed for airflow field reconstruction by incorporating the proposed implicit boundary representation, sparse observations, and the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations. The proposed framework is validated using both numerical simulations and experimental measurements. In the numerical case without an occupant using 15 sparse observation points, the proposed hard-constraint method reduced the root mean square error and mean absolute error components u by 19.4% and 33.6%, respectively, compared to the soft-constraint method. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and highlight its potential for practical airflow field reconstruction in complex engineering environments.

title: Data-driven seismic fragility and risk evaluation of existing reinforced-concrete bridge portfolios under limited data
abstract: Preliminary screening of existing transport infrastructure networks is essential to support timely maintenance and retrofit decisions, improve structural resilience, and reduce the economic and environmental impacts of severe damage, failure, and inefficient resource allocation. This study investigates a machine-learning-based pathway for quantitative, simplified seismic risk screening of typologically homogeneous reinforced-concrete girder-bridge portfolios under limited data, in accordance with the Italian Guidelines for existing bridges. Fragility labels are derived through a streamlined cloud-analysis benchmark for 75 simply supported reinforced-concrete lattice-girder bridges, yielding the lognormal fragility parameters: median intensity measure μ , logarithmic dispersion β , and ultimate displacement capacity d u . Supervised regression models are trained to map routinely available inventory descriptors, including geometric and mechanical proxies, to ( μ , β , d u ) . Among the tested models, Gaussian Process Regression provides the best balance between accuracy and stability in the small-sample regime, with cross-validated R 2 values close to 0.9 for all targets. The selected surrogate is applied to 10 additional bridge configurations to assess predictive capability on new cases. Finally, inferred fragility is coupled with site-specific seismic hazard to compute the mean annual frequency of exceedance λ , used to rank 25 bridges of the A19 motorway network in Sicily. Results show prioritization closely consistent with the cloud-analysis benchmark, while requiring substantially lower computational effort. Compared with qualitative guideline-based classes of attention, λ offers useful intra-class granularity for transparent, scalable prioritization. Limitations include reduced accuracy outside the training manifold, typology-specific validation, and lack of explicit condition and defectiveness features.

verified_metadata.title: A physics-informed neural networks framework based on free-form deformation for predicting thin-plate deflection with mixed boundary conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: Thin plates are common structural elements in engineering. Accurate and efficient prediction of its mechanical properties helps optimize equipment reliability and cost. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a type of deep learning model that incorporates physical laws, which can solve solid mechanics problems by learning physical principles. However, existing PINNs only consider simple, regular shapes due to the idealized assumptions. PINNs have limited capability to address irregular deformations that often occur during processes such as machining or assembly. Regarding the above issues, this paper first proposed an ideal rectangular plate PINNs (IRP-PINNs) framework under mixed boundary conditions. Accurate deflection predictions for thin-plate boundary loading problems are ensured by explicitly modeling the interaction between loaded and unloaded boundaries in the loss function. Second, based on the Free-Form Deformation (FFD) method, the irregular shape of the thin plate was described in matrix form. Combining matrix and IRP-PINNs, irregularly shaped plate PINNs (ISP-PINNs) and irregularly shaped shell PINNs (ISS-PINNs) were designed. Then, the accuracy of the model predictions was validated through comparison with the finite element method (FEM). Numerical validation shows that the relative error of IRP-PINNs is less than 1%, while the average relative error of ISS-PINNs is less than 2.73%. Finally, the predictive capability and computational efficiency of the model under actual operating conditions were evaluated through experiments. The proposed model can reduce prediction time by nearly tenfold while maintaining computational accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can efficiently and accurately accomplish the task of predicting thin plate deflection.

title: A physics prior-guided dual-stream attention network for motion prediction of elastic Bragg breakwaters
abstract: Accurate motion response prediction for elastic Bragg breakwaters is critical for their structural safety and operational integrity in marine environments. However, conventional deep learning models often exhibit limited generalization capabilities when presented with unseen sea states. These deficiencies stem from the neglect of natural decay observed in marine systems and inadequate modeling of wave-structure interaction (WSI). To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel Physics Prior-Guided Dual-Stream Attention Network (PhysAttnNet). First, the decay bidirectional self-attention (DBSA) module incorporates a learnable temporal decay to assign higher weights to recent states, aiming to emulate the natural decay phenomenon. Meanwhile, the phase differences guided bidirectional cross-attention (PDG-BCA) module explicitly captures the bidirectional interaction and phase relationship between waves and the structure using a cosine-based bias within a bidirectional cross-computation paradigm. These streams are synergistically integrated through a global context fusion (GCF) module. Finally, PhysAttnNet is trained with a hybrid time-frequency loss that jointly minimizes time-domain prediction errors and frequency-domain spectral discrepancies. Comprehensive experiments on wave flume datasets demonstrate that PhysAttnNet significantly outperforms mainstream models. Furthermore,cross-scenario generalization tests validate the model's robustness and adaptability to unseen environments, highlighting its potential as a framework to develop predictive models for complex systems in ocean engineering.

title: Combination of Fourier Neural Operators and Bayesian Neural Networks to identify anisotropic thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone from field heating tests integrating surrogate uncertainty
abstract: Reliable characterization of the thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone is critical for the long-term safety assessment of deep geological nuclear waste disposal. This work addresses the Bayesian Inference of key parameters, including transversely isotropic thermal conductivity characterized by the perpendicular conductivity, the anisotropy ratio, equivalent density, specific heat capacity using experimental data from two heating experiments TED and ALC1604. For this aim, the forward problem is first modeled with a three-dimensional COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, and synthesis data per experiment are generated to train surrogate models. We evaluate several machine learning surrogates, including classical regression, deep neural networks, Fourier Neural Operators, and Bayesian Neural Networks. Fourier Neural Operators provides accurate deterministic emulation and serves as the baseline surrogate for Bayesian Inference. To overcome the overconfidence inherent in plug-in approaches, we propose uncertainty-aware surrogates by leveraging the predictive distribution of Bayesian Neural Networks. Three strategies are investigated: (i) CES-style likelihood, marginalizing surrogate uncertainty directly in the likelihood formulation, (ii) E-lik, explicitly incorporates surrogate variance in the likelihood function and (iii) E-pos, propagating surrogate uncertainty at the posterior level via mixtures of posteriors. Bayesian inference is performed with Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and results demonstrate that integrating surrogate uncertainty broadens posterior credible intervals, improves calibration, and avoids overconfident estimates compared to deterministic surrogates. Our findings highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for surrogate uncertainty in Bayesian inversion of computationally demanding uncertainty-aware thermal modeling problems and provide a framework for robust parameter identification of host rock in nuclear waste repository safety assessment

verified_metadata.abstract: This paper proposes an evolvable physics-informed neural network (PINN) for experimental digital twins (EDTs) of industrial systems for real-time modeling and adaptation. The framework integrates three components: system identification with dynamic modeling PINN, stable prediction using temporal contrastive learning, and adaptive parameter learning based on residual adapters. The framework provides a foundation for evaluating system behavior and optimal strategies in dynamic industrial environments.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed neural networks for rapid flow field reconstruction in fluidized bed drying
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the challenges of real-time observation of gas-solid two-phase flow and the high computational cost/lack of real-time capability of traditional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations in fluidized bed drying processes, this paper proposes a rapid flow field reconstruction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). This method integrates sparse observation data with governing flow equations to achieve simultaneous prediction of key physical quantities including gas-phase velocity, solid-phase velocity, pressure, and solid volume fraction. A systematic evaluation was conducted under various conditions: spatial sparsity (20%, 5%, 1%), temporal sparsity (50%, 20%, 10%), noise interference (1%–20%), and cross-temporal extrapolation. Results show that with a spatial sampling rate as low as 5%, PINNs can still accurately reconstruct typical fluidization features such as bubble motion, solid-phase stratification, and pressure gradients. Even under an extreme sparsity of 1%, the overall flow pattern remains correct. Under dual spatio-temporal sparsity, the model demonstrates good information compensation capability, generating continuous and plausible transient evolution. With noise levels up to 20%, reconstruction errors exhibit only minor fluctuations, indicating strong noise resistance. Cross-temporal extrapolation experiments reveal that error growth over unseen time periods is steady and controllable, without non-physical oscillations. This study validates the stability, physical consistency, and robustness of PINNs under complex industrial scenarios involving sparsity, noise, and extrapolation, providing a viable technical pathway for real-time flow field reconstruction and intelligent monitoring in fluidized bed drying processes.

verified_metadata.title: Closed-loop generative inverse design of lattice structures via reinforcement learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Lattice structures are widely used in advanced engineering because of their lightweight characteristics and tunable mechanical properties. However, precise generative inverse design remains challenging because of the discrete combinatorial design space and nonlinear physical responses. Existing generative approaches often operate open-loop and focus on reproducing statistical distributions, making compliance with prescribed engineering targets difficult. To address this limitation, a performance-feedback-guided generative inverse-design framework integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a physics-constrained conditional variational autoencoder (PC-VAE). The PC-VAE provides a continuous latent representation of discrete lattice topologies, while a pretrained surrogate supplies immediate performance feedback. The inverse-design stage is formulated as a one-step goal-conditioned contextual decision problem, in which a task-specific proximal policy optimization (PPO) policy learns a distribution over complete latent vectors from surrogate-based rewards. Policy updates increase the likelihood of candidates satisfying prescribed mechanical conditions while retaining alternative topologies. The framework is evaluated in six scenarios involving point-target, interval-constrained, and simultaneous two-property matching. Compared with the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), PPO achieves comparable target-hit rates and consistently higher candidate uniqueness and topological diversity. Finite-element (FE) analyses of 48 prespecified validation structures were completed successfully. Median absolute surrogate-to-FE discrepancies were 3.03% for energy absorption and 3.88% for peak stress, with 87.50% of discrepancies within 10% for each property. For a given target, the method generates multiple topologically distinct structures with comparable mechanical responses, capturing the one-to-many relationship between prescribed properties and lattice topology. This study provides a flexible framework for target-directed generation of topologically diverse lattice candidates.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-driven multisource remote sensing image fusion: Advances, challenges, and future directions
verified_metadata.abstract: Multisource remote sensing image fusion has become an important solution to a long-standing limitation in Earth observation: individual sensors rarely provide high spatial detail, rich spectral information, reliable structural sensitivity, and frequent temporal coverage at the same time. This review examines how deep learning and artificial intelligence are being used to integrate multispectral, hyperspectral, panchromatic, optical, and synthetic aperture radar imagery for more reliable interpretation of complex ground scenes. It provides a technical synthesis of convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, transformer architectures, diffusion models, and hybrid model driven approaches, with attention to their fusion mechanisms, reconstruction behavior, computational demand, and suitability for operational use. Applications include land cover mapping, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, urban analysis, disaster assessment, and defense related interpretation. Rather than treating each fusion task separately, this review connects sensor heterogeneity, spatial and spectral resolution trade offs, radiometric correction, geometric correction, registration, noise reduction, and fusion level design within a single framework. The analysis indicates that convolutional models remain effective for stable local detail recovery, adversarial learning can improve visual sharpness but may introduce spectral distortion, transformer models better capture long range spatial and spectral relationships, and diffusion models offer refined reconstruction at greater computational cost. The review further identifies open challenges involving misregistration, spectral bias, limited labeled data, weak generalization across sensors, high memory requirements, and limited interpretability. Future progress should prioritize sensor aware learning, self supervised training, uncertainty aware evaluation, lightweight deployment, and application oriented benchmarks to improve reliability in operational Earth observation.

verified_metadata.title: From narrative to action: A hierarchical cognitive large language model agent framework for interpretable and adaptive human mobility behavior generation
verified_metadata.abstract: Understanding and replicating human mobility requires not only spatial–temporal accuracy but also an awareness of the cognitive hierarchy underlying real-world travel decisions. Existing approaches often lack interpretability and struggle to represent adaptive behavior under changing constraints. This study proposes a Narrative-to-Action hierarchical large language model agent framework that models human mobility as a cognitively interpretable, multi-level process. The framework decomposes mobility generation into macro-level narrative reasoning, meso-level reflective planning, and micro-level behavioral execution, enabling agents to produce semantically coherent and structurally executable daily schedules while allowing dynamic adjustment in response to contextual changes. A key component is a reflective mechanism drawing on Mobility Entropy by Occupation, which captures heterogeneous behavioral flexibility across occupational groups. Empirical evaluation using travel diary data from Guangzhou demonstrates improved fidelity across spatial, temporal, and semantic dimensions compared to baseline approaches. Overall, by explicitly modeling how individuals reason about and adapt to constraints, the framework provides a behaviorally grounded and interpretable approach for mobility analysis, providing a basis for more transparent future evaluation of policy interventions and equity impacts.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence for deep learning-based delamination detection in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer composites
abstract: The heterogeneous and anisotropic nature of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) introduces challenges in characterizing failure mechanisms, particularly delamination, in advanced composite engineering structures used across multiple industrial sectors. Although deep learning models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic performance in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), their inherent black-box nature limits interpretability and trust, thereby restricting deployment in real-world engineering applications. To address these limitations, this work proposes a methodology that integrates deep learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enable transparent and reliable delamination detection in CFRP structures. The main contribution in Artificial Intelligence lies in the integration of convolutional neural networks with time–frequency representations of guided-wave signals and model-agnostic explainability techniques for intelligent fault detection in composite materials. From an engineering perspective, the proposed approach is applied to SHM and delamination diagnosis of CFRP specimens subjected to fatigue loading in engineering systems using Lamb waves acquired by piezoelectric transducers. The recorded Lamb wave signals were transformed into time–frequency representations and used as inputs to multiple CNN architectures, evaluated under a leakage-controlled, leave-one-cycle-out cross-validation protocol with multi-seed statistical aggregation, achieving accuracy values of up to 95.9% with statistically validated inter-architecture comparisons The explainability analysis highlighted physically meaningful indicators of delamination, such as amplitude attenuation and frequency shifts, demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework as an intelligent decision-support tool for fault detection and monitoring in engineering applications involving composite structures.
