verified_metadata.title: A Large Language Model-based Generative Artificial Intelligence and hybrid machine learning framework for prediction and inverse design of jute fiber concrete
verified_metadata.abstract: The construction industry requires sustainable alternatives to conventional concrete to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining structural performance. Jute fiber concrete (JFC) is a promising low-carbon material; however, optimizing its mechanical properties is challenging because of complex nonlinear interactions among fiber characteristics and mix-design parameters. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Generative Artificial Intelligence (GEN-AI) with Decision Tree Boosting (DT-Boosting), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and GPR enhanced with Bayesian Optimization (GPR-BO) to predict and optimize JFC mechanical properties. An experimental dataset containing six input variables were expanded using a Large Language Model-based GEN-AI approach and validated through distribution analysis, boxplot comparisons, and Kendall correlation analysis. GPR-based models significantly outperformed DT-Boosting, reducing prediction errors by approximately 40–50%. The GPR-BO achieved the most consistent performance, with testing R^{2} values of 0.9242 for compressive strength and 0.9682 for tensile strength. However, the SHAP and Partial Dependence Plot analyses identified jute fiber volume fraction and fiber content as the most influential parameters, while the water–cement ratio exhibited a strong negative effect. Probabilistic validation confirmed accurate reproduction of strength distributions. Furthermore, integrating GPR-BO with NSGA-II enabled inverse mix design, automatically generating optimized JFC mixtures satisfying user-defined mechanical performance requirements. The optimization employed six mix-design decision variables and minimized both normalized prediction error and fiber volume fraction to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. The resulting framework extends forward prediction to practical inverse design, reducing trial-and-error experimentation and material waste while supporting resource-efficient, performance-based, and sustainable concrete mix development for engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: A secure federated learning framework with blockchain-based authentication for anomaly detection in cooperative smart farming
verified_metadata.abstract: Agriculture is still a crucial global pillar of the world economy, ensuring food security and livelihood. But changing climate conditions and increasing reliance on the Internet of Things (IoT) based precision agriculture have brought new challenges, mainly cybersecurity. Cooperative Smart Farming (CSF) schemes promote resource pooling among small farmers and thus, the adoption of cutting-edge technologies. Although democratizing precision farming also makes it more accessible to cyber threats. To sort out all these problems, the proposed method introduces a secure federated learning framework along with blockchain-based authentication for anomaly detection in CSFs. The proposed method employs a federated transfer learning-based shadow attention mechanism, in conjunction with the Zeiler and Fergus network, to amplify the performance of the anomaly detection technique. This allows farms to detect threats in premises while protecting data privacy, as only model updates that are encrypted are transmitted. A blockchain-backed decentralized authentication scheme based on the proof of authentication consensus protocol is built to provide trust and resistance to tampering. Moreover, the random k-sparsification technique with changing rank adjustment has a positive impact on communication efficiency, which results in the same level of accuracy but with less communication overhead. The proposed method is executed on four datasets, CSE-CIS-IDS2018, MQTTset, ToN-IoT, and Edge IoT, achieving classification accuracies of 99.99%,99.93%,99.94%, and 99.91%, respectively, and it performs better than the current techniques. This comprehensive framework provides a scalable and trusted method for anomaly detection in CSFs, enabling resilient, privacy-preserving, and intelligent smart farming ecosystems.

title: Pipe flow of thixotropic fluids: Experiments, simulations and neural networks
abstract: Thixotropy refers to the time dependent evolution of a material’s microstructure, where structural agglomerates are progressively broken down under shear and rebuild when flow ceases. This study examines how such microstructural dynamics influence the transient pressure response of thixotropic yield stress fluids in laminar pipe flow. Experiments on Laponite suspensions performed with a custom built pipe rig reveal a pronounced decay in pressure drop over time at constant flowrate, reflecting shear induced structural breakdown. Complementary computational fluid dynamics simulations based on the Houska thixotropic constitutive model reproduce the experimental observations and elucidate the interplay between structural breakdown and recovery that governs the evolution of flow. The simulations capture the transition from plug-like to shear thinning dominated velocity profiles as flow rate increases, accompanied by a reduction of unyielded regions. To reduce computational cost, a feed-forward neural network surrogate trained on a limited set of experimental and simulated data accurately predicts the time-dependent pressure drop across a wide range of flow conditions. The integrated experimental, computational, and data driven framework establishes a quantitative basis for modeling and predicting the unsteady transport behavior of thixotropic fluids in pipe flow.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial Intelligence-enhanced fine-grained anomaly detection for human-robot collaborative assembly
verified_metadata.abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA) extends traditional manual assembly by synergizing human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, and has become an important manufacturing paradigm in Industry 5.0. However, this synergy is frequently compromised by subtle human errors, whose automated detection presents a formidable challenge. This difficulty is fundamentally rooted in the visual ambiguity arising from high similarity in color, texture, and geometry between components and their assembly substrates. These conditions create low-contrast scenarios that obscure the fine-grained anomaly detection, such as minor positional offsets, rotational skews, and incorrect part substitutions. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-driven vision framework for fine-grained anomaly detection, enabling reliable in-process quality control for HRCA. The framework integrates three synergistic modules in a cohesive pipeline involving state perception, recognition and localization, and state discrimination. Firstly, a multi-task Keypoint Transformer U-Net (KP-TransUNet) performs concurrent component segmentation and keypoint detection with sub-pixel accuracy, establishing a robust foundation for geometric registration even in visually challenging environments. Subsequently, an improved You Only Look Once version 11 (Improved-YOLO11) algorithm precisely identifies and localizes assembly components. Finally, an Intersection over Union (IoU)-mask matching strategy combines box-level semantic matching with mask-level geometric deviation analysis to quantitatively discriminate among six typical assembly states. The efficacy of the proposed framework was empirically validated through a comprehensive case study on a satellite box assembly, achieving an overall anomaly detection accuracy of 97.30%.

title: Recursive online learning for stable long-term prediction of turbulent flows
abstract: Accurate long-term prediction of turbulent flows remains a key challenge in data-driven modeling owing to compounding errors during recursive rollout. We propose a recursive online learning (ROL) algorithm that incorporates simulation feedback into the learning process so as to reduce local prediction errors on surrogate-generated states encountered during long-horizon recursive rollout. We validated the ROL algorithm on both statistically stationary and extremely transient turbulent channel flows using several deep learning architectures. The results show that ROL consistently improves long-term stability and accuracy across the tested network architectures, even in a bypass-like transition. Importantly, ROL-enhanced models generalize robustly to strong noise perturbations and to larger domains beyond the training size while maintaining physically consistent turbulence dynamics. In addition, the trained models achieved speed-ups ranging from 33 × to 231 × relative to a graphics processing unit (GPU)-parallelized numerical solver. The proposed method is effective across the diverse network architectures tested, and enables fast and accurate inference, making it useful in scientific simulations that require robust long-horizon predictions.

title: Three-dimensional cementing displacement efficiency prediction based on domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network
abstract: Efficient displacement of drilling fluid by cement slurry is essential for ensuring cementing quality, and accurate flow-field prediction is crucial for improving displacement efficiency. Although computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is widely used to investigate displacement mechanisms, high-fidelity three-dimensional simulations are computationally expensive and inefficient for rapid engineering prediction and optimization. In recent years, data-driven neural networks have attracted attention due to their high computational efficiency; however, they rely heavily on large datasets, are prone to overfitting, and may produce predictions that violate physical laws. To address these issues, this study incorporates the governing fluid dynamics equations into the loss function of a deep neural network to impose physical constraints on flow-field evolution. Furthermore, a domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network (DD-PINN) is developed by dividing the computational domain into multiple coupled subdomains. Through parallel training and collaborative solving, the method alleviates convergence difficulties and instability commonly encountered by conventional PINNs in complex three-dimensional flow problems. Numerical experiments based on multi-condition three-dimensional datasets show that DD-PINN achieves higher prediction accuracy for pressure, velocity, and cement slurry concentration fields compared with purely data-driven models. For example, in predicting cement slurry volume fraction, the mean absolute error (MAE) is reduced from 1.27×10⁻² to 2.35×10⁻³. Compared with conventional PINN, the proposed method also significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining comparable accuracy. Additionally, it enables quantitative evaluation of displacement efficiency and provides guidance for parameter optimization in cementing operations.

verified_metadata.title: Seismic fragility prediction models for masonry buildings considering integration algorithms and deep learning frameworks
verified_metadata.abstract: The seismic fragility of masonry buildings have been ubiquitously discussed in multiple zones worldwide. However, field inspection and data collection after earthquakes demonstrate the disadvantages of being time-consuming and labour-intensive, which poses a challenge for quickly obtaining the seismic fragility features of masonry structure clusters. To improve the efficiency of earthquake damage prediction and the rapid estimation of the seismic fragility of masonry structures, a seismic fragility prediction model for masonry buildings involving gradient boosting machine (GBM), categorical boosting (CatBoost), and feedforward neural network (FNN) methods was developed via intelligent ensemble algorithms and deep learning techniques. Using dynamic response analysis and earthquake risk assessment processes, dynamic responsiveness, hazard analysis, and intelligent model development were conducted on 2,598,972 accelerations monitored by the Wenchuan earthquake (May 12, 2008) array group in China. A dataset of 2211 masonry buildings (investigated by the author) in Dujiangyan city was thoroughly analysed, and a fragility matrix considering the optimised seismic vulnerability (damage) grade was proposed. The input variables of the learning model were the construction year, major story, foundation, function, and instrument intensity; moreover, a sensitivity analysis of the characteristic parameters was conducted. The optimised vulnerability (damage) grade of masonry structures was used as the output variable of the integrated and deep learning models. Using the established database, 20% and 80% of the structural damage instances were stratified and selected for testing and training model development, respectively. An analytical (precision-recall) curve was generated to evaluate the correlation between the predicted parameters of a learning model. To confirm the predictive precision of the developed learning model, a set of seismic fragility comparison curves for masonry buildings considering intelligent and empirical data-driven strategies was generated.

verified_metadata.title: Deep reinforcement learning for autonomous driving decision-making: Algorithms, applications and challenges
verified_metadata.abstract: Autonomous driving has the potential to greatly enhance road safety, traffic efficiency, and overall transportation effectiveness. The decision-making module serves as the core intelligence of the system, producing high-level commands for lane keeping, lane changing, and adaptive cruise control. Deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a pivotal approach in this domain, owing to its capacity to learn driving strategies through environmental interaction. This paper presents a systematic review of decision-making methods based on deep reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicles. It starts by outlining the general architecture of autonomous driving systems and emphasizing the central role of the decision-making module. The paper then explains the theoretical foundations of deep reinforcement learning, along with their applicability in driving decision tasks. Through a range of common driving scenarios, including lane keeping, lane changing, overtaking, and intersection navigation, the paper analyzes the decision-making advantages of deep reinforcement learning in complex and dynamic settings. Furthermore, it addresses key challenges in applying deep reinforcement learning to driving tasks. Compared to existing reviews, this study provides a systematic analysis of deep reinforcement learning in multiple decision-making scenarios for autonomous driving, overcoming the limitation of previous reviews that often focus on single scenarios. Adopting a progressive narrative structure, from single lateral or longitudinal control to increasingly complex tasks involving lateral-longitudinal coordination, it systematically clarifies the characteristics of different deep reinforcement learning algorithms and their applicable conditions. This structured approach helps researchers select appropriate algorithms and fusion strategies when facing driving scenarios of varying complexity.

verified_metadata.title: Separated-variable spectral neural networks with characteristic-frequency multi-level initialization for high-frequency partial differential equations
verified_metadata.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a mesh-free paradigm for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), yet a spectral bias severely limits their ability to resolve high-frequency components of oscillatory problems, and conventional Fourier-feature remedies scale exponentially with dimension. To overcome these limitations, we propose Separated-Variable Spectral Neural Networks (SV-SNN), a physics-informed framework with three core innovations. First, a separated-variable spectral representation expresses multivariate solutions as sums of $N$ separable modes, each a product of univariate adaptive Fourier spectral factors with $K$ frequencies per direction; this unites the dimensional scalability of variable separation with the frequency control of spectral methods, reducing the number of trainable parameters from order ${K}^{d}$ of tensor-product spectral bases to order $dNK$, linear in the dimension $d$, while admitting closed-form spatial derivatives through a hybrid differentiation strategy. Second, a characteristic-frequency multi-level sampling strategy allocates spectral resources across low-, characteristic-, and high-frequency bands, thereby targeting spectral bias and reducing sensitivity to frequency-estimation errors, with the characteristic frequency estimated automatically when not available a priori. Third, an effective-rank diagnostic derived from the singular value decomposition of the residual Jacobian quantifies spectral-bias severity a posteriori, explaining why standard architectures fail on oscillatory problems and guiding architecture selection. Across nine benchmarks—high-wavenumber heat and Helmholtz equations, nonlinear elliptic and Poisson problems on complex domains, and incompressible Navier–Stokes flows—SV-SNN achieves lower error than every competing baseline in matched-budget comparisons, by factors of 1.9 to 94, and remains more accurate even when baselines are afforded 15 to 200 times more parameters. Training completes within 11 to 34 s per problem on a single graphics processing unit. SV-SNN thus provides an accurate and parameter-efficient framework for wave propagation, heat conduction, and incompressible flow simulation. The source code is available at https://github.com/xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding/tree/main/SV-SNN.

title: A cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power in electricity grids, accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) has become crucial for maintaining grid stability. Existing data-driven methods, while proficient in nonlinear modeling, are fundamentally limited by a lack of explicit cross-scale meteorological context. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration for Wind Power Forecasting (GRCMI-WPF), a cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework that incorporates artificial-intelligence-weather-model-derived atmospheric context from global weather models into local ultra-short-term WPF. Through a dedicated Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration (GRCMI) strategy, the framework extracts and injects multi-scale meteorological context surrounding target wind farms as weather-forecast-derived meteorological priors into the forecasting pipeline. Within this framework, we further propose the Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Network (DCFNet), which employs a Hierarchical Cross-modal Alignment Transformer (HCAT) to effectively mitigate the dimensional and semantic disparities between heterogeneous meteorological priors and power series, and a Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Gate (DCF-Gate) to adaptively allocate soft weights between historical power and meteorological modalities, achieving context-aware meteorological-prior-informed fusion. Extensive experiments on five real-world wind farm datasets demonstrate that the proposed GRCMI-WPF consistently outperforms the considered contemporary baselines under a unified evaluation protocol, confirming the value of integrating cross-scale meteorological priors for improving local WPF accuracy.

verified_metadata.title: Embedded artificial intelligence in battery management systems: Pruning and quantization for efficient state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation
verified_metadata.abstract: Online battery management requires accurate state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) estimates within strict memory and timing budgets. To address these constraints, this work investigates how stateful long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with multi-layer perceptron (MLP) heads can be optimized for embedded artificial intelligence (AI), using structured pruning and recurrent-weight quantization to reduce memory and computational costs while retaining estimation accuracy on an STM32H753ZI microcontroller. Using the open Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) Cycle Ageing Dataset, full-precision models provide the accuracy reference against which the compressed variants are evaluated. Long-horizon replay yields mean absolute error (MAE) values of 2.3–2.8 percentage points for SOC and 0.9–1.5 for SOH, showing that compression largely preserves accuracy. The evaluated 30% pruning configuration reduces flash by 37.2% and 43.3% in the available firmware builds and inference time by 42.9% and 44.0% in the recorded hardware-in-the-loop benchmarks for SOC and SOH, respectively. The analytical complexity model relates computational savings to pruning fraction and network dimensions. Quantization reduces flash by 49.7% and 55.9% relative to the respective full-precision models, but raises runtime in the mixed-precision implementation. Together, the study provides a reproducible reference for resource-efficient embedded battery-state estimation.

title: Automated measurement of rural highway widths using transformer-based models and point cloud analysis
abstract: This study presents an automated method for extracting roadway width measurements and lane counts from Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-derived point clouds of rural highways and evaluates the reliability of measurements obtained from point clouds labeled by a Transformer-based point classification model. The proposed approach was evaluated on five highway segments in Alberta, Canada, encompassing both multilane and two-lane, two-way (TLTW) highways. From an artificial intelligence perspective, the study proposes a hierarchical Transformer-based semantic segmentation strategy with a geometry-aware measurement algorithm to estimate traveled way widths, shoulder widths, and lane counts directly from three-dimensional point cloud data. Automated measurements derived from manually labeled point clouds demonstrated strong agreement with manual reference measurements, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.99 and mean absolute errors on the order of only a few centimeters for traveled way and shoulder widths. When applied to point clouds automatically segmented by the Transformer-based models, the framework continued to produce reliable results, with width estimation errors generally remaining within sub-meter ranges. Paired statistical tests indicated no statistically significant differences between automated and reference measurements at the 95% confidence level. Multiple lane count estimation strategies were evaluated, with lane-surface-based methods demonstrating increased robustness in scenarios where pavement markings were partially occluded or inconsistently detected. The results confirm that Transformer-based semantic segmentation, when combined with geometry-aware post-processing, can support accurate and scalable roadway geometry extraction from mobile LiDAR data. The proposed framework reduces reliance on manual surveys and offers a practical solution for automated roadway inventory generation and data-driven infrastructure management.

verified_metadata.title: A component-aware progressive transfer learning method for wind power forecasting in newly built wind farms
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for wind farm operation and grid integration. However, newly built wind farms often have limited historical data, restricting the performance of data-driven models. Under data scarcity, conventional deep learning models tend to overfit, while direct transfer learning may introduce irrelevant source-domain information when source and target farms differ. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a component-aware progressive transfer learning method for newly built wind farms. Relevant source wind farms are first selected based on combined power-sequence and meteorological similarity to reduce negative transfer. The original power sequence is then decomposed into trend and fluctuation components, which are modeled using a multilayer perceptron and a conditional generative adversarial network, respectively, and integrated through attention-based fusion. Rather than fine-tuning the entire model simultaneously, the proposed strategy progressively adapts the trend predictor, fluctuation model, and fusion module. Experiments on three newly built wind farm datasets yielded root mean square errors of 0.8850, 2.5060, and 5.0429 MW, representing reductions of 35.29%, 25.71%, and 33.03% over the best-performing benchmarks. On a United States dataset, the method achieved a root mean square error of 0.6543 MW and a coefficient of determination of 0.9870 for 15-min-ahead forecasting, while retaining its advantage over the comparison methods for forecasts 30 and 60 min ahead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of source relevance selection, component-specific modeling, and progressive transfer learning under limited target-domain data.

title: Uncertainty-aware prediction of asphalt pavement roughness using probabilistic machine learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of asphalt pavement deterioration is critical for data-driven infrastructure asset management. However, conventional data-driven models commonly provide deterministic estimates, offering limited insight into prediction confidence. This limitation restricts their application in risk-aware decision-making, where understanding the reliability of each prediction is essential. This study addresses this challenge by developing an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting pavement roughness using data from the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A curated dataset of 1,246 test sections across 50 states in the United States was compiled, covering diverse climate regions, structural configurations, traffic loading, and surface characteristics. Probabilistic modeling approaches, including Bayesian neural networks and Gaussian process regression, were used to predict pavement roughness while generating prediction intervals. Deterministic approaches, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, and artificial neural networks, were also developed under the same validation and optimization framework for benchmarking. All models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and optimized using a Bayesian optimization framework. The results showed that extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest point prediction accuracy, while Gaussian process regression and Bayesian neural networks provided competitive accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9133 and 0.9226, respectively, along with explicit uncertainty estimates. Gaussian process regression also demonstrated a reliable uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage of 95% prediction intervals ranging from 88.89% to 96.31% across climate regions. Initial roughness, rutting, and cracking were identified as the dominant predictors. Regional analyses further revealed generally lower prediction errors in non-freezing regions, and spatial analyses identified geographic variations in pavement deterioration.

verified_metadata.title: Safety evaluation of new energy three-electric systems using enhanced physics-informed neural networks
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate safety-state measurement of the three-electric system in new energy vehicles is essential for ensuring reliable and secure operation. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted safety measurement framework that integrates a searchable encryption mechanism with Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (EPINNs). In the proposed framework, the searchable encryption module supports privacy-preserving storage and retrieval of multi-source measurement data, while EPINNs serve as the core Artificial Intelligence (AI) model for multi-parameter state estimation and fault identification. A lightweight searchable encryption scheme based on block mapping is first designed to achieve feature-level obfuscation and protect sensitive measurement data. Then, an EPINNs-based state estimation model is developed by incorporating data-driven learning, subsystem physical constraints, and energy-consistency terms to enhance robustness under noisy sensor data. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves improved performance compared with conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models in battery state-of-health estimation, motor fault detection under injected fault conditions, and microgrid load measurement, with the motor fault detection accuracy exceeding 95% under the tested conditions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and secure technical solution for intelligent safety monitoring of new energy vehicle three-electric systems.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-guided interpretable machine learning for explicit resistance equation discovery in concrete penetration
verified_metadata.abstract: Classical Forrestal penetration calculations are attractive because they are explicit, but their empirical strength-only resistance term is too restrictive for heterogeneous concrete-penetration data. This study derives a closed-form resistance equation from a governed literature dataset, reducing 497 raw records from 41 source blocks to 443 useable records from 37 sources through duplicate removal, governed density completion, deep-penetration filtering, and descriptor-only anomaly screening. Forrestal inversion maps each measured penetration depth to an operator-consistent effective resistance target described by mechanics-informed dimensionless descriptors. The artificial-intelligence contribution is a constrained equation-discovery workflow in which a categorical gradient-boosting model learns the nonlinear resistance surface, Shapley additive explanations restrict the analytical term family, and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization with bound constraints identifies equation coefficients under a forward penetration-depth objective. The engineering contribution is a 16-term explicit resistance law that replaces the empirical resistance relation inside the Forrestal operator while retaining its deterministic calculation form. On the 89-record held-out set, the equation gives a coefficient of determination of 0.9543 and a mean absolute percentage error of 14.88%, compared with 0.9206 and 24.44% for classical Forrestal and 0.9551 and 13.95% for the nonlinear resistance-reference model; its mean prediction-to-measurement ratio is 0.984. Repeated random, source-grouped, strength-stratified, out-of-distribution, input-uncertainty, and density-robustness tests bound the useable domain. The 80–120 MPa interval remains cautionary because of weaker held-out accuracy and limited cross-source support.

title: Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-the-art attention-based baseline, favoring recall and missed-detection reduction at the cost of a higher false-alarm rate while consuming 13 microjoules (µJ) in low-power mode and requiring 370 microseconds (µs) in high-performance mode. This marks one of the first experimental validations of unsupervised on-device vibration diagnostics. Supervised counterparts achieve 96.06 % binary and 91.5 % multiclass accuracy, rivaling Residual Network (ResNet) with 1 5 . 8 × fewer parameters, at less than 235 µJ and not more than 6.3 ms (ms) inference. Relative to existing edge implementations, our approach is one to three orders of magnitude more energy-efficient and two orders faster, unlocking AI-enabled autonomous, low-latency predictive maintenance for large-scale distributed infrastructure monitoring.

title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. In the first stage, a novel multi-objective Optuna is developed to optimize the decomposition parameters using two criteria of compactness, bandwidth, and peakedness of a signal's frequency spectrum. The proposed methodology is utilized for hyperparameter tuning of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and De-mixing Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (D-MVMD) techniques. This enables an optimal data decomposition process by eliminating the need for manual parameter selection. In the second stage, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach, SHAPley Additive Explanations (SHAP), is used to identify the most influential components and analyze their interactions. These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to standalone forecasting models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models to forecast. In the final stage, a comprehensive Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to quantify uncertainties and perform reliability analysis. The SHAP-based feature selection reduced the input variables from 37 to 48 decomposed components to a single dominant predictor while maintaining nearly identical predictive accuracy across all forecast horizons, significantly lowering computational costs. Among the models, the SSA-RVFL demonstrated superior performance, with lower computational cost and the highest forecasting accuracy across all time horizons. This model achieved the highest Index of Agreement (IA: 0.81-1) and determination coefficient (R 2 : 0.49-0.98), and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE: 0.04-0.33) across stations and horizons. In addition, the results confirm operational reliability exceeding 88% for forecasts up to 6 h ahead. Overall, the fully optimized SSA integrated with the SHAP-RVFL-MCS results provides a robust framework for enhancing decision-making in coastal hazard and wave energy planning.

verified_metadata.title: Cryogenic distortion compensation in guided ultrasonic waves using a Physics-Informed Generative Adversarial Network
verified_metadata.abstract:
Reusable launch vehicles undergo severe thermal cycling, and cryogenic storage conditions introduce strong, nonlinear distortions in guided ultrasonic wave signals used for structural health monitoring. These temperature-induced effects obscure damage sensitive features and limit the robustness of both conventional compensation techniques and purely data driven learning models.

This paper proposes a physics informed machine learning framework, termed the Guided Wave Physics-Informed Generative Adversarial Network, to compensate cryogenic guided ultrasonic wave distortions in a physically consistent manner. The artificial intelligence component is realized through generative adversarial learning and is applied to cryogenic guided-wave temperature compensation The model adopts a residual generative formulation in the Hilbert-envelope domain and integrates adversarial sequence learning with wave-physics priors through curvature based regularization and peak morphology constraints. These physics-informed components explicitly suppress nonphysical temporal artifacts and preserve the modal structure of guided-wave responses, enabling stable compensation across varying cryogenic conditions.

Experiments conducted on an aluminum alloy plate under liquid-nitrogen cooling–heating cycles demonstrate that GW-PIGAN achieves high-fidelity reconstruction while maintaining consistent performance across varying reference temperatures. Compared with purely data-driven baselines, the proposed physics-informed formulation exhibits improved stability, physical plausibility, and generalization under extreme thermal conditions.

By embedding guided-wave physics into generative learning, the proposed framework provides a practical and interpretable physics-informed machine learning approach for cryogenic structural health monitoring. It also establishes a methodological basis for future monitoring applications in reusable aerospace structures under extreme cryogenic conditions.

verified_metadata.title: A defect and multi-physics informed neural network for fatigue life prediction in friction stir welded additive manufacturing AlSi7Mg
verified_metadata.abstract: Additively manufactured aluminium alloys joined by friction stir welding exhibit great potential for large-scale structural applications, yet their fatigue life prediction remains challenging due to the complex influence of internal defects and process-induced microstructural heterogeneity. To address this issue, a defect-based, physics-informed neural network framework was proposed for fatigue life prediction of additively manufactured AlSi7Mg friction stir welded joints. A multi-route physics-informed modeling strategy is introduced, incorporating physical prior knowledge through feature engineering, loss function design, and adaptive feature weighting. Four data augmentation methods are employed to enhance data diversity and model robustness, and the results show that among these approaches, Precise Physics Law (PPL) yields the best overall performance. The proposed Defect and Multi-Physics Coupled Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) dynamically adjusts the weights of physical loss terms based on defect and multi-physics features, achieving a better balance between data-driven learning and physical consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that the DM-PINN model outperforms both conventional artificial neural networks and standard physics-informed neural networks in terms of prediction accuracy, generalization capability, and physical interpretability. The model successfully predicts conditional fatigue limits under different processing conditions with errors below 15%, providing a reliable tool for fatigue life assessment and process optimization of defect-sensitive additive manufacturing components.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed neural networks for proportional delay differential equations: Forward and inverse problems
verified_metadata.abstract: Proportional delay differential equations model systems that depend on proportionally scaled historical states and arise in applications including astrophysics, engineering, and biology. However, proportional delays may span a wide, time-varying range and depend on states arbitrarily close to the initial time. Consequently, conventional discretization-based methods, particularly finite-difference-type approaches, require careful treatment of delayed arguments and can be computationally challenging. This study develops a unified physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for forward simulation and inverse parameter identification in proportional delay ordinary and partial differential equations. The framework incorporates differential equation residuals, initial or boundary conditions, and observational data into a composite loss function. An adaptive weighting strategy balances competing loss terms, while two-stage optimization and a multi-stage residual correction procedure improve training stability and accuracy. Numerical experiments show stable, high-precision solutions for highly oscillatory equations, the handling of challenging high-order nonlinear cases, and accurate identification of unknown delay parameters and coefficients under noisy or sparse data. Under stated assumptions, the Appendix further shows that a sufficiently small physics-informed loss yields a small solution approximation error. The proposed framework thus provides a mesh-free, effective, and theoretically supported approach for proportional-delay systems when conventional discretization-based methods are difficult to apply.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed deep learning for few-shot damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites under thermal variations
verified_metadata.abstract: Guided wave (GW)-based damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites is fundamentally challenged by thermal variations and sparse sensor configurations, which induce severe baseline distortions and imaging artifacts. Traditional physical algorithms suffer from geometric ambiguity, while purely data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) models are hindered by opaque interpretability and prohibitive data dependency. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework, an artificial-intelligence-driven approach, for few-shot damage localization under thermal variations. The network is architected with a dual-stream input design, comprising a data-driven layer enhanced by a one-dimensional coordinate attention (1D-CA) mechanism and a physics-informed layer built upon a differentiable time-of-flight (TOF) physical imaging layer. A hybrid physics-constrained loss function is formulated to suppress non-physical artifacts and enforce physical consistency. GW signals are experimentally collected from manufactured CFRP composite plates, and a comparative investigation is performed to thoroughly assess the PIDL performance. Results indicate that:(1) The presence of physical penalties effectively mitigates artifacts and achieves robust localization across thermal gradients; (2) The model demonstrates superior spatial generalization that the integration of acoustic physical constraints acts as a crucial regularization mechanism, maintaining a highly accurate mean relative error (MRE) of 3.88% on completely unseen damage coordinates; (3) By implementing a few-shot transfer learning strategy, the PIDL model shows adaptability for dynamic operational environments (45 degrees Celsius (°C)-75 degrees Celsius (°C)). This work offers a physically interpretable and data-efficient paradigm for structural health monitoring (SHM) in dynamic operational environments.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed transformer for pseudo-color infrared image super-resolution with application to insulator detection
verified_metadata.abstract: The accelerated deployment of smart grids has intensified the need for real-time insulator monitoring and health diagnostics, particularly for the early detection of thermal faults. While infrared thermography enables non-contact fault localization, industrial thermal imagers are often constrained by insufficient spatial resolution and inherent sensor artifacts, compromising both image quality and thermal interpretability. To address information compression and undersampling while recovering relative thermal-pattern information and structural representations, we introduce the Fidelity-aware InfraRed Enhancement Network (FIRE-Net), a physics-informed transformer for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven super-resolution of pseudo-color infrared images. The model incorporates an infrared denoising block to suppress sensor noise, employs learnable unsharp masking and high-frequency attention modules to recover structural details, and is supervised by a thermal-consistency loss function that constrains relative thermal patterns in a normalized palette-derived temperature-proxy domain. On the insulator infrared test set, FIRE-Net achieves peak signal-to-noise ratio values of 31.0021 dB (dB) (×2) and 27.6765 dB (×4), with structural similarity index scores of 0.9143 and 0.8591, respectively. The model also improves downstream detection performance, attaining mean average precision at intersection over union = 0.50 values of 0.857 (×2) and 0.904 (×4), representing improvements of 0.102 and 0.111 over the low-resolution baseline. Its cross-scenario performance is further evaluated on a hold-out photovoltaic dataset. We further analyze computational efficiency and outline future research directions, including domain-extended training and lightweight deployment. The results demonstrate that incorporating physics-inspired priors into super-resolution models effectively improves normalized temperature-proxy consistency and practical detection performance. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Sevil-cy/FIRE-Net.

verified_metadata.title: A physics-informed cascaded learning framework for end-to-end stress–strain prediction of recycled aggregate concrete under axial compression
verified_metadata.abstract: The reliable prediction of the full constitutive response in recycled aggregate concrete is frequently compromised by the high stochasticity of material properties and the unavailability of peak parameters during the structural design phase. This study develops a two-stage sequential learning framework for the end-to-end reconstruction of stress–strain trajectories without requiring predefined peak inputs. The architecture integrates gradient boosting surrogate models for peak stress and strain estimation with a physics-informed long short-term memory network for full-curve generation. By embedding failure constraints based on energy conservation alongside monotonicity and boundary priors into the learning process, the framework effectively suppresses non-physical behavior in the softening regime. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed system exhibits superior robustness and morphological fidelity, achieving a curve-level coefficient of determination of 0.923 and a mean dynamic time warping distance of 27.91. The framework remains stable under ten percent data contamination and utilizes quantile regression to provide quantified prediction intervals that address predictive uncertainty. Furthermore, analysis of the generated curves identifies the enhanced deformation capacity of high-replacement recycled aggregates can compensate for strength loss in high-porosity matrices. The energy toughness ratio is primarily governed by the aggregate replacement ratio rather than matrix strength, providing a standardized measure for the brittle-to-ductile transition. This research offers a computationally efficient numerical tool for characterizing sustainable concrete, ensuring that predicted responses are both mathematically optimized and thermodynamically consistent with fundamental failure mechanisms.

verified_metadata.title: Cognitive and mental state-aware autonomous driving with multi-task electroencephalography-based deep learning framework for hazard perception, trust prediction, cognitive load estimation, and brain–computer interface integration
verified_metadata.abstract: Autonomous driving systems are increasingly required to operate safely in dynamic and cognitively complex environments, yet the cognitive and mental states of vehicle occupants remain underexplored relative to vehicle perception and planning. This paper presents a multi-task electroencephalography (EEG, the recording of brain electrical activity)-based deep learning framework addressing four cognitive-state tasks relevant to autonomous driving: hazard perception, trust prediction, cognitive load estimation via EEG and heart-rate-variability (HRV) fusion, and brain-computer interface (BCI) motor-imagery classification. The framework is first developed on physiologically parameterized synthetic EEG signals derived from the structural characteristics of five open-source datasets (DEAP, DREAMER, PhysioNet, SEED, OpenNeuro); five classifiers — random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), support vector machine, a convolutional-recurrent neural network (CNN-RNN), and an EEG Transformer — attain near-ceiling accuracy on this synthetic benchmark, reflecting the separability built into the simulation rather than real-world decodability. To test this directly, the framework is subsequently validated on genuine human recordings from PhysioNet (21 subjects, motor imagery) and DREAMER (23 subjects, valence/arousal ratings used as proxies for trust-related affect and cognitive load, with electrocardiogram-derived HRV for multimodal fusion). On real data, accuracy falls to 51%–77% within-subject and to 44%–59% — at or below chance for some tasks — under subject-independent evaluation; permutation testing and a spectral comparison against the synthetic signals help explain this gap. Real HRV fusion yields a modest but genuine gain for cognitive-load estimation (+4.8 percentage points over EEG alone), unlike the synthetic-data result. No open dataset with a hazard-perception paradigm was available for real-data validation, which is reported here as an explicit limitation. Together, these synthetic and real-data results provide an artificial-intelligence-based benchmark for neurophysiological human-state monitoring in autonomous driving that is transparent about what is demonstrated versus what remains to be validated before real-time, in-vehicle deployment.

verified_metadata.title: Experimental and machine learning-assisted design of damaged reinforced concrete beams strengthened using carbon fiber reinforced polymer and fan-spike anchors
verified_metadata.abstract: Reinforced concrete (RC) beams often sustain flexural damage during their service life due to overloading or environmental degradation, requiring effective repair solutions; however, strengthening with carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) layers is limited by premature debonding of the CFRP from the concrete surface. In this paper, CFRP fan spikes were employed for anchoring the CFRP layers at the RC damaged beam ends. Engineered cementitious composites (ECC) were employed to form a crack control layer beneath the beam and in the damaged areas. Six RC beams were studied experimentally, analytically and by machine learning methods including control specimens, damaged specimens subjected to 25% and 50% of the maximum bending capacity, and damaged specimens strengthened with the CFRP fan spike system. Experimental results showed that the fan spike anchors efficiently prevent CFRP separation while also repairing and enhancing the mechanical properties of damaged RC beams. The proposed reinforcement technique greatly enhances stiffness and reduces crack width, making it a reliable option for repairing damaged RC beams. Analytical models supported the experimental findings and also an optimized machine learning (ML) model, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), can predict the unseen experimental response with 0.6-6.7% errors.

verified_metadata.title: A hybrid convolutional neural network and transformer model based on segmented sparse attention for medical image segmentation
verified_metadata.abstract: Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in clinical diagnosis and treatment. However, existing deep-learning methods can suffer from semantic gaps in encoder-decoder architectures, while the quadratic cost of self-attention limits computational scalability as the input sequence length increases. To address these issues, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network and Transformer-based model, Segmented Sparse Transformer Network, abbreviated as SegSparseTransNet. The innovation lies in: (1) We propose the Segmented Sparse Attention (SSA) mechanism to reduce computational complexity and ensure the global perception ability of the model. (2) We design the Dynamic Skip Attention (DSA) block to optimize feature fusion between the encoder and decoder. (3) We present the Cross-Modal Fusion (CMF) block to enhance the expressive power of advanced semantic features. Experiments on several medical image datasets show that the proposed SegSparseTransNet outperforms existing methods in multiple key metrics, such as mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and mean Dice Coefficient (mDice), demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness in medical image segmentation tasks. The code is available at: https://github.com/wuxianghu/SegSparseTransNet.git.

title: Computationally sustainable hybrid deep learning for month-ahead solar–wind power forecasting in two Saudi cities
abstract: This paper implements artificial intelligence for month-ahead renewable power forecasting by fusing synchronized solar and wind information from the Sakaka Solar Plant and Dumat Al-Jandal Wind Farm in Saudi Arabia. Ten hybrid deep-learning architectures are evaluated under a common temporal framework using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, coefficient of determination, training time, and computational carbon dioxide emissions. The convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model with attention achieves the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 80, a root mean squared error of 129, a mean absolute percentage error of 6.6%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.87. The Temporal Fusion Transformer provides the strongest accuracy-sustainability compromise under the 70:30 Sustainable Artificial Intelligence score, while the wavelet-convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit model records the lowest training footprint at 768 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent. A 10,000-draw perturbation sensitivity analysis of the error and emission values confirms that the preferred deployment model is decision-dependent rather than universally dominant: the Temporal Fusion Transformer is most frequently top-ranked under the central weighting, whereas carbon-heavier or carbon-lighter alternatives become preferred as decision weights change. The contribution is therefore system-level: the framework integrates cross-resource data fusion, leakage-aware long-horizon evaluation, carbon-aware model selection, Pareto analysis, and explicit decision-robustness testing. Reported carbon reductions refer to model computation and should not be interpreted as measured reductions in grid curtailment or citywide operational emissions.

verified_metadata.title: Local evolution decoupling paradigm for neural network constitutive models of history-dependent materials: Theory, architecture, and applications to shape memory polymers
verified_metadata.abstract: The mechanical response of history-dependent materials depends on loading paths and thermomechanical histories, rendering neural network-based constitutive modeling challenging. Existing methods typically establish global memory based on historical sequences, requiring large model scales and extensive training data. Targeting materials whose states can be fully described by finite-dimensional internal variables, this paper proposes a Local Decoupling Evolution Operator Network (LDEONet) grounded in the Markovian property. The proposed framework explicitly decomposes the internal variable evolution model into evolution direction and evolution intensity. Using the thermomechanical cycle of shape memory polymers as a case study, eight models are trained, and a series of experiments are designed, including path generalization tests, discretization generalization tests, and decoupling ablation studies. Experimental results demonstrate that the model contains 242 trainable parameters and requires only about 1/175 of the training curves compared to sequence-based models, while making predictions without needing historical memory. The model maintains accurate predictions across various unseen loading paths and unseen step sizes, and the decoupling architecture is shown to provide structural guarantees for generalization. The Local Decoupling Evolution Operator Network thus offers a lightweight modeling approach with both path generalization and discretization generalization capabilities for history-dependent materials that possess explicit internal variable models.

title: A lightweight deep learning architecture for crack segmentation in structural health monitoring
abstract: Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.

title: A multi-stage graph-conditioned probabilistic forecaster with dual-stream temporal encoding for wind speed forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is a critical foundation for wind power dispatch and the grid integration of renewable energy. The non-stationary fluctuations in wind speed time series, the spatially dependent variations among multiple wind turbines, and forecasting uncertainties continue to pose significant challenges for wind farm-level forecasting. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence framework for multi-turbine wind speed forecasting, termed the Multi-Stage Graph-Conditioned Probabilistic Forecaster (MGPF).The model fuses prior graphs and data-driven graphs at the node-pair level, enabling differentiated spatial connection representations for different wind turbine pairs. Simultaneously, it sets up two candidate temporal encoding paths, a Generative Pre-trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) and a lightweight Patch, and determines the appropriate configuration based on comparative results across different datasets. Spatio-temporal cross-attention further establishes interactions between spatial and temporal features, while the probabilistic prediction head constructs prediction intervals by estimating the mean and variance of future wind speeds. Experimental results on two wind farm datasets with markedly different scales show that MGPF reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) by 35.56% and 3.92%, respectively, compared to the corresponding optimal baselines, experiments at the Kelmarsh external wind farm further validate the model's applicability under different wind farm data conditions. Probabilistic forecast results show that MGPF outperforms the probabilistic baseline overall in terms of probability distribution fitting and forecast interval quality, encoder and pre-training control experiments also validate the effectiveness of the time-encoding design.

Probabilistic forecast results show that MGPF outperforms the probabilistic baseline overall in terms of probability distribution fitting and forecast interval quality, encoder and pre-training control experiments also validate the effectiveness of the time-encoding design.

verified_metadata.title: A condition-aware adaptive physics-informed residual network for chiller energy consumption modeling
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate chiller energy consumption prediction is critical for enhancing heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) system efficiency and building energy conservation. However, existing models exhibit limited generalization under variable operating conditions and sparse data, and conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) struggle with adaptive physical weight adjustment and deep network convergence. To address these issues, this study proposes a condition-aware adaptive physics-informed residual network (CAA-PIResNet) for chiller energy consumption modeling. A one-dimensional residual network (ResNet) is adopted as the backbone to extract nonlinear features and alleviate the vanishing gradient problem. The Stoecker semi-empirical model provides a chiller-specific physical prior, while a fuzzy neural network (FNN)-based condition-aware mechanism adjusts the data loss and Stoecker-based physics-guided loss weights according to operating conditions. Experiments are conducted to evaluate prediction accuracy, physical interpretability, computational cost, noise robustness, data efficiency, and generalization performance. Results demonstrate that CAA-PIResNet outperforms benchmark models. When trained using only 10% of the available training data, CAA-PIResNet remains stable and achieves at least 12.05% lower mean absolute error (MAE) than the benchmark models. In part-load-ratio (PLR) hold-out experiments, it reduces MAE and root mean square error (RMSE) by 8.21% and 10.05%, respectively, compared with the Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN). The learned adaptive weights and semi-empirical coefficients demonstrate operating-condition-dependent loss balancing and stable physical parameter calibration, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed semi-empirical prior and adaptive mechanism.

title: Structured variational quantum control for spin-chain state transfer: Expressivity, trainability, and robustness
abstract: We propose a hybrid variational framework for quantum optimal control of high-fidelity state transfer in spin chains. The continuous-time control problem is reformulated as a trainable Trotterized quantum circuit, where drift dynamics are encoded by fixed two-qubit interaction blocks and control fields by parameterized on-site R Z rotations. This provides a physics-informed variational ansatz directly connecting the Hamiltonian model to hybrid quantum–classical optimization. We compare two control parameterizations: an expressive local scheme with site-wise trainable parameters and a compact global scheme with shared parameters per Trotter layer. Numerical experiments on XXZ spin chains show that both achieve near-unit fidelity for the main noiseless end-to-end transfer task. The reduced optimization dimension of the global parameterization provides favorable optimization behavior for several larger systems, while additional source–target experiments demonstrate that this advantage is task dependent and that local control can perform better for interior transfers. Studies under depolarizing and dephasing noise show that relative noise-induced degradation depends on system size, noise strength, and noise model, with no uniform robustness ordering. Additional analyses examine circuit depth, initialization sensitivity, empirical gradient statistics, interaction anisotropy, Trotter error, exact piecewise-constant control, and hardware execution. Overall, the results reveal a trade-off between control expressivity, optimization dimensionality, task structure, and noise sensitivity, providing a physically grounded framework for structured variational quantum control of distributed quantum systems.

verified_metadata.title: Uncertainty-aware surrogate-assisted optimization for concrete mix design using data-centric and physics-informed learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Concrete mix design is a nonlinear, constraint-sensitive problem in which empirical approaches require repeated adjustments and rarely account explicitly for predictive uncertainty. This study develops an artificial intelligence-based, uncertainty-aware surrogate-assisted optimization framework for concrete mixtures under engineering constraints. A database of 1508 experimental observations from heterogeneous sources was harmonized through physical plausibility screening and evaluated using leakage-resistant, composition-family-grouped validation. An artificial neural network surrogate was optimized through hyperparameter search and enhanced with physics-informed features and synthetic data generated by a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network, followed by local real-data support filtering, with physical plausibility and cross-model consistency assessed as complementary credibility diagnostics. Predictive disagreement across an ensemble was empirically calibrated and incorporated into the strength constraint through a conservative lower bound. On an independent test set, the final hybrid surrogate achieved a mean absolute error of 2.32 MPa, a root mean squared error of 3.16 MPa, a coefficient of determination of 0.951, and a mean absolute percentage error of 9.28%. Constrained cost minimization employed particle swarm optimization, a genetic algorithm, and simulated annealing. Computational candidate mixtures were identified for ordinary 25-MPa concrete, supplementary cementitious material-based 25-MPa concrete, and high-strength 65-MPa concrete. For supplementary cementitious material-based candidates, predicted cement content decreased by approximately 19–21% while satisfying surrogate-based constraints. The high-strength candidates exhibited greater uncertainty and cross-model disagreement; two of three failed the cross-model target check. These findings support computational mixture screening, not experimentally verified performance; targeted laboratory testing remains necessary before implementation.

title: Artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse design of low-carbon concrete under carbonation constraints
abstract: This study develops and tests an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design workflow for supplementary-cementitious-material-blended concrete, with artificial intelligence applied to surrogate prediction, uncertainty quantification, dosage-effect interpretation, and multi-objective candidate generation. Optuna-tuned feedforward neural networks were trained on four open datasets and coupled with split conformal prediction, continuous-treatment forest analysis, and non-dominated multi-objective search. The source-aware compressive-strength model achieved a mean absolute error of 7.20 megapascals and a coefficient of determination of 0.687. Under standard cross-validation, embodied carbon achieved a mean absolute error of 2.41 and a coefficient of determination of 0.999, while carbonation depth achieved a mean absolute error of 2.56 millimetres and a coefficient of determination of 0.847. A leakage audit showed that the exceptional embodied-carbon fit is largely attributable to an almost deterministic relation between mixture quantities and the carbon target, although performance was sensitive to source grouping. Continuous-treatment re-analysis showed substantial pre-adjustment imbalance and wide ninety-five-percent effect intervals, so the dosage results are interpreted conditionally rather than as universal causal effects. Three-objective optimization produced seventy-two computational candidates; sixteen, or 22.2 percent, had negative raw carbonation predictions and were excluded from representative reporting. A physically non-negative balanced candidate predicted 75.8 megapascals strength, 141.7 embodied carbon, and 0.064 millimetres carbonation depth. Applicability-domain analysis showed that none of the optimized candidates lay inside a strict joint ninety-five-percent domain for all retained endpoints, emphasizing that the generated mixtures are hypotheses for laboratory validation rather than design-ready prescriptions.

title: A distributed intelligent decision-making method for game-based adversarial pursuit-evasion of moving target by multiple unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: To address the challenges of slow decision-making, insufficient adaptability, and limited generalization in tracking moving targets by multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) within complex airspace, this paper proposes an Intrinsic-curiosity and Attention-based Multi-Agent Hierarchical Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (IA-MAHDDPG) algorithm for multi-UAV pursuit-evasion confrontation and intelligent decision-making. First, an autonomous confrontation engine is constructed according to the requirements of the multi-UAV pursuit game, and a decision-coupled trajectory prediction network is designed, which incorporates inter-UAV cooperative information during target trajectory prediction, thereby enabling multiple UAVs to accurately track moving targets based on the current situation. Second, building upon Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), an intrinsic curiosity reward and a self-attention mechanism are integrated: the curiosity-based novelty is extended from single-agent evaluation to decentralized cooperative evaluation among multiple UAVs, and the intrinsic reward is adaptively weighted in a task-relevant manner, allowing the UAVs to focus on key subtasks while effectively incentivizing target tracking and capture while avoiding excessive exploration. Finally, by incorporating hierarchical reinforcement learning, a semi-Markov decision process is introduced to construct a hierarchical autonomous decision-making architecture, which enables the reuse and transfer of subpolicies and improves the generalization and stability of the pursuit-evasion confrontation. Comparative experiments, generalization tests, and multi-target round-up experiments under various scenarios demonstrate that IA-MAHDDPG achieves good overall performance in convergence speed, encirclement success rate, and generalization capability. The proposed method achieves efficient and stable multi-UAV cooperative tracking and encirclement in dynamic and complex environments, thereby better meeting the requirements of realistic UAV flight missions.

title: Unraveling the neurotoxic mechanisms of tranexamic acid in epilepsy induction: a network toxicology and molecular docking approach
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid, an antifibrinolytic drug, is effective for surgical hemostasis and bleeding-related disorders but may induce neurotoxicity, such as epilepsy. The mechanisms driving TXA-induced epilepsy remain poorly understood, as traditional toxicology approaches fall short in capturing its complex toxicity profile. This study employs network toxicology and molecular docking to elucidate the multi-target molecular mechanisms of TXA-induced epilepsy, aiming to enhance its safe clinical application. METHODS: TXA toxicity was predicted using ADMETlab2.0, PROTOX3.0, toxCSM, and ADMET-AI, with SMILES sequences obtained from PubChem, and a TXA target library was constructed using databases such as ChEMBL. EP-related targets were screened from databases such as GeneCards, and target intersections were analyzed using R software. Networks were constructed using Cytoscape and STRING, with GO and KEGG analyses performed to investigate molecular pathways. Molecular docking was conducted using the CB-Dock2 platform to analyze TXA binding to core targets. RESULTS: TXA poses a neurotoxicity risk, with 51 intersecting targets identified between TXA and EP, among which GABRA1, GABBR2, GABRA5, GABRA2, and GAD1 exhibited the greatest relevance. Analysis revealed that TXA induces EP by disrupting GABA signaling and synaptic function. The PPI network confirmed five core targets, and GO and KEGG analyses elucidated their roles in neural suppression. Molecular docking demonstrated stable binding of TXA to these targets, with Vina scores ranging from - 5.2 to - 6.9. CONCLUSION: This study elucidates the mechanisms of TXA-induced EP through network toxicology and molecular docking, confirming its interference with GABA-related targets and neural suppression functions. The study overcomes the limitations of traditional toxicology, providing a scientific basis for the safe use of TXA and prevention of neurotoxicity.

title: Accelerated brain aging in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and its prognostic associations: a cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease, appearing to be associated with accelerated brain aging. Although increased brain age has been associated with mortality risk in older adults, it remains unclear how the brain aging process is accelerated in ALS and how this acceleration relates to patient prognosis. METHODS: One hundred seventy sporadic ALS patients and 84 age- and sex-matched HCs were recruited and underwent neuropsychological tests and T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. A brain-age prediction model was developed using a 3D-Conformer deep learning framework trained on 4310 healthy T1-weighted MRI data from public datasets. Brain age was predicted in HCs and ALS patients, and then the predicted-age difference (PAD = brain age-chronological age) was calculated. In the ALS cohort, the neuroanatomical association of PAD was examined, and cell-specific gene expression of PAD-related volume loss was analyzed using transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas. Associations between PAD, neuropsychological performance, clinical characteristics, and survival outcomes were further evaluated in ALS patients. RESULTS: The brain aging process was accelerated in ALS by an average PAD of 1.77 years, which was predominantly associated with a widespread loss of gray matter volume. Cell-specific gene expression analyses showed microglia, inhibitory neurons, endothelial cells, and pericytes as significant contributors to the accelerated brain aging in ALS, with endothelial cells and pericytes being essential for constructing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and microglia being involved in neuroinflammation. The acceleration in brain aging was more prominent in older patients and was associated with cognitive impairments. Notably, older brain age at initial diagnosis was an independent risk factor for death (hazard ratio, 1.026; 95% CI [1.008, 1.045]) and was associated with shorter survival and more rapid disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: Accelerated brain aging is common in ALS; this could be hypothesized to be associated with the interplay between BBB breakdown and neuroinflammation, leading to gray matter degeneration. Furthermore, older brain age at initial diagnosis is associated with worse clinical outcomes. These findings suggest that therapeutic strategies targeting neuroinflammation and BBB integrity may help attenuate accelerated brain aging and improve prognosis.

title: Expanding access to cerebrovascular imaging with routine MRI for pre-surgical assessment of intracranial tumor patients: an AI model development and multi-center validation study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiography is the gold standard for assessing the relationship between cerebral arteries and intracranial tumors, but its use is limited in low- and middle-income countries for various reasons. Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (T1C) is much more widely available, yet an accurate vessel segmentation method on this modality has not been established. METHODS: In this multicenter study, 1174 cases from four private institutions and one public dataset were used to train and evaluate an automatic segmentation model for intracranial arteries on T1C. Performance was assessed with Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), recall, and Hausdorff distance (HD) on both internal and external test sets. Prospective clinical validation was performed using paired time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA) to compare our model with the gold standard and to investigate the reasons for discrepancies. RESULTS: In internal test, the model achieved DSC = 0.886 ± 0.015, recall = 0.878 ± 0.033, and HD = 10.220 ± 3.821 mm. External test demonstrated robust generalization across four independent institutions, with DSC ranging from 0.859 to 0.884, recall ranging from 0.885 to 0.802, and HD ranging from 9.867 mm to 13.089 mm. Prospectively, clinical evaluation revealed the proposed model identified all target vessels and covered 88.5% of total vessel visible on TOF-MRA, provided a practical anatomic roadmap, but underestimated vessel diameter by 16.7% due to quality of inputs. Still, experts judged the majority of outputs clinically acceptable for presurgical planning. CONCLUSIONS: The model developed a reliable method to segment vessels on T1C, offering a practical alternative for vascular assessment in low-resource settings.
